plugins.author: dajoey
plugins.name: LazyCrucible
plugins.punchline: Crucible of the Unbroken familiar picks, filled in for every fight
plugins.description: For the Beastmaster duty Crucible of the Unbroken. Fills the ten-familiar run roster at the Bentbranch Meadows entry menu and the three Battlehorn slots before every fight with the familiars that answer that fight's mechanics: elemental weakness, interrupts, dispels, cleanses and crowd control, skipping knocked-out familiars and benching badly hurt ones. Picks are announced in chat. Every automation has its own toggle and manual edits always win. Includes the beast-pick advisor for every board and a read-only recorder that writes each Crucible screen to the Dalamud log. Use /lazycrucible to open.
plugins.changelog:
v0.1.9.18 (2026-11-14) [testing]
- The plugin windows have been rebuilt on the shared LalaUiKit: one consistent layout with themed section headers, unified spacing and colour accents. All settings and behaviour are unchanged, and existing configuration loads as-is.

v0.1.9.17 (2026-11-10) [testing]
- Rebuilt against the Dalamud 15.0.4.0 payload for game patch 7.58. No functional changes.

v0.1.9.16 (2026-10-13) [testing]
- **"Score: three familiars" run-roster mode, off by default.** For score runs. A run roster of one to three familiars scores the Beast Squad III bonus on every board, so with the option on the run roster is the best three familiars for the whole board instead of the board's full roster. The three are chosen from the familiars you own and that are not knocked out: they cover as many of the board's required interrupt, dispel and cleanse needs as any three can, then the damage the board calls to be blunted, then three of one kin when that costs no required cover (the Gambit bonus), then the rest by points. A roster of three saved for a different board is rewritten for the board you enter. Whatever the three cannot answer on the board is named on the window's summary line; nothing pops up. With three or fewer familiars the game registers the battlehorns itself, so the plugin leaves them alone. Found in the settings window and the Lazy Hub as "Score: three familiars".
- With the option off, nothing changes. While AutoDuty drives the run roster the plugin stands by there, option on or off.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v0.1.9.15 (2026-10-13) [testing]
- **Mitigation in the horn picks.** Fights with a damage wall now field a familiar that blunts it, ranked below every interrupt, dispel and cleanse need, and counted only for a familiar above the danger HP line. Durga's Atomic Ray gets a magic answer (drake's Smoldering Scales, pugil's Water Wall or a Scalekin's Scaleskin); Borgny gets coblyn's Vulcanize for the poison plus a magic answer; Gargoyle's Sweeping Evisceration gets a physical answer (a Beastkin's Beastskin, coblyn's Vulcanize or adamantoise's Harden Shell). The fight guide lists these under "Calls for".
- One telemetry line per fight names the team on the horns and the needs it cannot answer (`uncovered=`).
- **Works with AutoDuty.** While AutoDuty runs, it handles the run roster, shop, treasure, spoils and campsite itself, so the plugin stands by there; the battlehorns are AutoDuty's only with its "Fight picks" on, and the plugin picks them otherwise. AutoDuty's active profile is read through AutoDuty's own interface (its config file when that is unavailable), never changed; when neither can be read, every screen stands by, as before. The window shows one quiet line naming the screens it is standing by on.
- **No more corrections on top of AutoDuty's familiar picks.** AutoDuty re-applied its own picks every time, so they never reached a fight.
- **Fight guide: the Snarl -> Parting Blow advice is gone** (Parting Blow no longer dodges a hit since the September 17 hotfix). Plain tankbusters say to let a familiar with enough HP take them under Snarl; poisoning ones (Deadly Thrust, Cold Caress, Toxic Vomit) say to Parting Blow right after the hit so the poison leaves with the familiar; Gargoyle's Sweeping Evisceration says to save the Blink tome for it.
- Item values: Beastly Knife is valued like the elemental axes; Hero's Crown counts its Excellence proc (9 s of nullified attacks); Rapid Recast gear is valued; reraise items are worth a little less at Third Degree.
- **Patch 7.57: battlehorns the game registered itself (teams of three or fewer) are left alone**; a knocked-out member of a three-familiar team is no longer toggled off the horns.
- **Patch 7.57: the board's degree survives a job change** (the game now keeps the Crucible Mode until logout), so the degree passed to Gluttony Combo is no longer reset when the character returns to Beastmaster. It is forgotten at logout.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v0.1.9.14 (2026-10-06) [testing]
- **The board's difficulty degree now reaches Gluttony Combo during a fight.** The degree is set in the lobby (by a click or by AutoDuty) and the character then zones into the duty; the plugin used to forget it at every loading screen, so a fight always read as an unknown degree. It is now kept across loading screens and still forgotten when the Beastmaster job is left or the plugin unloads.

v0.1.9.13 (2026-10-06) [testing]

plugins.name: LazyFoodBuff
plugins.punchline: Never forget to eat your food again.
plugins.description: Auto-eats food in combat duties with per-job selection, auto-select based on best stats, and a low-food warning.
plugins.changelog:
v0.1.5.3 (2026-11-14) [testing]
- The plugin windows have been rebuilt on the shared LalaUiKit: one consistent layout with themed section headers, unified spacing and colour accents. All settings and behaviour are unchanged, and existing configuration loads as-is.

v0.1.5.2 (2026-11-10) [testing]
- Rebuilt against the Dalamud 15.0.4.0 payload for game patch 7.58. No functional changes.

v0.1.5.1 (2026-10-03) [testing]
- **Quick controls for the Lazy Hub window.** The plugin now offers auto-eating, "Only in combat duties", the minutes of food left before eating again and the low-food warning with its count to Lazy Hub (`/lazy`) over Dalamud IPC, so they can be changed from one window next to the other lalalazy plugins. Each change does exactly what the matching setting in the plugin's own window does.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Without Lazy Hub installed the plugin behaves exactly as before.

v0.1.5.0 (2026-09-21)

- **"Only eat in combat duties" now covers Crucible of the Unbroken.** The five boards count as combat duties, and so does the Bentbranch Meadows entry area while playing Beastmaster (the one job that can enter), so the meal is eaten before a run starts. Eating before entry matters: a meal eaten inside does not refill HP to the raised maximum.

v0.1.4.0 (2026-09-05)

- Optional decision diagnostics, off by default. Turn on "Log food decisions" (settings window, Advanced / Diagnostics) or run `/lazyfoodbuff telemetry on`, and every time the plugin settles on a food for the current job it writes one line to the plugin log: the food it picked, its score, and the runner-ups it beat â€” plus a second line when that food is actually eaten. The point is the runner-ups: "picked X at 41.20 over Y at 40.80" is the shape of evidence that can eventually say whether the auto-select weights are right. Nothing leaves the machine; the lines only go to the local plugin log.

- Honest caveat: this is a data-collection investment, not an answer. The outcome side (what a food actually did to damage) needs weeks of encounter data before it says anything statistically â€” the plugin log will quietly accumulate the decision half in the meantime.
- Nothing about food selection changed. When the toggle is off, the only cost is one boolean read.

v0.1.3.1 (2026-09-05)

- The "What's new" popup now opens after this very update. 0.1.3.0 stayed silent the first time it ran because it had no record of the last version shown; the gate now tells an updated plugin (settings file already present) apart from a brand-new install (none yet) and only the latter stays quiet (`ChangelogGate.Options.ExistingInstall`, read from `pi.ConfigFile.Exists`.

- Nothing else changed. The notes can be reopened later with `/lazyfoodbuff changelog`.

plugins.author: dajoey
plugins.name: LazyRetainerLive
plugins.punchline: Real-time retainer venture countdowns for your dashboard.
plugins.description: Serves the logged-in character's live retainer and venture state on loopback HTTP (127.0.0.1:10504) so the ffxiv dashboard relay can show real-time venture countdowns instead of AutoRetainer's occasionally-stale file cache.
plugins.changelog:
v0.1.0.4 (2026-11-14) [testing]
- The plugin windows have been rebuilt on the shared LalaUiKit: one consistent layout with themed section headers, unified spacing and colour accents. All settings and behaviour are unchanged, and existing configuration loads as-is.

v0.1.0.3 (2026-11-10) [testing]
- Rebuilt against the Dalamud 15.0.4.0 payload for game patch 7.58. No functional changes.

v0.1.0.2 (2026-10-03) [testing]
- **Quick controls for the Lazy Hub window.** The plugin now offers the switch that serves retainer data (the port stays in the plugin's own window) to Lazy Hub (`/lazy`) over Dalamud IPC, so they can be changed from one window next to the other lalalazy plugins. Each change does exactly what the matching setting in the plugin's own window does.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Without Lazy Hub installed the plugin behaves exactly as before.

v0.1.0.1 (2026-09-05)


- Corrected a wrong claim in the v0.1.0.0 notes below (and on the mod's web page): **the endpoint does not answer 503 on logout.** Once logged in, it keeps serving that character's last known retainer state - including at the title screen - and only ever answers 503 if it has never read the retainer table at all since the plugin loaded (i.e. it started at the title screen and no login has happened yet). That freeze is deliberate and is the better behaviour: measured previously the frozen live snapshot was still *newer* than AutoRetainer's file, so falling back to the file on logout would have shown the dashboard **older** data, not fresher. No behaviour was changed here - only the description was wrong.
- The settings window no longer reports "serving live snapshot" while logged out. It now distinguishes three states: no snapshot yet, serving a live snapshot, or serving the last-known snapshot while the game is in transition.


- For anything scripting against this endpoint: `readAt` is the time the request was **served**, not the time the data was read from the game, so it does not reveal how stale a frozen snapshot is. Use the settings window (or `/lazyretainerlive debug`) to tell live from frozen.

v0.1.0.0 (2026-09-05)


- First release. LazyRetainerLive reads the logged-in character's LIVE retainer table (the same in-memory data AutoRetainer uses to drive its own countdowns) and serves it as JSON on `http://127.0.0.1:10504/retainers`, so the ffxiv dashboard's retainer panel can show venture countdowns that update the moment a venture is collected instead of whenever AutoRetainer next saves its config file.
- When not logged in (or the live table has no data yet) the endpoint answers HTTP 503, which tells the dashboard relay to fall back to AutoRetainer's file. Loopback only - the port is never reachable from other machines.


- Companion of AutoRetainer - it reads, it never writes, assigns, or collects anything. Settings: Enabled (default on) and loopback port (default 10504). Commands: `/lazyretainerlive` opens settings, `/lazyretainerlive debug` dumps listener + snapshot state, `/lazyretainerlive changelog` reopens this popup.
- Why this exists: AutoRetainer's `DefaultConfig.json` (which feeds the dashboard today) is saved only at AutoRetainer's own save points, so its venture rows can be tens of minutes stale while ventures are actually completing. The countdown for the logged-in character lives in the game's memory - this plugin is a small read-only window onto it.

plugins.author: Haselnussbomber
plugins.name: LeveHelper
plugins.punchline: A little helper for Levequests.
plugins.description: A little helper to check which Levequests have been completed and which are missing.
plugins.changelog:
- Added: You can now click on the group header in the Type filter to filter for either all Fieldcraft, Tradecraft or Grand Company Leves.
- Added: When GatherBuddy is installed, the Queue and Recipe Tree now display GatherBuddys tooltip on fish and spearfish, including info about the Bait, Time and Weather restrictions and the next uptimes.  
  - Please note that GatherBuddy uses the client language, not Dalamuds UI language like LeveHelper. It's out of my control.
- Fixed: Some gatherables did not show up in the Queue.

Regarding the Levemete filter

The game's database doesn't list which Levemete issues which Levequests and multiple old NPCs also rotate their Levequests when you complete one.

I used to scrape a wiki to gather this data, but two weeks ago, we added Levequest issuer tracking to the Tracky plugin and already have more entries than the wiki provided!

Some entries that I could confirm through another wiki are still missing, so manually added those back in for now.

If you'd like to help us, please install the Tracky plugin and enable uploads in its settings.

Thank you! :)

plugins.author: Aida Enna
plugins.name: Macro Chain Redux
plugins.punchline: A modified fork of the old Macro Chain that allows you to run multiple macros one after the other (or repeat them).
plugins.description:
Allows for a macro to continue onto the next macro by using '/nextmacro' on the last line of a macro.
Adding '/nextmacro' on the last line of Macro #01 will automatically execute Macro #02
Adding '/nextmacro down' on the last line of Macro #01 will automatically execute Macro #11
Also allows executing any macro from chat using '/runmacro'
You can repeat a macro by using /runmacro inside the macro followed by the number of the macro you're editing
Using '/macrocancel' will stop the currently running macro

plugins.author: Akari
plugins.name: Mahjong Advisor
plugins.punchline: Discard advice and optional auto-play for Doman Mahjong.
plugins.description: Reads your Doman Mahjong hand, discards, dora, scores and called melds, then ranks each discard by hand speed against deal-in risk. Auto-play and file logging are on by default in this build: sit at a casual table and it plays, then /mjadv bundle packages the logs for support. /mjadv stop or the Automation tab returns to manual suggestions instantly. Discard piles and meld strips are found automatically; the node tools are only a fallback.
plugins.changelog: v0.4.4.0: Chi picker freeze fix. When a call prompt's claimed tile could not be identified, the single-shape chi gate counted shapes for the wrong tile: each candidate offered one run, but the actual tile completed two, so the game opened its shape-selection dialog - which ignores call callbacks - and the match froze (live at South 4 while leading 38,400; bundle 20261030-081345). Chi now fires only when the claim is pinned to one tile, or when every tile that could legally be on offer completes exactly one run; anything else passes instead. The picker-stall warning also logs once rather than every frame. The stale Advisor block that earlier builds wrote into the plugin config is no longer serialised: it was never read, is ignored on load, and disappears at the next config save. An experimental rollout-search re-ranking of discard candidates is included but ships OFF: a 240-match paired simulator A/B (two seeds) rejected it - it traded a 39% relative win-rate drop for nothing - so it stays a foundation for later work. v0.4.3.0: Result-screen retry. The result panel can swallow the first advance callback while it animates; the controller fired it twice and then its acted guard blocked every retry, leaving the screen waiting indefinitely (live Advanced freeze, state 29 unresolved for 12s). Advances now retry every 2.5 seconds while the result state persists, capped at 8 attempts so the deliberately manual match-end screen is not spammed. v0.4.2.0: Match-level tuning. A full hanchan evaluator now plays East+South with real score accounting, dealer rotation, honcha, riichi sticks and placement, and 120 paired matches showed the old risk settings were too passive. Win value 1800 and deal-in cost 4000 beat 1300/5200 on identical deals (average place 2.55 vs 2.65, more firsts, fewer fourths) with the deal-in rate unchanged at 9.3%. A v7 config migration applies the new values. Riichi hand value and placement stance were also tested and left unchanged - both were flat across 60-match arms. v0.4.1.0: Advanced-table defence. Cross-seat genbutsu now uses the pond lengths captured at the instant a riichi marker appears; the old turn-count shortcut broke once calls shortened ponds and could mark a tile discarded before the riichi as safe. Two declared riichi also force a fold for any hand that is not tenpai, overriding the placement chase. The simulator now records the same declaration snapshots: over 1,000 hands the defence fix moved deal-in rate from 10.3% to 9.5% and average points from -22 to +17, while the double-riichi rail was neutral there because the simulation has no placement stance. Live Advanced trial on 0.4.0.0 finished 1st, 4th, then leading when stopped; the 4th lost two deal-ins to one riichi player, the second 12,000 while two were in riichi. v0.4.0.0: Exact scoring core. Completed hands are now scored by yaku, fu, dora and the payment table (closed and open, riichi through yakuman), and the offline simulator uses that scoring for win legality and payouts. Ready-hand valuation was built and benchmarked but stays out of live decisions: over 1,500 simulated hands, mixing exact tenpai values with the existing one-away estimate cut the win rate from 15.4% to 8.1%, so the value scale must be unified for every shanten first. Advice is memoised per table state so the overlay and controller do not recompute the same decision. v0.3.10.0: Silent-endgame defence. The threat model measured a silent opponent as at most 19% likely tenpai, so on a table with no riichi and no melds every safety rule stayed off - the controller pushed one-away hands with 6-9 tiles left to draw into damaten twice in one match (4,200 and 2,200 deal-ins) and paid full tsumo on 14,300 and 20,000 hands. Silent seats now take on a readiness floor that rises from zero at wall 32 to a concrete threat at wall 16, arming the existing late-wall fold and per-tile safety ranking on quiet tables. v0.3.9.0: Chi freeze fixed. The shape-selection dialog ignores scripted call picks (confirmed by the first picker dump), so chi now only fires when exactly one shape is possible - that path completes with no dialog. Multi-shape chi passes instead of stalling; the pass log records how many shapes were declined. v0.3.8.0: Late-wall defence. When an opponent is a concrete threat and the wall is down to the last four go-arounds, the controller folds any hand that is not tenpai instead of pushing a 1-shanten no-riichi hand. This was the 12,000 deal-in in the first match. Diagnostic bundles now also include chi picker dumps. The end-of-match results screen still waits for you by design - that is the one click after a match. v0.3.7.0: Chi is now fully automated. The controller calls chi when the advisor ranks it best, and if the client shows the shape-selection surface it fires the first variant and re-evaluates the hand. The picker layout is dumped once per session to the log folder so shape-specific selection can be refined against real captures. A v6 config migration enables chi. v0.3.6.0: Read each opponent meld strip independently. A hidden empty strip for one quiet seat no longer suppresses every visible meld on the table, so the threat model sees called sets when they exist. This is a readiness/defence accuracy change; automation logic is unchanged. v0.3.5.0: Fix the second freeze. A complete open hand is no longer assumed to be a legal tsumo: the controller checks for an actual yaku and keeps discarding when there is none. Call prompts now prefer the newest board addition over a possibly stale pond tile (the live log claimed 6z/dragon while the actual Pon was 9m), and the log records the last discard tile/seat. A v5 config migration re-enables auto-play/logging. v0.3.4.0: Fix the self-kan freeze. A Kan/Pass bar at state 6 is ignored and the normal discard proceeds instead of firing a Pass callback the client ignores. Session stats are preserved after /mjadv stop so the bundle still shows the run, and a v4 config migration re-enables auto-play/logging for the next launch. v0.3.3.0: Reset the exposed tuning sliders to the fitted win-rate defaults (base hand value 1300, deal-in 5200, noten 1500, opponent hand 4000) with a one-time v3 config migration. Diagnostic bundles now include the actual Dalamud plugin config file from pluginConfigs. v0.3.2.0: State 15 is now treated as the generic other-players state unless real call buttons are present, state 22 (forced riichi discard) is automated, and state 27 (between-hands result/score) is recognised instead of showing stale advice. Overlay/advice are now gated to actual decision states, and diagnostic bundles can read the Dalamud log while it is open. v0.3.1.0: Auto-play and file logging are now on by default, /mjadv session starts a clean logged session, and /mjadv bundle packages the recent JSONL logs, config, layouts, Dalamud log tail and a full last-read snapshot into one zip. Status changes are now logged as auto-status records. v0.3.0.1: Re-arm auto-play on a state change even when the hand happens to repeat, and wait for the Riichi/Pass prompt to close before cutting the riichi tile. v0.3.0.0: Optional auto-play. Replays the client's FireCallback protocol for discards, calls, riichi, ron/tsumo and result advancement, using the reference solver's live-verified handshake and timing guards. Off by default; /mjadv auto [on/off] or /mjadv stop toggles it. Pon/ron/tsumo/riichi are enabled by default, chi and kan are opt-in, the chi shape picker pauses for a manual choice, and the new-hand screen is never auto-advanced. Added /mjadv hand and /mjadv options diagnostics. v0.2.0.2: Keep the previous wall count, so the wall-jump half of new-hand detection actually fires. v0.2.0.1: Reset the pond baselines at the start of a new hand, so the first discard of the hand is tracked and the first call prompt gets the right claimed tile. v0.2.0.0: Meld containers now read by default (112-115 families), with a fail-closed check against our own called-meld count. Own meld tiles are recovered from hand deltas when nodes are unavailable, so ukeire no longer counts tiles already in a call. Riichi detection is marker-node only; the dead rotation and score-drop paths are gone. One node-tree walk per read instead of up to seven. Fixed dead hands getting a nonzero win rate and Pass inventing a yaku path. Red-five decoding accepts both absolute and alias ids. Removed the obsolete fold-threshold setting. Setup window no longer reopens every launch. Added /mjadv melds diagnostics and richer log records.

plugins.punchline: Automated character rotation and quest sequence execution
plugins.description:
Automated character rotation and quest sequence execution for Questionable.

Automates multi-character MSQ progression by intelligently switching between characters based on quest completion and level requirements. Features include:
- Automatic character switching and quest tracking
- MSQ progression monitoring across all characters
- Allied Society quest rotation and prioritization
- Event quest automation with prerequisite checking
- Chauffeur Mode for following main character through quests
- Data Center travel automation
- Stop point configuration for controlled progression

Required Plugins: Questionable, AutoRetainer

plugins.author: Legends of the Game
plugins.name: Tales of Milestones
plugins.punchline: Remember every step, Warriors of Light.
plugins.description: Quest progression and pacing — a reflective notebook for your story journey, not a scoreboard.
plugins.changelog:
Tales of Milestones:
- Eat buttons on the Bonuses tab. Each meal in your inventory has an Eat button. One click eats one meal. The button is not available when the game refuses the meal.
- Eat button in /tm food. The food window has the same button for a meal that is in your inventory.
- /tm eat. `/tm eat dps`, `tank`, `healer`, `battle`, `craft`, `gather` or `all` eats your meal of that kind when you hold only one such meal. When you hold more than one, the Bonuses tab opens and you select the meal.
- Playtime in the export. The export adds the time that the plugin recorded after your last `/playtime` reply, so the playtime is current at the time of the export. The plugin does not run `/playtime`.
- Armor, GARO and more weapons in the export. "Copy collections" and "Copy everything" now include relic armor, GARO gear, and the Figmental, Exquisite and Deep Dungeon weapons.
- The native windows use less processor time. The at-a-glance window and the tabs of the main window now update one time each second, not on each frame. In a test, the at-a-glance window changed from about 1.2 ms to about 0.08 ms for each frame.
- Fix: the plugin no longer writes its settings file every 5 seconds while Cosmic Exploration data is loaded. It writes the file only when a tool's progress changes.
- Fix: the job list on the Progression tab no longer scrolls past its end.
- KamiToolKit is updated to its current version.
Adventurer's Ledger (Pandora Lunar):
- New layout. Next Steps is the first screen. It shows 5 cards for what to do next, and "Show 5 more" shows 10. Daily, Weekly and Seasonal rows are below it in the rail. The header shows the area title, the age of your data and 4 clocks.
- Challenge Log. Each Challenge Log entry has its own row, with links and typed counts. Suggested and Completed groups are included.
- Routine sub-checks. A routine can have its own boxes: one for each roulette, a Tank You pick, 12 allied society boxes and Grand Company chips. "Edit routines" changes the rows.
- Relics by job. The Relics area has a By job view and line cards with progress bars. To fill the Armor and GARO frames, update Tales of Milestones to this version and import a new export.
- Societies, currents and collections. Societies show unlock lines and rank bars. Aether currents are listed by zone. Collections are grouped by availability, with Online Store links.
- Settings area. Character, display, and backup and import settings are in one area. The Ledger holds up to 8 characters, and times can show in UTC or local time.
- Themes. The three themes are Lunar night, Crystarium and Light. Expansion tags use the colours of the Lodestone patch notes.
- Jobs meter. The rail has a Jobs meter that adds your combat, crafting and gathering levels, out of 3,330.
- Fix: after an import, the relic row in the list of changes counts relic items. Before, a stage upgrade showed no change, for example "9 to 9".

Current features include queue time estimates and notifications via Discord, so you can know when you make it into the game, as well as anonymously collecting and reporting statistics about your queue times to crowdsource information about FFXIV server load and activity. Join our Discord for more information!

Discord URL: https://waiting.camora.dev/discord
rawManifest.Punchline: Set out for Dawntrail and make your queues a breeze. Waitingway provides crowdsourced FFXIV login queue times, now with Discord queue notification features.

rawManifest.TestingChangelog:
0.8.30, changes since 0.8.0:
- Gear repair, on by default: between targets of the books, the Atma farm and between autopilot steps, a worn piece at or below 30 % (set in the main tab) gets repaired. Self repair with Dark Matter goes first. Anything still worn after that goes to Alistair, the mender in Limsa Lominsa Lower Decks. If a repair fails, the run goes on and tries again 30 minutes later.
- Books: the 4 second take-off check now starts once vnavmesh has found the route. Long flights, such as across Coerthas, took 4 seconds to plan, so the check cancelled the route and the character rode on the ground instead.
- Messages about missing gear or materia no longer tell Free Trial accounts to buy them. They say the market board is not available and to craft the gear or extract the materia. This covers A Relic Reborn's weapon, the meld step, the HQ Zodiac materials and the Novus materia.
- The autopilot stops before A Relic Reborn when you lack the weapon Gerolt asks for (Barbarian's Bardiche for Bravura, and so on) with its 2 materia melded and cannot buy it. The popup names the weapon and why it was not bought. Before, WigglyQuest talked to Gerolt in a loop.
- On a Free Trial account the "Buy from market board" box shows unticked and cannot be changed. Your saved choice stays for other accounts.
- On a Free Trial account the materia row of the main tab says "by hand (Free Trial)" instead of "autopilot", since nothing is bought on the market board there.
- Report a problem now writes the .log file and copies your text, then gives two buttons: one opens this plugin's thread on our Discord, the other is the server invite for people who are not members yet, since the thread link does not open for them.
- Capture leves also take an armour piece off when one hit removes more than 30 % of a target's HP, before it can die. A level 70 summoner took a winter nix from 100 % to 42 % with one auto-attack.
- Capture leves fight the other spawns that attack you, like the Ragged Hippogryph, with the normal AI and rotation instead of the auto-attack alone, then turn them off again for the targets.
- Report a problem now opens our Discord instead of a GitHub issue. Send the .log file to Kyuuso by DM or post it in the plugin's thread in #plugins. The text you typed is copied to the clipboard so you can paste it with the file.
- Capture leves keep your armour on at first. Each target that dies before the /soothe takes one more piece off for that job and level, body and legs first, and the count is saved. A level 100 character may lose a few targets the first time while it learns.
- Free Trial accounts skip every market board purchase and the main tab says so, since the game does not let them use the market board.
- Capture leves no longer switch to normal combat after riding to the next target. Before, the AI came back on and attacked a winter nix that was already pacified.
- Capture leves start the auto-attack with the hotbar's Auto-attack command. The old call got "Cannot execute at this time." with the weak weapon on, so the targets were never hit.
- Capture leves send the chocobo away and turn off the BossMod AI, its preset and Rotation Solver, even when you had them on. Only the auto-attack hits the targets, so a skill or the chocobo no longer kills one before the /soothe.
- Capture leves in the books no longer swap between the weak weapon and the Atma weapon every second. The Atma weapon goes back on after the targets are soothed, before the turn-in.
- The books summon the chocobo companion with Gysahl Greens for their enemies and FATEs, as the Atma farm already did. Leves stay without it, so it cannot kill a capture target.
- Escort leves (Someone's in the Doghouse): when the escort falls more than 20 yalms behind, the character walks back to it. It used to stay up to 30 yalms ahead, stuck on a rock, sending /beckon that the game answered with "Too far away".
- Dungeon unlocks that need another dungeon cleared first (Halatali before Halatali (Hard)) wait until you are out of it. The clear used to count when the last boss died, so the talk to Hugubert started inside Halatali, three teleports failed, and the book stopped on Mumuepo the Beholden.
- Trips to an NPC wait up to 3 minutes for a duty or cutscene to end before teleporting.
- Lure leves (Don't Forget to Cry): a prime location that lures nothing within 8 seconds is skipped. It used the lure on the same wrong spot every 5 seconds.
- New "Dungeon coffers" option in the Debug tab for book, Braves and unlock dungeons: boss coffers only (default), every coffer, no coffers, or your own DAD/AutoDuty loot settings.
- FATE combat after a dungeon: AutoDuty/DAD turn the BossMod AI off and clear its autorotation preset. /vbmai on is now sent again after each zone change, and without Rotation Solver your last preset (or VBM Default) is set for the fight and cleared after it.
- Atma FATEs inside the U'Ghamaro Mines are done on the ground; the mount stays off past the entrance.
- Jalzahn's furnace is used from (445.9, -66.3), where it worked by hand. When WigglyQuest hovers at Gerolt or the furnace, it lands and walks in.
- The "Do you really want to trade a high-quality item?" prompt is answered on quests Zodiac Helper started.
- Main tab: materia and the class weapon read "autopilot" when market buying is on.
Still to test before 1.0: party sharing between two clients, and a second relic on the same character.

plugins.author: dajoey
plugins.name: PvP Solver
plugins.punchline: PvP-only auto-rotation
plugins.description: PvP-only auto-rotation for FFXIV. Activates in PvP zones.
plugins.changelog:
v0.1.2.15 (2026-11-14) [testing]
- The plugin windows have been rebuilt on the shared LalaUiKit: one consistent layout with themed section headers, unified spacing and colour accents. All settings and behaviour are unchanged, and existing configuration loads as-is.

v0.1.2.14 (2026-11-10) [testing]
- Rebuilt against the Dalamud 15.0.4.0 payload for game patch 7.58. No functional changes.


- **Removed the AI decision layer.** The optional relayed decision model (focus picking, Limit Break firing and the healer-call shadow lines, with their "call the shots" settings row and its relay address field) is gone from the plugin. No fight snapshot is built or sent anywhere anymore, and the plugin makes no decision calls of any kind.
- Targeting, Guard, Recuperate, the defensive table, StickyTarget and every other rotation behavior are unchanged. The defensive rules keep reading real HP (current HP out of the maximum) under the neutral name `RealHp.HpRatio`; no threshold or default moved.
- PvP Solver still never moves the character and never fires a PvP Limit Break on its own logic, exactly as before.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.


- **The Jev co-pilot logs the plain code rule's answer beside Jev's, for both of its questions.** Each `JV|focus-pick` line names the enemy Jev picked and the enemy the plain rule would pick (the lowest-HP enemy in attack range); each `JV|lb-shadow` line names Jev's Limit Break call and the code rule's. Both answers are recorded side by side and graded after the session, to show which one decides better. Log only: targeting, Limit Break firing and every other behavior are unchanged.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.


- Upstream engine sync (RotationSolverReborn a560469db): the rotation engine now builds in upstream's merged single-project layout.
- Ports upstream engine fixes: the action manager is read at call time instead of a pointer cached at startup (a stale-pointer crash class), configuration saves are atomic (write to a temp file, then replace), and the shield-value calculation can no longer overflow on very large HP values.
- No rotation behavior change; the 21 PvP rotations and their presets are untouched.

v0.1.2.10 (2026-11-01) [testing]
- **The per-job defensive actions also read real HP.** Heart of Corundum, Tempera Coat, Earth's Reply, Riddle of Earth, the Bloodbath rows, Lady of Crowns, Microcosmos, Meisui, Impalement, Xenoglossy's low-HP arm and Shadowbringer's HP arm compared their "use below this HP" thresholds against predicted HP, which counts heals still on the way; predicted can read 84% one second before a death at about 40% real HP. They now compare against the current HP out of the maximum, the same real value Guard and the defensive table already use. Thresholds and defaults are unchanged, and reads of enemies' and allies' HP (Smite, Guardian, Blasting Zone, Perfectio, the burst target) are untouched.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v0.1.2.9 (2026-11-01) [testing]
- **Self-defence now reads real HP.** Guard, Recuperate and the generic defensive actions (the "use below X% HP" table) compared their thresholds against predicted HP, which counts heals still on the way; predicted can read 84% one second before a death at about 40% real HP, so nothing fired. All of them now compare against the current HP out of the maximum, the same real value the Jev snapshot uses. Thresholds and defaults are unchanged.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v0.1.2.8 (2026-10-31) [testing]
- **"Let Jev call the shots" now sees real HP.** The player's and allies' HP sent to Jev is the current HP out of the maximum, no longer PvP Solver's predicted HP, which counts heals still on the way. In one match Jev was told 84% one second before a death at about 40%.
- **Jev's pick no longer drops when Jev is briefly unsure.** The relay now keeps the last pick itself while that enemy is still hittable, and drops it on purpose when the enemy goes under Guard, out of reach or stale. PvP Solver follows the relay's call and never brings a dropped pick back. Only with an older relay does PvP Solver keep the last pick, for up to three seconds after Jev gave it, while that enemy is still a valid target.
- **The Limit Break log matches what happened.** `JV|lb-fired` is written once when the Limit Break goes off in a fire window. `JV|lb-fire-skip` is written only when a window closes without it, with the reason: unusable, follow-up, out-of-range, no-target or timeout. A report of the use that arrives up to two seconds late still counts as fired. Before, a skip line could appear in windows that then fired, and windows that really failed wrote nothing.
- **Each action used is reported once.** The game reports each action twice; the same action on the same target within 1.5 seconds now counts once in the snapshot.
- **Alliance members are included (Frontline).** After the party members, the nearest alliance members are sent too, marked as alliance, up to eight allies in all. Each ally now carries its object id, so Jev can name an ally to heal.
- **Healer call, logged only.** When Jev suggests whom a healer should heal (an ally, self, attack or Guard), the suggestion is written as one `JV|heal-shadow` log line for the first suggestion in each fight and each time it changes; an answer with no suggestion does not count as a change. Nothing acts on it yet.
- **Relay failures are visible in the log.** One summary line per fight (when combat ends, or every 60 seconds while calls fail) counts calls that succeeded, timed out, got an error reply or failed. No line per call, and no call is counted in a later fight. An unreadable heal or Limit Break value in a reply no longer drops the rest of the answer.
- PvP Solver still never moves the character.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.1.2.7 (2026-10-29) [testing]
- **"Let Jev call the shots" reports what actually happened.** Each snapshot also carries the player's current target and the actions actually used since the last one (action and target only), so each of Jev's picks can be checked against what PvP Solver did and whether that enemy went down.
- Jev's focus pick is kept steady: it moves to another enemy only when that one is clearly the better pick.
- **A line, cone or splash Limit Break that Jev called could be skipped** because the action kept its own "most enemies" target. It is now aimed at the enemy Jev chose, which the game has just confirmed as a valid target. A skipped fire writes one reason line to the log.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

plugins.author: dajoey
plugins.name: AutoPotion
plugins.punchline: Per-job HP, MP, and deep dungeon potion automation.
plugins.description: Auto-uses the highest-tier HP potion, MP potion (Ether), and the deep dungeon regen potion (Sustaining / Eurekan / Orthos / Pilgrim's) at configurable thresholds. Each potion's threshold and on/off state is stored per-job, so casters and tanks can have completely different setups.
plugins.changelog:
v0.2.5.4 (2026-11-14) [testing]
- The settings window has been rebuilt on the shared LalaUiKit: one consistent layout with themed section headers, unified spacing and colour accents across every page. All settings, presets and automation behaviour are unchanged, and existing configuration loads as-is.

v0.2.5.3 (2026-11-10) [testing]
- Rebuilt against the Dalamud 15.0.4.0 payload for game patch 7.58. No functional changes.

v0.2.5.2 (2026-10-10) [testing]
- **Automatic item uses no longer cancel an open action sequence.** Any potion, ether, deep dungeon medicine or Echo Drops that would land while mudra seals or Ten Chi Jin are held is delayed until the sequence completes, instead of cancelling the ninjutsu mid-chain. The delay lasts only while the sequence is up (a mudra window is about six seconds) and lifts immediately after; at or below 25% HP the heal fires regardless - a cancelled jutsu is cheaper than dying. No other job's behaviour changes.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- With the optional decision log enabled, a held use is recorded with the `heldmudra` near-miss reason, rate-limited like every other near-miss line.

v0.2.5.1 (2026-10-03) [testing]
- **Quick controls for the Lazy Hub window.** The plugin now offers the master switch, "Only in combat", "Only in a duty", the HP, MP and Regen potion switches with their thresholds, and Cure Silence (Echo Drops) to Lazy Hub (`/lazy`) over Dalamud IPC, so they can be changed from one window next to the other lalalazy plugins. Each change does exactly what the matching setting in the plugin's own window does.
- The potion settings apply to the active job's profile, as in the settings window.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Without Lazy Hub installed the plugin behaves exactly as before.

v0.2.5.0 (2026-09-05)

- New per-job option: "Auto-use Echo Drops when silenced". When it is on and Silence lands (mob silence spells, AoE silences, deep dungeon traps), AutoPotion uses Echo Drops from inventory to cure it automatically. Item use is not blocked by Silence, so the cure works exactly when nothing else can.
- OFF by default like every option, and per job like the rest: tick the new box in the settings window for the jobs it should apply to. With it off (the default) nothing changes - not even a status check.
- It reuses the same machinery as the potions: HQ Echo Drops are preferred over normal ones, the shared 750 ms cooldown after any potion use applies, and a Silence that arrives during that cooldown is cured on the next tick.
- If the diagnostic tap is enabled, the cure logs as an `e` event; when it cannot fire the near-miss reasons are `edblocked` (on cooldown / blocked) or `ednostock` (none in the bags).
- No change to potion behaviour. HP/MP/regen thresholds, the overshoot guard, the deep dungeon Rehabilitation lockout and the in-combat / in-duty gates all work exactly as before.

v0.2.4.0 (2026-09-05)

- Added an optional "Log potion decisions" diagnostic, OFF by default. plugins.author: dajoey
plugins.name: Armoire Auto-Fill
plugins.punchline: Per-dungeon view of which armoire-eligible gear pieces you're still missing
plugins.description: Lists every armoire-eligible dungeon drop in the game and shows whether each is in your inventory, in your armoire, or still missing. Sort by level, hide completed dungeons, toggle to show owned items too. Open the armoire UI at an inn once per session to populate the in-armoire state; in-inventory and equipped state is detected automatically.
plugins.changelog:
v0.5.7.2 (2026-11-14) [testing]
- The plugin windows have been rebuilt on the shared LalaUiKit: one consistent layout with themed section headers, unified spacing and colour accents. All settings and behaviour are unchanged, and existing configuration loads as-is.

v0.5.7.1 (2026-11-10) [testing]
- Rebuilt against the Dalamud 15.0.4.0 payload for game patch 7.58. No functional changes.

v0.5.7.0 (2026-10-10)
- **The PvP shopping list now includes gear sold for Trophy Crystals and Wolf Collars.** The crystal quartermaster's Trophy Crystal Exchange (weapons, armour, accessories) and the collar quartermaster's exchange were missing from the list because their cost currencies were not mapped, so the PvP code came out empty. Both quartermasters are in the list now, checked against Knightshopper's own vendor catalog: every exported pair is one it accepts.
- Pieces no import code can name are now listed in the window by name with the reason (the shop has no vendor link in the game data, or Knightshopper has no vendor for its shop), instead of being dropped quietly. The Wolf Mark gear behind the mark quartermaster falls in this list: its shop opens through a dialogue handler, so no vendor pair can be written for it.
- The shopping summary line showed placeholder braces instead of the counts; it shows the numbers now.

v0.5.6.0 (2026-10-08)
- **Import codes now carry only what can actually be bought today.** Some pieces are gated behind more than a quest: seasonal vendors also gate pieces on an achievement, and the previous filter only knew about quests, so pieces the game would not sell yet were still written into the codes, and the first one of them made Knightshopper refuse the whole import ("Item N is not available from its shared Gil vendor"). The shopping list now checks live quest and achievement progress: what can be bought now goes into the code, a piece whose cheapest listing is locked falls back to a listing that can be bought, and a piece with no buyable listing at all is left out and counted at the bottom of the window ("N missing piece(s) need quest or achievement progress you don't have yet - left out of the import"). The rule applies to every currency, not just gil.

v0.5.5.0 (2026-10-08) [testing]
- **Import codes now name vendors that Knightshopper itself has.** The previous build still produced Gil codes that Knightshopper refused whole ("Item N is not available from its shared Gil vendor"): the rule it used to decide which vendors Knightshopper knows was a guess and was wrong for most Gil shops. The rule now follows how Knightshopper builds its own vendor list: a vendor is an NPC the game actually places in an area, and seasonal NPCs that are re-used under new ids with the same name and the same shops count once. It applies to every currency, not just gil. The Gil code now carries several times as many pieces, because shops the old rule dropped by mistake are back.
- Placeholder items with no name are no longer put in a code; Knightshopper has no entry for them.
- Every code and every catalog entry was checked offline against the vendor data produced by Knightshopper's own library (not against this plugin's own model): no refusals. This is not yet confirmed in the game, and newer game patches than the one checked are not covered.
- The shopping-list section says what the codes were checked against and that it is not yet confirmed in-game; the copy message also explains that Knightshopper names only the first item it refuses.
- The vendor placement is read from the game's area files once per session in the background (about one second), with one log line.

v0.5.4.0 (2026-10-08) [testing]
- **Import codes no longer contain items Knightshopper would refuse.** Knightshopper rejects a whole import when even one item is not in its own catalog, which the previous Gil code hit: shops whose vendors only spawn for an event never enter Knightshopper's catalog, but this plugin was still naming them. The catalog now only names shops with a permanently placed vendor, matching how Knightshopper derives its own list, and the same rule applies to every currency, not just gil.
- Pieces that this leaves out are no longer silent: the window shows "N items left out: Knightshopper cannot buy them", the build log counts the skipped shops, and the copy buttons never produce a code Knightshopper would answer with "not available from its shared vendor".

plugins.author: dajoey
plugins.name: Gluttony Combo
plugins.punchline: Lalalazy fork of Wrath Combo - XIVCombo for very lazy players.
plugins.description: Gluttony Combo - lalalazy fork of Gluttony Combo. XIVCombo for very lazy players.
plugins.changelog:
v1.0.4.339 (2026-11-14) [testing]
- The plugin windows have been rebuilt on the shared LalaUiKit: one consistent layout with themed section headers, unified spacing and colour accents. All settings and behaviour are unchanged, and existing configuration loads as-is.

v1.0.4.338 (2026-11-10) [testing]
- Rebuilt against the Dalamud 15.0.4.0 payload for game patch 7.58. No functional changes.

v1.0.4.337 (2026-11-09) [testing]
- **The AI decision layer is gone.** The Fight Brain's question side - the raidwide mitigation ask, the pre-pull plan reader (party finder text and the `/gluttony plan` note command), and the party-callout reader - has been removed from the plugin, together with its relay address setting and the two "Plan Reader"/"Callout Reader" switches. GluttonyCombo no longer asks any decision model anything, sends no snapshot anywhere, and keeps no relay URL: the only network path it still uses is the movement tap's `/move/ingest` upload, which records the movement profiles and never carried a decision.
- What stays is pure code and unchanged: the rotation and every combo, the Fight Brain forecast reads and `FB|forecast` lines, the countdown strip, the shadow cast-gate lines, the party-data shadow rules (`FB|party-mit`, `FB|pos-zone`), and the movement recorder and shadow move planner. The move planner's `MP|` decision lines keep their exact format and now always carry the code pick only.
- The shadow move planner no longer has its ask-side toggle; `/gluttony movelog` now switches the recorder and the planner together, and its status line reads two switches instead of three.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.336 (2026-11-09) [testing]
- **Saving a custom action to a hotbar while in PvP now writes the PvP layout.** The custom-action editor's hotbar save told the game the write was a normal-slot write regardless of the current content, so a save made while in PvP updated the regular hotbar set instead of the PvP one; the call now passes the content check (upstream's fix), so the PvP variant of the slot is the one written.
- **The action-replacing hook answers in the game's own yes/no shape.** The IsActionIdReplaceable detour and its delegate declared an unsigned 64-bit return where the game's callback uses a boolean, so the replace decision relied on 0/1 marshalling to land correctly; both signatures now match the native BOOL return (upstream's fix), and the early-return values read true/false instead of 1/0. No behavior change is intended - this removes a latent hook-contract mismatch.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.335 (2026-11-07) [testing]
- **AoE heals no longer fire back to back on a party that is at or near full HP.** Follow-up to 1.0.4.334: on a party whose bars all read full or nearly full, the auto-rotation kept pressing AoE heals - a bar just under 100% never counted as full (regen-tick oscillation and display rounding), and a heal that had just gone out did not stand the press path down while it landed. Two changes, shared by Astrologian, White Mage, Scholar and Sage. First, a member only counts as needing an AoE heal on a real deficit: a bar at or above 98% reads as full for both the one-button average and the auto-rotation's member count, so no threshold setting (including the 100 "disable this check" setting, and a target count of 0, which is now floored at 1) can make a full party eligible. Second, the auto-rotation presses one AoE heal at a time: after a press goes out, the next waits out that cast's flight plus a second for the heal to land and party HP to propagate, so a movement-cancelled cast is no longer re-issued every tick. Real damage is never starved - a party still under the threshold after the window heals again immediately. Single-target heals, raidwide pre-casts and the 1.0.4.334 out-of-range fix are unchanged; the manual one-button still heals when pressed.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.334 (2026-11-07) [testing]
- **Healer one-button AoE heals no longer trigger off party members the heal cannot reach.** The Astrologian, White Mage, Scholar and Sage one-button AoE heal rotations averaged the whole party's HP: a member standing outside the heal's radius kept the average under the threshold, so the rotation kept choosing AoE heals (Helios, Medica, Succor, Prognosis and their oGCD neighbours) that could never heal that member. The trigger now averages only the members inside the heal's own effect radius (15y for the Helios family), alive and targetable, so the rotation returns to damaging while nobody reachable needs healing, and heals again the moment the far member comes back into range. Single-target healing is untouched: a member returning to range is picked up by the single-target path exactly as before. Raidwide pre-casts and the auto-rotation's own cast gate are unchanged.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

plugins.name: Lazy WT Math
plugins.punchline: FFXIV Wondrous Tails probability calculator.
plugins.description: Adds row probabilities to the Wondrous Tails display along with the average probability of what would happen if you shuffled. Upgraded for modern FFXIV.
plugins.changelog:
v3.2.3.6 (2026-11-14) [testing]
- The bundled interface toolkit no longer carries an unused image-processing library, so the plugin installs fewer files and no longer ships a package with known security advisories. No behavior changes.

v3.2.3.5 (2026-11-10) [testing]
- Rebuilt against the Dalamud 15.0.4.0 payload for game patch 7.58. No functional changes.

v3.2.3.4 (2026-11-07) [testing]

- No plugin-code changes: the plugin now builds against a fixed Dalamud library set (the pinned staging 15.0.3.9 payload) instead of whichever libraries the build machine happens to have installed, so packaging this plugin works reliably again. The Wondrous Tails probability readout is unchanged.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v3.2.3.3 (2026-11-05) [testing]

v3.2.3.4 (2026-11-07) [testing]

- No plugin-code changes: the plugin now builds against a fixed Dalamud library set (the pinned staging 15.0.3.9 payload) instead of whichever libraries the build machine happens to have installed, so packaging this plugin works reliably again. The Wondrous Tails probability readout is unchanged.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

- Updated the UI framework bundled inside the plugin to the current upstream KamiToolKit; the Wondrous Tails probability readout is built on the framework's current internals now.
- Kept the fork's hot-reload safety guard: the plugin's hooks disable, let any call already inside them finish, and only then dispose, so an update while the game is running can no longer crash the game from a call landing on a hook that is gone.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

plugins.name: Lazy Currency Spender
plugins.punchline: Find the absolute best way to spend all your FFXIV currencies.
plugins.description: Fork of CurrencySpender by Blackcatz1911. Never wonder 'What should I do with this?' again. Access real-time prices from Universalis, identify missing collectibles tied to your currencies, and unlock new possibilities for utilizing your in-game resources effectively.
plugins.changelog:
v1.3.1.5 (2026-11-14) [testing]
- The plugin windows have been rebuilt on the shared LalaUiKit: one consistent layout with themed section headers, unified spacing and colour accents. All settings and behaviour are unchanged, and existing configuration loads as-is.

v1.3.1.4 (2026-11-10) [testing]
- Rebuilt against the Dalamud 15.0.4.0 payload for game patch 7.58. No functional changes.

v1.3.1.3 (2026-10-17) [testing]
- The configuration wizard's auto-open step now sets the actual auto-open setting instead of toggling the sellables table.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v1.3.1.2 (2026-10-08) [testing]
- Added a map location for the Faux Commander (the Faux Hollows vendor in Idyllshire). Its Flag and TP buttons now draw like every other listed shop, and the plugin no longer logs a `Missing location: 1033921` error once at every startup.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v1.3.1.1 (2026-10-07) [testing]
- **Upstream sync through CurrencySpender 1.3.1.** New tracked currencies (Faux Leaf, Achievement Certificate, Oizys Credit, Auxesia Credit) and vendors (Quinnana, Faux Commander), data-driven custom-shop generation (in-code CustomShops replaces the hardcoded Cosmocredit item lists), upstream's config version migrations, and the Service.ObjectTable API rename.
- **New optional integrations:** Lifestream and vnavmesh IPC wrappers with upstream's MovementTask movement helpers, and the NPC/menu highlight services. All are gracefully skipped when the providing plugin is absent.
- Font rendering keeps the fork's Dalamud asset-font setup; the fork keeps its own tab UI (Windows/), teleport flow, Hub integration and Quick Controls.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v1.2.7.4 (2026-10-05) [testing]
- Added map locations for the two shop NPCs at the Gold Saucer that had none: the tack & feed trader at Chocobo Square and the euphoric attendant. Both now draw their Flag and TP buttons like every other listed shop instead of having no buttons at all.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Five shop NPCs remain without a location on purpose: the game's own data places them nowhere (no Level-sheet placement, no placement dataset entry - campaign and seasonal attendants such as Eirene's Rain Exchange and Ermina that only exist while their event runs). They keep the behaviour introduced in 1.2.7.3: one note at debug level, no buttons.

plugins.author: croizat, dajoey
plugins.name: Lazy Fate Automation
plugins.punchline: Fully automated FATE grinding utilizing vnavmesh, lifestream, and Gluttony Combo.
plugins.description: Automates FATE grinding, including Zodiac Atma, Anima Luminous Crystals, Resistance Memories, Phantom Demiatmas, Yo-kai Watch Medals, and Bicolor Gemstones. Seamlessly integrates with vnavmesh for pathing and flight, lifestream for zone swapping, TextAdvance for dialogue skipping, and Gluttony Combo/BossMod for combat. Use /lazyfate to open.
plugins.changelog:
v0.0.3.12 (2026-11-14) [testing]
- The plugin windows have been rebuilt on the shared LalaUiKit: one consistent layout with themed section headers, unified spacing and colour accents. All settings and behaviour are unchanged, and existing configuration loads as-is.

v0.0.3.11 (2026-11-10) [testing]
- Rebuilt against the Dalamud 15.0.4.0 payload for game patch 7.58. No functional changes.

v0.0.3.10 (2026-10-31) [testing]
- **The FATE grind no longer starts FATEs above your level.** Level sync only lowers your level to match a FATE, it never raises it, so a FATE above your level could not be contributed to and walking to it only wasted time. FATEs above your level are now skipped; the tracker's unavailable list shows "FATE level N is above your level M". FATEs at or below your level run exactly as before.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.0.3.9 (2026-10-18) [testing]
- **Display name format and sort order changes are now saved.** Edits in the FATE tracker's "Sorting & Display" settings previously lived only in memory and reverted on the next plugin load; every change now persists immediately.
- **Reset to Default restores the actual default sort order.** The reset button dropped the Time Remaining criterion and put Time Remaining Urgent in ascending order (urgent FATEs last); it now restores the shipped six-entry default, shared with the config's own default so the two cannot drift apart.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.0.3.8 (2026-10-13) [testing]
- **BossMod Reborn no longer runs its own job rotations beside Gluttony Combo during FATEs.** The FATE grind creates and uses its own BossMod preset, "LazyFateAutomation", holding only the movement, FATE-targeting, level-sync and stay-close-to-target modules (melee and tanks close in, other roles hold at 10 yalms), and rewrites it each time the grind starts so an old or edited copy cannot bring job rotations back.
- **The grind no longer clears a BossMod preset another plugin (such as AutoDuty) or the player set.** It turns its preset on and off with BossMod Reborn's standard preset calls and only ever clears its own. Two calls BossMod Reborn does not provide, which failed on every attempt, are gone, and a failing call is logged once per run.
- The BossMod preset named "Gluttony" that earlier versions created is no longer used. It is left untouched in BossMod's preset list and can be deleted there by hand.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v0.0.3.7 (2026-10-05) [testing]
- **The boss FATE icon on the server info bar entry now actually renders.** The previous testing build showed no icon at all because the glyph reference pointed at an empty slot instead of the boss FATE icon; the icon value is now pinned so it stays the boss glyph.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Click behavior, the confirming second click and every other part of the server bar entry are unchanged.

plugins.author: dajoey
plugins.name: Lazy Skyward Tracker
plugins.punchline: Track your Skyward points for all jobs toward the Pteranodon mount
plugins.description: Tracks all jobs' Skyward points for the Pteranodon mount achievement. Scans your inventory for Skybuilders turn-in items and projects how many points they'll add, shown as a cyan bar extension on each job's progress bar. Use /lazysky to open.
plugins.changelog:
v0.0.3.3 (2026-11-14) [testing]
- The plugin windows have been rebuilt on the shared LalaUiKit: one consistent layout with themed section headers, unified spacing and colour accents. All settings and behaviour are unchanged, and existing configuration loads as-is.

v0.0.3.2 (2026-11-10) [testing]
- Rebuilt against the Dalamud 15.0.4.0 payload for game patch 7.58. No functional changes.

v0.0.3.1 (2026-10-04) [testing]

- Fixed a rare game crash when the plugin updates while the game is running: while the achievement-progress hook is active and the plugin is updated again, it is disabled only after any call still inside it has finished, so a call can no longer land on a hook that is already gone. Skybuilders' point tracking is unchanged.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.0.3.0 (2026-09-05)

- Added the in-game "What's new" popup. After Lazy Skyward Tracker updates, its changelog now opens once inside the game so the changes are visible without a trip to GitHub. It waits until the character is logged in and out of combat, duty, cutscenes and zoning; closing it (Got it, X or Escape) marks it read. Type `/lazysky changelog` any time to reopen it.
- No change to tracking: Skybuilders' points per job, the achievement progress read and the Diadem crediting all work exactly as before.

v0.0.2.2 (2026-06-26)

- **Gathered Diadem items are now credited to the correct gathering class.** Miner

- **Class is now read from the game's own data.** `BuildGathererLookup` derives the

- No change to which items count or their point values. Raw, non-collectable node

plugins.author: dajoey
plugins.name: LazyFoodBuff
plugins.punchline: Never forget to eat your food again.
plugins.description: Auto-eats food in combat duties with per-job selection, auto-select based on best stats, and a low-food warning.
plugins.changelog:
v0.1.5.3 (2026-11-14) [testing]
- The plugin windows have been rebuilt on the shared LalaUiKit: one consistent layout with themed section headers, unified spacing and colour accents. All settings and behaviour are unchanged, and existing configuration loads as-is.

v0.1.5.2 (2026-11-10) [testing]
- Rebuilt against the Dalamud 15.0.4.0 payload for game patch 7.58. No functional changes.

v0.1.5.1 (2026-10-03) [testing]
- **Quick controls for the Lazy Hub window.** The plugin now offers auto-eating, "Only in combat duties", the minutes of food left before eating again and the low-food warning with its count to Lazy Hub (`/lazy`) over Dalamud IPC, so they can be changed from one window next to the other lalalazy plugins. Each change does exactly what the matching setting in the plugin's own window does.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Without Lazy Hub installed the plugin behaves exactly as before.

v0.1.5.0 (2026-09-21)

- **"Only eat in combat duties" now covers Crucible of the Unbroken.** The five boards count as combat duties, and so does the Bentbranch Meadows entry area while playing Beastmaster (the one job that can enter), so the meal is eaten before a run starts. Eating before entry matters: a meal eaten inside does not refill HP to the raised maximum.

v0.1.4.0 (2026-09-05)

- Optional decision diagnostics, off by default. Turn on "Log food decisions" (settings window, Advanced / Diagnostics) or run `/lazyfoodbuff telemetry on`, and every time the plugin settles on a food for the current job it writes one line to the plugin log: the food it picked, its score, and the runner-ups it beat â€” plus a second line when that food is actually eaten. The point is the runner-ups: "picked X at 41.20 over Y at 40.80" is the shape of evidence that can eventually say whether the auto-select weights are right. Nothing leaves the machine; the lines only go to the local plugin log.

- Honest caveat: this is a data-collection investment, not an answer. The outcome side (what a food actually did to damage) needs weeks of encounter data before it says anything statistically â€” the plugin log will quietly accumulate the decision half in the meantime.
- Nothing about food selection changed. When the toggle is off, the only cost is one boolean read.

v0.1.3.1 (2026-09-05)

- The "What's new" popup now opens after this very update. 0.1.3.0 stayed silent the first time it ran because it had no record of the last version shown; the gate now tells an updated plugin (settings file already present) apart from a brand-new install (none yet) and only the latter stays quiet (`ChangelogGate.Options.ExistingInstall`, read from `pi.ConfigFile.Exists`.

- Nothing else changed. The notes can be reopened later with `/lazyfoodbuff changelog`.

plugins.author: dajoey
plugins.name: Lazy Gear Collector
plugins.punchline: Track upgradable gear sets and what it costs to finish them
plugins.description: Tracks upgradable gear collections piece by piece. Starts with Occult Crescent: North Horn's Phantom Vision sets - all 7 roles, 5 slots, 4 tiers. Shows which pieces you own and at what tier, what the next upgrade costs, and the exact obol/fixative shortfall to finish a role or the whole collection. Every item ID and price is read from the game's own shop data at runtime, so it stays correct across patches. Also flags Arcanaut's gear you can trade up for free. Use /lazygear to open.

Each change does exactly what the matching setting in the plugin's own window does.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Without Lazy Hub installed the plugin behaves exactly as before.

v0.0.2.0 (2026-09-05)

- Added the in-game "What's new" popup. After Lazy Gear Collector updates, its changelog now opens once inside the game so the changes are visible without a trip to GitHub. It waits until the character is logged in and out of combat, duty, cutscenes and zoning; closing it (Got it, X or Escape) marks it read. Type `/lazygear changelog` any time to reopen it.
- No change to collection tracking: the Phantom Vision set, tier detection, ownership counting and the remaining-cost figures are all unchanged.

- **First release.** Tracks upgradable gear collections: which pieces are owned, what tier each one

plugins.author: dajoey
plugins.name: LazyCrafter
plugins.punchline: What can I make right now, what's it worth, and what would it take to make the rest?
plugins.description: Catalogs every recipe you can craft, buckets them by how much effort the missing materials take, prices them with Universalis, and hands the missing-material work to Artisan / GBR / ARC / Lifestream.
plugins.changelog:
v0.1.7.11 (2026-11-14) [testing]
- The plugin windows have been rebuilt on the shared LalaUiKit: one consistent layout with themed section headers, unified spacing and colour accents. All settings and behaviour are unchanged, and existing configuration loads as-is.

v0.1.7.10 (2026-11-10) [testing]
- Rebuilt against the Dalamud 15.0.4.0 payload for game patch 7.58. No functional changes.

v0.1.7.9 (2026-10-17) [testing]
- **Market-price lookups no longer log warnings while they retry.** When Universalis is slow or busy it answers with a temporary "try again" status or takes longer than before; the price client already retries those on its own with a pause between tries - that is its designed behavior, not a fault, so those lines now go to the debug log. Only one warning is written when a batch gives up entirely after all retries, and stale cached prices are used meanwhile, exactly as before.
- **The price client now waits up to 60 seconds per request instead of 20.** Under load, Universalis sometimes finishes a large price query just after the old 20-second cutoff; the request was cancelled while the server was still working on it and the prices for that batch were refetched from scratch. The longer budget lets those queries land.
- Market-price log lines no longer paste a hundred item numbers into the log; a batch is described as its item count instead.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Full harness: 401/401 PASS (6 new).

v0.1.7.8 (2026-10-07) [testing]
- **Knightshopper no longer buys units that are sitting on a retainer.** The purchase target counted everything the catalog can see, but the fetch-from-retainer step runs after the purchase and brings those units in anyway - with 90 units on a retainer, none in the bags and 9 missing, the run bought 99 instead of 9. The target now counts what is physically in the bags, and the fetch tops the bags up to exactly what the cart needs; every currency routes on the same corrected target.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Full harness: 395/395 PASS (4 new).

v0.1.7.7 (2026-10-07) [testing]
- **Cart dispatches can hand vendor purchases to Knightshopper.** When a dispatch is missing materials that a vendor sells - gil vendors, and currency vendors priced in one currency Knightshopper supports - the run groups that list by currency and buys it through Knightshopper's purchase IPC at target inventory totals, before any shopping stop fires. The run prints each group, its currency and the estimated total cost before anything is spent. Market-board items are never routed, and one attempt per group means a refused purchase never retries; a repeat dispatch asks for the same target totals at most, so nothing is ever bought twice.
- If Knightshopper is missing, busy, refuses LazyCrafter, or has no unlocked vendor for an item, those items fall back to the usual shopping stops - flagged and named in chat exactly as before. Purchases also need LazyCrafter on Knightshopper's allowed-plugins IPC list, which is set in Knightshopper's own settings (IPC permissions); LazyCrafter never changes Knightshopper's settings. The new switch (on by default) is "Buy vendor items through Knightshopper during a dispatch" in the settings.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- With the switch off, or without Knightshopper installed, the run behaves exactly as before.
- Full harness: 391/391 PASS (16 new).

v0.1.7.6 (2026-10-03) [testing]
- **Quick controls for the Lazy Hub window.** The plugin now offers the catalog and price settings (recipes above the character's level, the undersupplied thresholds, the revenue basis, pricing at the home world only, the price refresh interval, the price-match message) and the cart-run hand-off switches (fetching materials from retainers, walking to a summoning bell or to vendors, preferring a currency shop) to Lazy Hub (`/lazy`) over Dalamud IPC, so they can be changed from one window next to the other lalalazy plugins. Each change does exactly what the matching setting in the plugin's own window does.
- The cart-run hand-off switches can only be changed while no cart run is active.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Without Lazy Hub installed the plugin behaves exactly as before.

plugins.author: dajoey
plugins.name: Lazy Market Companion
plugins.punchline: Auto-lists your always-sell items and matches market board prices
plugins.description: Keep an Auto-Market list of items you always sell. The companion lists them through your retainers in the stack size you choose (keeping a reserve in your bags if you want), prices every listing by matching the lowest board price instead of undercutting, and can do all of it inside AutoRetainer's venture cycle. Also re-prices existing listings (Auto Pinch). Successor to Dagobert Price Matcher; your old settings are imported automatically.
plugins.changelog:
v0.2.8.21 (2026-11-14) [testing]
- The plugin windows have been rebuilt on the shared LalaUiKit: one consistent layout with themed section headers, unified spacing and colour accents. All settings and behaviour are unchanged, and existing configuration loads as-is.

v0.2.8.20 (2026-11-10) [testing]
- Rebuilt against the Dalamud 15.0.4.0 payload for game patch 7.58. No functional changes.

v0.2.8.19 (2026-11-10) [testing]
- **Mannequin listings are now detected on clients in any language.** The mannequin check matched a hardcoded English/German/French list of the context menu's "adjust price" label, so on a client in any other language a mannequin listing was never detected and the automation clicked "adjust price" on a mannequin item. The check now compares the menu against the client's own localized Adjust Price label (the fix is ported from upstream Dagobert's Auto Pinch, whose absorbed price formula this plugin already carries).
- **The manual post hotkey now starts from fresh prices.** Opening a retainer's sell dialog while the post hotkey was held kept whatever the previous session had left behind - cached board prices, an in-flight price lookup, per-session gates - so the price written into the dialog could be stale. The session state is now cleared when the sell dialog opens, before the post chain runs (the fix is ported from upstream Dagobert's Auto Pinch).
- **The manual post chain no longer fires from unrelated windows.** The listener behind the post hotkey was registered for every addon opening, so any window that opened while the hotkey was held could queue a manual post chain for a window that was not the retainer sell dialog. It is now scoped to the retainer sell dialog itself (the fix is ported from upstream Dagobert's Auto Pinch).
- Untried build: tested offline against the plugin's offline test suite, not yet in the game.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.2.8.18 (2026-11-09) [testing]
- **Holding the pinch hotkey no longer re-fires the pinch.** The hotkey was read as a level: on every frame the key stayed down the retainer list and sell list draws each re-ran their pinch check, so holding the key queued a new Auto Pinch every drawn frame - and fired again the moment a finished run freed the busy guard. The key is now read as an edge: one press is one fire, and a held key stays quiet until it is released and pressed again (the fix is ported from upstream Dagobert's Auto Pinch, whose absorbed price formula this plugin already carries). Cancelling a run is unchanged: the Cancel button and the /lmc command; the upstream press-again-to-cancel shortcut was deliberately not adopted.
- Untried build: tested offline against the plugin's offline test suite, not yet in the game.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.2.8.17 (2026-11-06) [testing]
- **The overlay buttons no longer have to cover the retainer windows' own controls.** The Auto Pinch, Auto Market and Sweep to Bags buttons are pinned to the top-right corner of the retainer list and retainer sell list windows, where they can cover the venture currency and the windows' close button (reported in issue #12). Each of the three buttons can now be hidden individually under Settings -> Retainers & Hotkeys -> "Retainer window buttons". A hidden button's action stays reachable through the /lmc subcommands, and the Cancel button shown while a run is in progress is never hidden. All three default to shown, so existing settings keep working exactly as before.
- Untried build: tested offline against the plugin's offline test suite, not yet in the game.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.2.8.16 (2026-10-17) [testing]
- **Fresh installs no longer show an import notice for a plugin that was never installed.** A leftover line in the configuration loader set the "imported from Dagobert Price Matcher" flag true on every load that created a new configuration, so a brand-new install showed the import notice and the uninstall hint even though no settings were ever imported. The flag now keeps its false default; a genuine import from a found Dagobert configuration still sets it, and the load log's imported= field reports the real value.
- Untried build: tested offline against the plugin's offline test suite, not yet in the game.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
