plugins.author: dajoey
plugins.name: Lazy Fish Sitter
plugins.punchline: Sits you down while you fish. That's it.
plugins.description: Checks every few seconds while you are fishing; if you are not sitting, it runs /sit for you. Leaves you alone once you are seated (ground sit, chair, or pose).
plugins.changelog:
v0.1.5.3 (2026-11-14) [testing]
- The plugin windows have been rebuilt on the shared LalaUiKit: one consistent layout with themed section headers, unified spacing and colour accents. All settings and behaviour are unchanged, and existing configuration loads as-is.

v0.1.5.2 (2026-11-10) [testing]
- Rebuilt against the Dalamud 15.0.4.0 payload for game patch 7.58. No functional changes.

v0.1.5.1 (2026-10-03) [testing]
- **Quick controls for the Lazy Hub window.** The plugin now offers the "Sit while fishing" switch to Lazy Hub (`/lazy`) over Dalamud IPC, so they can be changed from one window next to the other lalalazy plugins. Each change does exactly what the matching setting in the plugin's own window does.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Without Lazy Hub installed the plugin behaves exactly as before.

v0.1.5.0 (2026-09-25)

- Persistent seating across fishing hole visits: if the character stands up during a visit to a fishing hole (such as putting the rod away to change bait or use cordials, or manually standing up), the automation now detects the stand and re-seats upon resuming fishing or on the subsequent cast.
- Unaccepted send cap: the 3-send limit per hole visit is now scoped to consecutive unaccepted sends rather than a lifetime cap per hole visit. When a sit is accepted by the game, the counter resets, ensuring long fishing sessions with multiple bait changes or pauses remain seated while still guarding against unbounded retry loops if commands are blocked.

v0.1.4.0 (2026-09-25)

- Sits after a cast: the automated /sit check now runs after a cast once the line is settled in the water (`LineInWater`), in addition to the pre-cast standby beat (`PoleReady`). In active fishing loops or when using automated casting tools, the standby beat between casts typically lasts under a second, which previously prevented the automation from ever triggering across repeated casts (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `IsStandbyBeat`).
- Safe timing: commands are sent only after the line has been in the water for at least 1 second to ensure the cast animation has resolved, and continue to be refused during active casting, biting, hooking, reeling, and position change animations.

v0.1.3.0 (2026-09-05)

- Correction first, because the last release's notes got the game wrong: FFXIV does NOT force standing on every hooked fish. If the character is sitting when the cast starts, the game keeps it seated for the whole loop - a hook may cause a momentary stand, but the game sits back down on its own. v0.1.2.0 was designed around that mistake (one /sit per cast) and this release replaces it entirely.
- Sit once, then stay out of the way. The plugin now sends a single /sit per fishing trip, at a moment the game will actually accept it, and then does nothing for the rest of the trip (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `Decide`).
- That moment is the standby beat: rod out, no line in the water (`FishingEventHandler.State == PoleReady`), held for a second, at least 3 seconds clear of a bite/hook/reel, with the character read as standing for 3 seconds straight. It will never fire mid-cast, with a line in the water, mid-bite, mid-reel, or while already sitting down or standing up (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `IsStandbyBeat`).
- That is why v0.1.1.0 looked like it did nothing: it sent its one /sit the instant the fishing flag came on, which is after the line is already out, and the game swallows the emote there - ten sends across ten sessions, no effect. v0.1.2.0 still counted "line in water" as a valid moment and would have done the same thing.
- No re-sit after every cast, ever. A brief standing read just after a bite, hook, reel or collectable prompt is treated as the game's own animation, not as the character standing up, so the plugin does nothing and lets the game re-seat (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `IsHookish`).
- A "trip" is one visit to a fishing hole, not one cast. The fishing flag drops between casts (v0.1.1.0 saw ten "sessions" in 21 minutes), so the limits are now anchored to the hole and only reset after 20 seconds away from it (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `StartTrip` / `EndTrip`).
- Anti-yo-yo guards, all hard, because a /sit on a seated character STANDS them: never sends while any seated signal reads seated; at least 10 seconds between sends; at most 3 sends per trip with a log line when it stops; and once the game has taken a sit this trip it will not send again unless the seated read has proved it still reports seated with the rod out (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `Decide`, guards 1-5).
- The settings window now shows the trip counters: whether the character is at a hole, sits used out of 3, whether the game took the sit, and whether the seated read works while fishing (file: `ConfigWindow.cs`).
- Removed the "check interval" slider. The plugin now looks every frame, because every limit that matters is a real time limit (10 seconds between sends, 3 seconds of standing before it believes the read, 3 sends a trip) and a 2-second poll just made it step over short standby beats between quick casts. Saved values are ignored, not lost (files: `ConfigWindow.cs`, `Configuration.cs`).
- The policy is now a plain C# class with no game code in it (`Core/SitPolicy.cs`), replayed offline against 26 scripted fishing sessions by `tests/LazyFishSitter.Harness`. Three releases in a row shipped a rule that only broke in game; the harness caught three more before this one shipped, including a dead window that would have stopped a refused /sit from ever being retried.
- Keeps the detailed state logging (every fishing-state and posture change, 40 lines a minute max) and adds a one-line trip summary, so the still-open question - does the game ever report seated while a line is out - can be answered from the log without typing anything in game (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `EndTrip`).

plugins.name: LazyRetainerLive
plugins.punchline: Real-time retainer venture countdowns for your dashboard.
plugins.description: Serves the logged-in character's live retainer and venture state on loopback HTTP (127.0.0.1:10504) so the ffxiv dashboard relay can show real-time venture countdowns instead of AutoRetainer's occasionally-stale file cache.
plugins.changelog:
v0.1.0.4 (2026-11-14) [testing]
- The plugin windows have been rebuilt on the shared LalaUiKit: one consistent layout with themed section headers, unified spacing and colour accents. All settings and behaviour are unchanged, and existing configuration loads as-is.

v0.1.0.3 (2026-11-10) [testing]
- Rebuilt against the Dalamud 15.0.4.0 payload for game patch 7.58. No functional changes.

v0.1.0.2 (2026-10-03) [testing]
- **Quick controls for the Lazy Hub window.** The plugin now offers the switch that serves retainer data (the port stays in the plugin's own window) to Lazy Hub (`/lazy`) over Dalamud IPC, so they can be changed from one window next to the other lalalazy plugins. Each change does exactly what the matching setting in the plugin's own window does.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Without Lazy Hub installed the plugin behaves exactly as before.

v0.1.0.1 (2026-09-05)


- Corrected a wrong claim in the v0.1.0.0 notes below (and on the mod's web page): **the endpoint does not answer 503 on logout.** Once logged in, it keeps serving that character's last known retainer state - including at the title screen - and only ever answers 503 if it has never read the retainer table at all since the plugin loaded (i.e. it started at the title screen and no login has happened yet). That freeze is deliberate and is the better behaviour: measured previously the frozen live snapshot was still *newer* than AutoRetainer's file, so falling back to the file on logout would have shown the dashboard **older** data, not fresher. No behaviour was changed here - only the description was wrong.
- The settings window no longer reports "serving live snapshot" while logged out. It now distinguishes three states: no snapshot yet, serving a live snapshot, or serving the last-known snapshot while the game is in transition.


- For anything scripting against this endpoint: `readAt` is the time the request was **served**, not the time the data was read from the game, so it does not reveal how stale a frozen snapshot is. Use the settings window (or `/lazyretainerlive debug`) to tell live from frozen.

v0.1.0.0 (2026-09-05)


- First release. LazyRetainerLive reads the logged-in character's LIVE retainer table (the same in-memory data AutoRetainer uses to drive its own countdowns) and serves it as JSON on `http://127.0.0.1:10504/retainers`, so the ffxiv dashboard's retainer panel can show venture countdowns that update the moment a venture is collected instead of whenever AutoRetainer next saves its config file.
- When not logged in (or the live table has no data yet) the endpoint answers HTTP 503, which tells the dashboard relay to fall back to AutoRetainer's file. Loopback only - the port is never reachable from other machines.


- Companion of AutoRetainer - it reads, it never writes, assigns, or collects anything. Settings: Enabled (default on) and loopback port (default 10504). Commands: `/lazyretainerlive` opens settings, `/lazyretainerlive debug` dumps listener + snapshot state, `/lazyretainerlive changelog` reopens this popup.
- Why this exists: AutoRetainer's `DefaultConfig.json` (which feeds the dashboard today) is saved only at AutoRetainer's own save points, so its venture rows can be tens of minutes stale while ventures are actually completing. The countdown for the logged-in character lives in the game's memory - this plugin is a small read-only window onto it.

plugins.author: dajoey
plugins.name: LazyCrucible
plugins.punchline: Crucible of the Unbroken familiar picks, filled in for every fight
plugins.description: For the Beastmaster duty Crucible of the Unbroken. Fills the ten-familiar run roster at the Bentbranch Meadows entry menu and the three Battlehorn slots before every fight with the familiars that answer that fight's mechanics: elemental weakness, interrupts, dispels, cleanses and crowd control, skipping knocked-out familiars and benching badly hurt ones. Picks are announced in chat. Every automation has its own toggle and manual edits always win. Includes the beast-pick advisor for every board and a read-only recorder that writes each Crucible screen to the Dalamud log. Use /lazycrucible to open.
plugins.changelog:
v0.1.9.18 (2026-11-14) [testing]
- The plugin windows have been rebuilt on the shared LalaUiKit: one consistent layout with themed section headers, unified spacing and colour accents. All settings and behaviour are unchanged, and existing configuration loads as-is.

v0.1.9.17 (2026-11-10) [testing]
- Rebuilt against the Dalamud 15.0.4.0 payload for game patch 7.58. No functional changes.

v0.1.9.16 (2026-10-13) [testing]
- **"Score: three familiars" run-roster mode, off by default.** For score runs. A run roster of one to three familiars scores the Beast Squad III bonus on every board, so with the option on the run roster is the best three familiars for the whole board instead of the board's full roster. The three are chosen from the familiars you own and that are not knocked out: they cover as many of the board's required interrupt, dispel and cleanse needs as any three can, then the damage the board calls to be blunted, then three of one kin when that costs no required cover (the Gambit bonus), then the rest by points. A roster of three saved for a different board is rewritten for the board you enter. Whatever the three cannot answer on the board is named on the window's summary line; nothing pops up. With three or fewer familiars the game registers the battlehorns itself, so the plugin leaves them alone. Found in the settings window and the Lazy Hub as "Score: three familiars".
- With the option off, nothing changes. While AutoDuty drives the run roster the plugin stands by there, option on or off.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v0.1.9.15 (2026-10-13) [testing]
- **Mitigation in the horn picks.** Fights with a damage wall now field a familiar that blunts it, ranked below every interrupt, dispel and cleanse need, and counted only for a familiar above the danger HP line. Durga's Atomic Ray gets a magic answer (drake's Smoldering Scales, pugil's Water Wall or a Scalekin's Scaleskin); Borgny gets coblyn's Vulcanize for the poison plus a magic answer; Gargoyle's Sweeping Evisceration gets a physical answer (a Beastkin's Beastskin, coblyn's Vulcanize or adamantoise's Harden Shell). The fight guide lists these under "Calls for".
- One telemetry line per fight names the team on the horns and the needs it cannot answer (`uncovered=`).
- **Works with AutoDuty.** While AutoDuty runs, it handles the run roster, shop, treasure, spoils and campsite itself, so the plugin stands by there; the battlehorns are AutoDuty's only with its "Fight picks" on, and the plugin picks them otherwise. AutoDuty's active profile is read through AutoDuty's own interface (its config file when that is unavailable), never changed; when neither can be read, every screen stands by, as before. The window shows one quiet line naming the screens it is standing by on.
- **No more corrections on top of AutoDuty's familiar picks.** AutoDuty re-applied its own picks every time, so they never reached a fight.
- **Fight guide: the Snarl -> Parting Blow advice is gone** (Parting Blow no longer dodges a hit since the September 17 hotfix). Plain tankbusters say to let a familiar with enough HP take them under Snarl; poisoning ones (Deadly Thrust, Cold Caress, Toxic Vomit) say to Parting Blow right after the hit so the poison leaves with the familiar; Gargoyle's Sweeping Evisceration says to save the Blink tome for it.
- Item values: Beastly Knife is valued like the elemental axes; Hero's Crown counts its Excellence proc (9 s of nullified attacks); Rapid Recast gear is valued; reraise items are worth a little less at Third Degree.
- **Patch 7.57: battlehorns the game registered itself (teams of three or fewer) are left alone**; a knocked-out member of a three-familiar team is no longer toggled off the horns.
- **Patch 7.57: the board's degree survives a job change** (the game now keeps the Crucible Mode until logout), so the degree passed to Gluttony Combo is no longer reset when the character returns to Beastmaster. It is forgotten at logout.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v0.1.9.14 (2026-10-06) [testing]
- **The board's difficulty degree now reaches Gluttony Combo during a fight.** The degree is set in the lobby (by a click or by AutoDuty) and the character then zones into the duty; the plugin used to forget it at every loading screen, so a fight always read as an unknown degree. It is now kept across loading screens and still forgotten when the Beastmaster job is left or the plugin unloads.

v0.1.9.13 (2026-10-06) [testing]
- **The board's difficulty degree is now read and shared with Gluttony Combo.** The Crucible board layout reports the degree whenever it is set, by a click or by AutoDuty; the plugin keeps the last one (Standard, First, Second or Third) and offers it to Gluttony Combo 1.0.4.288 or newer, which uses it to price the hits a familiar or the character will take. The degree is forgotten when the Beastmaster job is left, and until the first time it is set the plugin reports none. The change is logged as one `PS|` line (`note=degree`).
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

plugins.author: dajoey
plugins.name: Lazy Hub
plugins.punchline: One window for every lalalazy plugin.
plugins.description: One in-game window for the whole lalalazy suite. Turn plugins on and off, change their common settings and open their windows from one place, with Gluttony Combo's Auto-Rotation switch and drag-to-hotbar action buttons up front, plus a server info bar entry. Open it with /lazy.
plugins.changelog:
v0.1.1.5 (2026-11-14) [testing]
- The bundled interface toolkit no longer carries an unused image-processing library, so the plugin installs fewer files and no longer ships a package with known security advisories. No behavior changes.

v0.1.1.4 (2026-11-14) [testing]
- The plugin windows have been rebuilt on the shared LalaUiKit: one consistent layout with themed section headers, unified spacing and colour accents. All settings and behaviour are unchanged, and existing configuration loads as-is.

v0.1.1.3 (2026-11-10) [testing]
- Rebuilt against the Dalamud 15.0.4.0 payload for game patch 7.58. No functional changes.

v0.1.1.2 (2026-11-07) [testing]

- No plugin-code changes: the plugin now builds against a fixed Dalamud library set (the pinned staging 15.0.3.9 payload) instead of whichever libraries the build machine happens to have installed, so packaging this plugin works reliably again. The hub window is unchanged.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.1.1.1 (2026-11-05) [testing]

v0.1.1.2 (2026-11-07) [testing]

- No plugin-code changes: the plugin now builds against a fixed Dalamud library set (the pinned staging 15.0.3.9 payload) instead of whichever libraries the build machine happens to have installed, so packaging this plugin works reliably again. The hub window is unchanged.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

- Updated the bundled KamiToolKit UI library to the current upstream version; the hub window is built on the framework's current internals now, and the window-frame tint targets the framework's texture-backed chrome nodes.
- The native window is created on the game's main thread after the UI framework finishes initializing, instead of during plugin load.
- Kept the fork's hot-reload safety guard: teardown disables the hooks, lets any call already inside them finish, and only then disposes.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

plugins.author: NightmareXIV
plugins.name: Splatoon
plugins.punchline: Scriptable overlay engine for drawing mechanics, markers, and indicators in real-time
plugins.description:
Splatoon is a scriptable telegraph and overlay engine for Final Fantasy XIV, built on the Dalamud plugin framework. It allows scripts to draw shapes, markers, labels, and indicators directly in the game world. These overlays can be attached to actors, positions, or events, and are rendered with precise positioning.

Splatoon does not include presets or encounter logic by default. If you want presets, you must create them yourself or import them from others.

In short, Splatoon draws things. What it draws is up to you!
plugins.changelog:
- Library updates
- Improvements to map effect tab

plugins.author: Aida Enna
plugins.name: Macro Chain Redux
plugins.punchline: A modified fork of the old Macro Chain that allows you to run multiple macros one after the other (or repeat them).
plugins.description:
Allows for a macro to continue onto the next macro by using '/nextmacro' on the last line of a macro.
Adding '/nextmacro' on the last line of Macro #01 will automatically execute Macro #02
Adding '/nextmacro down' on the last line of Macro #01 will automatically execute Macro #11
Also allows executing any macro from chat using '/runmacro'
You can repeat a macro by using /runmacro inside the macro followed by the number of the macro you're editing
Using '/macrocancel' will stop the currently running macro
plugins.changelog: - Updated for patch 7.5

plugins.author: Haselnussbomber
plugins.name: LeveHelper
plugins.punchline: A little helper for Levequests.
plugins.description: A little helper to check which Levequests have been completed and which are missing.
plugins.changelog:
- Added: You can now click on the group header in the Type filter to filter for either all Fieldcraft, Tradecraft or Grand Company Leves.
- Added: When GatherBuddy is installed, the Queue and Recipe Tree now display GatherBuddys tooltip on fish and spearfish, including info about the Bait, Time and Weather restrictions and the next uptimes.  
  - Please note that GatherBuddy uses the client language, not Dalamuds UI language like LeveHelper. It's out of my control.
- Fixed: Some gatherables did not show up in the Queue.

Regarding the Levemete filter

The game's database doesn't list which Levemete issues which Levequests and multiple old NPCs also rotate their Levequests when you complete one.

I used to scrape a wiki to gather this data, but two weeks ago, we added Levequest issuer tracking to the Tracky plugin and already have more entries than the wiki provided!

Some entries that I could confirm through another wiki are still missing, so manually added those back in for now.

If you'd like to help us, please install the Tracky plugin and enable uploads in its settings.

Thank you! :)

plugins.author: The Combat Reborn Team
plugins.name: Rotation Solver Reborn
plugins.punchline: Analyses combat information every frame and finds the best action.
plugins.description:
Analyses combat information every frame and finds the best action.

This means almost all the information available in one frame in combat, including the status of all players in the party, the status of any hostile targets, skill cooldowns, the MP and HP of characters, the location of characters, casting status of the hostile target, combo, combat duration, player level, etc.
Then, it will highlight the best action on the hot bar, or help you to click on it.
It is designed for `general combat`, not for savage or ultimate. Use it carefully.

plugins.author: The Redheaded Witch, WillWolf76
plugins.name: Fashion Report Calculator / Dye Finder
plugins.punchline: Know your Fashion Report points on the spot and help crowdsource new items and dyes!
plugins.description:
This is the new and improved Fashion Report System. This plugin will allow you to open a window that will show you what your fashion report status is vs the current week's theme.

There are a few parts to this. Since the only way to get Fashion Report for the week to my knowledge is speaking to Masked Rose after Tuesdays reset, this plugin takes the first person who does talk to him and updates everyone else. So only one person per week needs to speak to Masked Rose.

You can click on a theme and pull all the known items for that theme for that specific slot. You also get a very detailed breakdown of how much points you are getting based on what you are currently wearing.

The plugin also stores the attempts of those using the mod (just the data from fashioncheck, no user information) so that we can figure out the dyes faster and share information faster. The information in this table is wiped every week since once we discover the dyes, it is useless.

I still have more upgrades to do, including adding a dye window and the window that will help calculate the weekly dyes. I already have an idea of how I want to write them, so it shouldn't take me too long. If you have suggestions on how I can upgrade this, please share with me on github!

Credit for the program goes to it's original creator, WillWolf76, who wrote this for me originally.

When this plugin updates the database, it also updates my Discord Bot which you can set up to post fashion report each week. It's set to update on Tuesdays and Fridays (week start and dye information added). Link to add the Discord Bot is in the about section.
plugins.changelog: Fixed some minor bugs.

plugins.author: Asteria Nocturna
plugins.name: Divination.AetheryteLinkInChat
plugins.punchline: Quick teleport for mob hunts and treasure hunts!
plugins.description: Display a teleport link to the nearest aetherite for the map link from the in-game chat. Type /alic to configure the plugin.
plugins.changelog:
e8f691d: Merge pull request #816 from SlashNephy/feat/alic-hunt-journeys

feat(AetheryteLinkInChat): prefer Faloop's starting points for hunt spawn points
74b4951: feat(AetheryteLinkInChat): add exits missing from the game's map markers

The game's map markers do not describe the exit from Yanxia to the
Doman Enclave (The One River): the marker in Yanxia points to the
obsolete map 437, and the current map 463 has no marker back to Yanxia.
So routes through the Doman Enclave were never considered, which is the
Yanxia example in #656.

- Add MapConnections for such exits, starting with Yanxia <-> the Doman
  Enclave. Comparing Faloop's boundary starting points with the game's
  map markers found no other missing exit
- Consider them in the route calculation as ConnectionTeleportPath,
  without counting the distance inside the connected map, as where the
  exit leads to is not known
- Show them like zone boundaries, and stop the Lifestream teleport there

Refs #656

Co-Authored-By: Claude Mythos 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
a3c0a1f: feat(AetheryteLinkInChat): prefer Faloop's starting points for hunt spawn points

Straight-line distance on the map ignores terrain, height and walls, so
the nearest aetheryte is often not the best one to start from.

Faloop's zone data has the spawn points of hunt marks, each with a
journeyPoiId that points to the aetheryte or zone boundary to start
from. Embed them (generated by Scripts/generate_hunt_journeys.py) and,
when a map link is at a known spawn point, only consider the routes that
enter the map at its starting point. Otherwise, fall back to the
straight-line distance as before.

Refs #656

Co-Authored-By: Claude Mythos 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
97ddbb9: Merge pull request #815 from SlashNephy/fix/alic-detect-world

fix(AetheryteLinkInChat): prefer the world name after the cross world icon
e5d9e91: fix(AetheryteLinkInChat): prefer the world name after the cross world icon

DetectWorld picked the first public world in World sheet order whose
name appeared anywhere in the message. Mob names such as Odin and
Behemoth are also world names, so "Odin <map link> <CrossWorld>Cerberus"
resolved to Odin (row 66) instead of Cerberus (row 80), while
"Odin ... Omega" happened to work because Omega is row 39. The map link
trimming only removes text from the link marker (U+E0BB), so the mob
name before the link was kept.

- Prefer the world name right after the cross world icon, or the cross
  world character typed as text
- Otherwise use the world name that appears last in the message

Close #661

Co-Authored-By: Claude Mythos 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
6ae42a0: Merge pull request #814 from SlashNephy/fix/faloop-login-failure

fix(FaloopIntegration): report rejected logins instead of retrying
7900863: fix(FaloopIntegration): report rejected logins instead of retrying

Faloop responds to a login with wrong credentials with 400 and
{"success":false,"msg":"Incorrect username or password."}. The client
threw on it, so nothing was shown in chat, and the connection loop
treated it as a transient error and kept retrying.

- Read the 400 response as a rejected login instead of throwing
- Print the reason to chat and stop retrying

Close #742

fix(FaloopIntegration): reconnect with a new client after disconnection
47500d7: fix(FaloopIntegration): log the whole spawn_location payload

Passing the nullable ZonePoiId alone as the params argument of the log
call made it a null array when the value was null (CS8604). Log the
whole payload instead, as the spawn case does.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Mythos 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
3cf9a9e: fix(FaloopIntegration): reconnect with a new client after disconnection

After "transport close", SocketIOClient's own reconnection kept the
engine.io session alive (pings continued) but the plugin never received
mob reports again until it was disabled and enabled.

Handle reconnection in the plugin instead, mirroring what re-enabling
the plugin does:

- Disable SocketIOClient's reconnection
- Run a connection loop that logs in again and connects with a new
  Socket.IO client on every disconnection, with exponential backoff
  from 5 seconds up to 5 minutes
- Time out a connection attempt that the server never accepts, since
  ConnectAsync only times out at the transport level
- Stop retrying when the credentials are rejected
- Ignore events from clients that have already been replaced

Refs #687

rawManifest.Name: Divination.AetheryteLinkInChat
rawManifest.Punchline: Quick teleport for mob hunts and treasure hunts!
rawManifest.Description: Display a teleport link to the nearest aetherite for the map link from the in-game chat. Type /alic to configure the plugin.
rawManifest.Changelog:
e8f691d: Merge pull request #816 from SlashNephy/feat/alic-hunt-journeys

feat(AetheryteLinkInChat): prefer Faloop's starting points for hunt spawn points
74b4951: feat(AetheryteLinkInChat): add exits missing from the game's map markers

The game's map markers do not describe the exit from Yanxia to the
Doman Enclave (The One River): the marker in Yanxia points to the
obsolete map 437, and the current map 463 has no marker back to Yanxia.
So routes through the Doman Enclave were never considered, which is the
Yanxia example in #656.

- Add MapConnections for such exits, starting with Yanxia <-> the Doman
  Enclave. Comparing Faloop's boundary starting points with the game's
  map markers found no other missing exit
- Consider them in the route calculation as ConnectionTeleportPath,
  without counting the distance inside the connected map, as where the
  exit leads to is not known
- Show them like zone boundaries, and stop the Lifestream teleport there

Refs #656

Co-Authored-By: Claude Mythos 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
a3c0a1f: feat(AetheryteLinkInChat): prefer Faloop's starting points for hunt spawn points

Straight-line distance on the map ignores terrain, height and walls, so
the nearest aetheryte is often not the best one to start from.

Faloop's zone data has the spawn points of hunt marks, each with a
journeyPoiId that points to the aetheryte or zone boundary to start
from. Embed them (generated by Scripts/generate_hunt_journeys.py) and,
when a map link is at a known spawn point, only consider the routes that
enter the map at its starting point. Otherwise, fall back to the
straight-line distance as before.

Refs #656

Co-Authored-By: Claude Mythos 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
97ddbb9: Merge pull request #815 from SlashNephy/fix/alic-detect-world

fix(AetheryteLinkInChat): prefer the world name after the cross world icon
e5d9e91: fix(AetheryteLinkInChat): prefer the world name after the cross world icon

DetectWorld picked the first public world in World sheet order whose
name appeared anywhere in the message. Mob names such as Odin and
Behemoth are also world names, so "Odin <map link> <CrossWorld>Cerberus"
resolved to Odin (row 66) instead of Cerberus (row 80), while
"Odin ... Omega" happened to work because Omega is row 39. The map link
trimming only removes text from the link marker (U+E0BB), so the mob
name before the link was kept.

- Prefer the world name right after the cross world icon, or the cross
  world character typed as text
- Otherwise use the world name that appears last in the message

Close #661

Co-Authored-By: Claude Mythos 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
6ae42a0: Merge pull request #814 from SlashNephy/fix/faloop-login-failure

fix(FaloopIntegration): report rejected logins instead of retrying
7900863: fix(FaloopIntegration): report rejected logins instead of retrying

Faloop responds to a login with wrong credentials with 400 and
{"success":false,"msg":"Incorrect username or password."}. The client
threw on it, so nothing was shown in chat, and the connection loop
treated it as a transient error and kept retrying.

- Read the 400 response as a rejected login instead of throwing
- Print the reason to chat and stop retrying

Close #742

d2ea413: feat: use a divination-deploy App token instead of DEPLOY_GITHUB_TOKEN (#799)

reusable-deploy-plugin.yml checks out the distribution repository, opens
a pull request there and merges it. Mint a GitHub App installation token
scoped to that repository instead of using a bot PAT.

Drop the Authorization header when fetching commits.json. This
repository is public so the request needs no authentication, and
expanding a token on the command line exposes it through the process
list.

Reference the reusable workflow by local path. Pinning it by SHA means a
change here does not take effect until every caller is updated, which
would leave a broken intermediate state whenever a secret is renamed.

Drop the explicit create-pull-request author: it defaults to
github.actor, which attributes the deployment to whoever triggered it.

3cf9a9e: fix(FaloopIntegration): reconnect with a new client after disconnection

After "transport close", SocketIOClient's own reconnection kept the
engine.io session alive (pings continued) but the plugin never received
mob reports again until it was disabled and enabled.

Handle reconnection in the plugin instead, mirroring what re-enabling
the plugin does:

- Disable SocketIOClient's reconnection
- Run a connection loop that logs in again and connects with a new
  Socket.IO client on every disconnection, with exponential backoff
  from 5 seconds up to 5 minutes
- Time out a connection attempt that the server never accepts, since
  ConnectAsync only times out at the transport level
- Stop retrying when the credentials are rejected
- Ignore events from clients that have already been replaced

d2ea413: feat: use a divination-deploy App token instead of DEPLOY_GITHUB_TOKEN (#799)

reusable-deploy-plugin.yml checks out the distribution repository, opens
a pull request there and merges it. Mint a GitHub App installation token
scoped to that repository instead of using a bot PAT.

Drop the Authorization header when fetching commits.json. This
repository is public so the request needs no authentication, and
expanding a token on the command line exposes it through the process
list.

Reference the reusable workflow by local path. Pinning it by SHA means a
change here does not take effect until every caller is updated, which
would leave a broken intermediate state whenever a secret is renamed.

Drop the explicit create-pull-request author: it defaults to
github.actor, which attributes the deployment to whoever triggered it.

plugins.author: Legends of the Game
plugins.name: Tales of Milestones
plugins.punchline: Remember every step, Warriors of Light.
plugins.description: Quest progression and pacing — a reflective notebook for your story journey, not a scoreboard.
plugins.changelog:
Tales of Milestones:
- Eat buttons on the Bonuses tab. Each meal in your inventory has an Eat button. One click eats one meal. The button is not available when the game refuses the meal.
- Eat button in /tm food. The food window has the same button for a meal that is in your inventory.
- /tm eat. `/tm eat dps`, `tank`, `healer`, `battle`, `craft`, `gather` or `all` eats your meal of that kind when you hold only one such meal. When you hold more than one, the Bonuses tab opens and you select the meal.
- Playtime in the export. The export adds the time that the plugin recorded after your last `/playtime` reply, so the playtime is current at the time of the export. The plugin does not run `/playtime`.
- Armor, GARO and more weapons in the export. "Copy collections" and "Copy everything" now include relic armor, GARO gear, and the Figmental, Exquisite and Deep Dungeon weapons.
- The native windows use less processor time. The at-a-glance window and the tabs of the main window now update one time each second, not on each frame. In a test, the at-a-glance window changed from about 1.2 ms to about 0.08 ms for each frame.
- Fix: the plugin no longer writes its settings file every 5 seconds while Cosmic Exploration data is loaded. It writes the file only when a tool's progress changes.
- Fix: the job list on the Progression tab no longer scrolls past its end.
- KamiToolKit is updated to its current version.
Adventurer's Ledger (Pandora Lunar):
- New layout. Next Steps is the first screen. It shows 5 cards for what to do next, and "Show 5 more" shows 10. Daily, Weekly and Seasonal rows are below it in the rail. The header shows the area title, the age of your data and 4 clocks.
- Challenge Log. Each Challenge Log entry has its own row, with links and typed counts. Suggested and Completed groups are included.
- Routine sub-checks. A routine can have its own boxes: one for each roulette, a Tank You pick, 12 allied society boxes and Grand Company chips. "Edit routines" changes the rows.
- Relics by job. The Relics area has a By job view and line cards with progress bars. To fill the Armor and GARO frames, update Tales of Milestones to this version and import a new export.
- Societies, currents and collections. Societies show unlock lines and rank bars. Aether currents are listed by zone. Collections are grouped by availability, with Online Store links.
- Settings area. Character, display, and backup and import settings are in one area. The Ledger holds up to 8 characters, and times can show in UTC or local time.
- Themes. The three themes are Lunar night, Crystarium and Light. Expansion tags use the colours of the Lodestone patch notes.
- Jobs meter. The rail has a Jobs meter that adds your combat, crafting and gathering levels, out of 3,330.
- Fix: after an import, the relic row in the list of changes counts relic items. Before, a stage upgrade showed no change, for example "9 to 9".

plugins.author: Ice
plugins.name: Gather & Chill
plugins.punchline: The gathering companion that we all needed.
plugins.description: A gathering plugin that will help you with your gathering needs. Between gathering items for you, or self applying buffs to make the task of gathering monotonous.
plugins.changelog:
- Cordials now have a node type restriction allowance
	- You can set if you want to (or not) used them for ephemeral, legendary, and normal nodes
- Collectables got a little bit of a logic overall
	- Short end, less strict and less following the TC guide... this might backfire on me, but allows for being a bit more reserved in gp usage. Will probably still fine tweak this as time goes on
- Collectables also have a setting to set which goal you would like to go for (high/mid/low)
- General gatherables have profiles that can be assigned with rules
	- The baseline is still there, if you don't feel like fucking with it, you don't have to
	- Allows for setting a minimum maximum integrity to allow for specific buffs to be used
	- I haven't tested this *-extensively-*, but for ya'll who want to nit pick which buffs you wanna use, it's there now
- Added a calculator for gatherable as well, that way you can tell what you're roughly going to gather based on what you have enabled for that profile
- Gathering also has a replay built into it, it'll track
	- What you gathered at a node
	- What buffs it used
	- How many items you got
	- This is mainly so I can actually tell what's being used on gathering nodes, and why certain things aren't. 
- Maps have been told they are *-in fact-* hidden items (they weren't in the sheets, so now... well now they are)

plugins.author: nxships
plugins.name: PlayerNexusTracker
plugins.punchline: Track every adventurer you meet in Eorzea.
plugins.description:
Track players you meet in FFXIV — who they are, when you ran into them, how their characters change over time. A focused social tracker built on the NexusKit framework.

Per-player detail view with Summary, Equipment, Class/Jobs, Achievements, Free Company, Encounters, History and Notes tabs. Optional enrichment from Lodestone (gear, FC link, achievement progress) and FFXIVCollect (mounts, minions, full achievement catalog). Live throttled refresh queue keeps external data fresh without hammering either service.

Configurable chat and toast notifications when players you've seen before change — rename, server transfer, Free Company join/leave/switch, achievement growth, refresh failures. Per-event filtering and history grouping so the chat doesn't drown you.

Powerful player-filter language with live preview to slice your list however you want; encounter history scoped per duty and content type; optional bridges to other Dalamud plugins (Lifestream world-travel, more to come).

Local-first: all data lives in a single SQLite file under your XIVLauncher config. Automated weekly maintenance keeps it tidy. English and German localization.
plugins.changelog:

* fix: guard detail header table setup by @nxships in https://github.com/NexusFFXIV/PlayerNexusTracker/pull/65

plugins.author: DhogGPT
plugins.name: Deep Ducking
plugins.punchline: Deep Ducking public host and authenticated module access.
plugins.description:
The Deep Ducking public host provides the introduction, community links and authenticated loading of separately supplied DDuck modules. /deepducking and /dduck open the introduction when no module is loaded.

Full module required for all commands below except opening the host window.

Commands (use /deepducking; /dduck is an alias):
/deepducking [toggle main window]
/dduck [alias for /deepducking; accepts all commands below]
/deepducking mini [toggle Mini]
/deepducking settings [open Settings]
/deepducking config [open Settings]
/deepducking debug [reveal and open Advanced for this plugin load]
/deepducking help [open command help]
/deepducking start [floor] [start or continue selected save; optional fresh-run floor]
/deepducking party-start [floor] [alias for start]
/deepducking party [select fixed-party POTD while idle]
/deepducking adopt [bind eligible already-entered party dungeon]
/deepducking hold [pause local output; retain run for Resume]
/deepducking resume [resume retained local run after readiness checks]
/deepducking nextstop [exit after next boss]
/deepducking ns [exit after next boss]
/deepducking stop [FULL STOP; persist local lock across reloads; stay in duty]
/deepducking reset-stop [clear eligible FULL STOP after cleanup; do not start]
/deepducking status [print local status]
/deepducking inspect [record read-only client and native observations]
/deepducking saves [open Saves]
/deepducking saves info <dungeon> [inspect native saves]
/deepducking saves delete <dungeon> <1|2> [delete selected save after native checks; no extra confirmation]
/deepducking saves dof <dungeon> <1|2> <on|off> [set future-failure deletion preference; no deletion now]
/deepducking saves cancel [cancel pending save or Start preparation; completed actions remain]

Dungeon arguments: potd, hoh, eo, pt. [floor] is optional; <...> is required. Choose one value for 1|2 or on|off; omit brackets when typing. Start can replace stopped state; Resume can release an eligible retained in-dungeon run. nextstop and ns retain the save and keep Mini open until return is observed; repeat to confirm the same request. Use the existing boss-break button to cancel.

If DailyDuty is installed, /dd is unavailable for Deep Ducking; use /deepducking. An alias owned by another plugin is preserved.

rawManifest.Description: Early beta. Helper for the ARR Zodiac relic line that works next to ZodiacBuddy Reborn. Infuses the materia you hold into your Sphere Scrolls, hands your relics to Jalzahn for each upgrade, and farms Light and Mahatmas through AutoDuty, with Remon attaching the next Mahatma. Optional: AutoDuty for the farms, vnavmesh for walking to the NPCs, Lifestream for inn rooms.
rawManifest.TestingChangelog:
0.8.30, changes since 0.8.0:
- Gear repair, on by default: between targets of the books, the Atma farm and between autopilot steps, a worn piece at or below 30 % (set in the main tab) gets repaired. Self repair with Dark Matter goes first. Anything still worn after that goes to Alistair, the mender in Limsa Lominsa Lower Decks. If a repair fails, the run goes on and tries again 30 minutes later.
- Books: the 4 second take-off check now starts once vnavmesh has found the route. Long flights, such as across Coerthas, took 4 seconds to plan, so the check cancelled the route and the character rode on the ground instead.
- Messages about missing gear or materia no longer tell Free Trial accounts to buy them. They say the market board is not available and to craft the gear or extract the materia. This covers A Relic Reborn's weapon, the meld step, the HQ Zodiac materials and the Novus materia.
- The autopilot stops before A Relic Reborn when you lack the weapon Gerolt asks for (Barbarian's Bardiche for Bravura, and so on) with its 2 materia melded and cannot buy it. The popup names the weapon and why it was not bought. Before, WigglyQuest talked to Gerolt in a loop.
- On a Free Trial account the "Buy from market board" box shows unticked and cannot be changed. Your saved choice stays for other accounts.
- On a Free Trial account the materia row of the main tab says "by hand (Free Trial)" instead of "autopilot", since nothing is bought on the market board there.
- Report a problem now writes the .log file and copies your text, then gives two buttons: one opens this plugin's thread on our Discord, the other is the server invite for people who are not members yet, since the thread link does not open for them.
- Capture leves also take an armour piece off when one hit removes more than 30 % of a target's HP, before it can die. A level 70 summoner took a winter nix from 100 % to 42 % with one auto-attack.
- Capture leves fight the other spawns that attack you, like the Ragged Hippogryph, with the normal AI and rotation instead of the auto-attack alone, then turn them off again for the targets.
- Report a problem now opens our Discord instead of a GitHub issue. Send the .log file to Kyuuso by DM or post it in the plugin's thread in #plugins. The text you typed is copied to the clipboard so you can paste it with the file.
- Capture leves keep your armour on at first. Each target that dies before the /soothe takes one more piece off for that job and level, body and legs first, and the count is saved. A level 100 character may lose a few targets the first time while it learns.
- Free Trial accounts skip every market board purchase and the main tab says so, since the game does not let them use the market board.
- Capture leves no longer switch to normal combat after riding to the next target. Before, the AI came back on and attacked a winter nix that was already pacified.
- Capture leves start the auto-attack with the hotbar's Auto-attack command. The old call got "Cannot execute at this time." with the weak weapon on, so the targets were never hit.
- Capture leves send the chocobo away and turn off the BossMod AI, its preset and Rotation Solver, even when you had them on. Only the auto-attack hits the targets, so a skill or the chocobo no longer kills one before the /soothe.
- Capture leves in the books no longer swap between the weak weapon and the Atma weapon every second. The Atma weapon goes back on after the targets are soothed, before the turn-in.
- The books summon the chocobo companion with Gysahl Greens for their enemies and FATEs, as the Atma farm already did. Leves stay without it, so it cannot kill a capture target.
- Escort leves (Someone's in the Doghouse): when the escort falls more than 20 yalms behind, the character walks back to it. It used to stay up to 30 yalms ahead, stuck on a rock, sending /beckon that the game answered with "Too far away".
- Dungeon unlocks that need another dungeon cleared first (Halatali before Halatali (Hard)) wait until you are out of it. The clear used to count when the last boss died, so the talk to Hugubert started inside Halatali, three teleports failed, and the book stopped on Mumuepo the Beholden.
- Trips to an NPC wait up to 3 minutes for a duty or cutscene to end before teleporting.
- Lure leves (Don't Forget to Cry): a prime location that lures nothing within 8 seconds is skipped. It used the lure on the same wrong spot every 5 seconds.
- New "Dungeon coffers" option in the Debug tab for book, Braves and unlock dungeons: boss coffers only (default), every coffer, no coffers, or your own DAD/AutoDuty loot settings.
- FATE combat after a dungeon: AutoDuty/DAD turn the BossMod AI off and clear its autorotation preset. /vbmai on is now sent again after each zone change, and without Rotation Solver your last preset (or VBM Default) is set for the fight and cleared after it.
- Atma FATEs inside the U'Ghamaro Mines are done on the ground; the mount stays off past the entrance.
- Jalzahn's furnace is used from (445.9, -66.3), where it worked by hand. When WigglyQuest hovers at Gerolt or the furnace, it lands and walks in.
- The "Do you really want to trade a high-quality item?" prompt is answered on quests Zodiac Helper started.
- Main tab: materia and the class weapon read "autopilot" when market buying is on.
Still to test before 1.0: party sharing between two clients, and a second relic on the same character.

rawManifest.Description:
The one-stop shop to your cosmic exploration needs! This plugin is meant to be a collective source of being able to grind out your gather and crafter relics, while also being able to help grind out the score to 500k on each class for that sleek black mech that you want ~.

- Has the ability to re-roll missions for you until you get the desired one that you want to farm
- Crafters can be fully automated with support of artisan. 
- Fisher can also be fully automated with the support of AutoHook and Navmesh
- Botanist/Miner only need Navmesh, thanks to having gathering built in directly to the plugin <3. 
- Setup what items you want to buy from the shop for cosmocredits, or spend your planetary tokens on the cosmowheel of fortune!
rawManifest.Changelog: - Cosmic will only enable autohook if it needs to start a fishing mission, will not try and disable it.

plugins.author: The Combat Reborn Team
plugins.name: Rotation Solver Reborn
plugins.punchline: Analyses combat information every frame and finds the best action.
plugins.description:
Analyses combat information every frame and finds the best action.

This means almost all the information available in one frame in combat, including the status of all players in the party, the status of any hostile targets, skill cooldowns, the MP and HP of characters, the location of characters, casting status of the hostile target, combo, combat duration, player level, etc.
Then, it will highlight the best action on the hot bar, or help you to click on it.
It is designed for `general combat`, not for savage or ultimate. Use it carefully.

rawManifest.TestingChangelog:
[Pet Nicknames 3.0.0.0]

Helloooo helloooooo!
This is a majour rewrite of Pet Nicknames that has been ongoing for the last year.
Sorry this took so long.

- Added support for Beast Master naming.
- Added an ephemeral chat replace (on by default) where chat messages will update retroactively and disappear when the plugin turns off.
- Massive stability improvements, naming is now much more consistant, and lots of UI elements will update themselves.

plugins.author: Critical_Impact
plugins.name: Allagan Tools
plugins.punchline: Get organized in FFXIV, easily locate/show where to sort items, plan your crafting, and search for mobs, duties, airships, and submarines!
plugins.description:
Allagan Tool's primary purpose is to keep track of items across your characters/retainers/free company. With it's filter system you'll never lose track of items or not know where they should be sorted.

While this is it's primary purpose, it has quite an exhaustive list of other features including:
	- Craft planning
	- Market board integration
	- Item highlighting in inventories when searching/sorting and picking ingredients for crafts
	- Item window that includes vendor and source information among other things
	- Duty/mob/airship/submarine windows that are fully searchable
	- A filtering system that lets you setup complex searches for specific items 
	- Tooltip integration that'll let you see where the items are on hover
plugins.changelog:
### Added
- Added a Locations column to the Mobs compendium, click a flag to link the spawn location in chat or right click it to teleport
- Added a "Hunt Mark?" column to the Mobs compendium
- When the Mobs compendium is grouped by zone, a Current Zone menu can open the tab for the zone you are in, or follow you as you change zones
### Fixed
- Map links printed to chat from the compendium were showing the wrong name

plugins.author: Blooym
plugins.name: GoodFriend
plugins.punchline: Improvements to the in-game friend system, including login and logout notifications for your friends, and more.
plugins.description:
Key Features:
- Receive notifications when friends using GoodFriend log in or out.
- Chat messages show how many of your friends are online when you log in.

Developer's Note on Using This Plugin After Patch 7.0:
As of Patch 7.0, some of the data that GoodFriend uses to identify players during login/logout events is now visible to anyone nearby your character in-game (not just your friends or party members). GoodFriend itself will still only show notifications for people you've added to your in-game friends list - however, please use this plugin only if you're comfortable with your login/logout activity being theoretically visible to nearby players (note: GoodFriend never sends data for users who don't have the plugin installed).

If you ever want to stop sending login/logout events, simply disable or uninstall the plugin. The server does not store any data about you.

For added privacy, you can now set a 'group key' in the plugin settings. This allows events to be shared only with people using the same key (for example, everyone in your raid group). When a group key is active, your events are never visible to anyone outside your group no matter what.

rawManifest.TestingChangelog:
_Hey all, your average plugin developer rewriting their entire plugin every few months here with some exciting news.. I've rewritten GoodFriend from scratch!_

**:warning: Please note that upon updating to the new version, your configuration will be completely wiped as it is no longer compatible. You will also be unable to send events or receive events with your friends using the older version.**

## What's changed?

A new modular design has been used when rewriting so that new functionality can be added in the future with less development work. All the existing functionality of the plugin has been re-implemented already so you shouldn't notice anything missing.

Thanks to this new design, you can now toggle each module on/off independently so that you only have the functionality that you actually want to have.

The interface has also been completely redesigned to clearly show each module as well as plugin-wide configuration options. At the very least, I think it looks better (I'm not a UI/UX designer)

### New Modules

- Login State Notifications: Get notified when other people using GoodFriend on your in-game friends list log in or log out with customizable filtering to only catch the notifications you want to see. (As this is the old functionality of the plugin this module has been enabled by default)

- World Change Notifications: Get notified when other people using GoodFriend on your in-game friends list change worlds using the world visit system while logged in with filtering to only see when people visit your own world (Disabled by default, still being improved as of now)

### Bug Fixes

- Too many to list here, but most of the fixes are related to connectivity problems.

Let me know what you think in either the `#plugin-testing` channel or the GoodFriend plugin thread! Thanks in advance to the plugin reviewers that have to review this as well.

[Happy pride month btw](https://pbs.twimg.com/media/FxqJcqvXgAE65GU?format=jpg&name=large)

plugins.name: Magitek Stratagem
plugins.punchline: Tobii and Eyeware Eye and Opentrack tracker support for FFXIV
plugins.description: Developed by the ingenious Garlean engineer Tobiias, this revolutionary Magitek device empowers adventurers by enabling hands-free enemy targeting with unparalleled precision.
plugins.changelog:
# Version 1.4.0

A complete visual overhaul, plus market value estimates.

- Every window redesigned around one theme: dark glass panels, brass rules and crystal-blue highlights.
- Removed the Compact and Neon layouts. Classic is now the only view and received all of the design work.
- Settings moved from stacked collapsing headers to a sectioned window with a navigation rail.
- New: estimated market value of everything you loot, priced for your home world via Universalis. The running total is independent of how many items the list keeps and has its own reset button. Can be turned off in the settings.
- Statistics charts are now properly drawn, with hover tooltips, in place of the old text bars.
- Statistics are computed off the draw thread; large histories no longer freeze the game when the window opens.
- Fixed an O(n^2) pass over the whole history that stalled the game for seconds on large collections.
- The loot list highlights new drops, marks rarity on every row and sizes its columns to the content.
- The roll window is now a set of rarity-tinted cards with a countdown ring and a crown on the winner.
- New: release notes appear once after each update, and from Settings - About.
- The overlay now waits until your character has finished logging in before it appears.
- Loot parsing recognises "sprig of".
- Fixed a drawing error being able to leave ImGui's window stack unbalanced.

rawManifest.TestingChangelog:
It's been a while! There's way too much to put into a single changelog, since this was basically a *total* rewrite of XIVDeck. In no particular order:

- A revamped communication system means communication between the Stream Deck and the game is *much* faster.
    - Windows users get to use Named Pipes for communication, while Linux and macOS users get Unix Domain Sockets.
    - The websocket server is still available (and will remain so), but is no longer preferred for use.
- The Stream Deck Plugin now can render hotbar slots far more faithfully to the game.
    - Sub-icons, costs, ***and cooldowns*** are now rendered on buttons that support them!
    - The in-game hotbar watcher will now only track visible hotbar slots, improving overall performance.
- The Stream Deck plugin has been ported to NodeJS, which should provide some performance boosts as well.
- New plugin internals means certain features should be much easier to add in the future.
- Linux is now finally officially supported via [OpenDeck](https://github.com/nekename/OpenDeck)!
- A new process detection engine should detect FFXIV much more reliably now across all operating systems.
- Multiboxing is now properly supported, with your Stream Deck buttons following your last-focused game client. 
  - The ability to "pin" a button to use a specific game client will be coming in a future update.
- **[DEPRECATION]** While never officially supported, control of XIVDeck over the network is no longer available. This may be readded in a later update, but for now it's just not possible.

It's very important to note that this is a pre-release change, and this new version of XIVDeck is considered beta. If you need things to work, I strongly suggest you wait for 0.5.1 or later. **Since the XIVDeck protocol has been remade, old clients will not be able to connect.** 

## Testing Notes

It's been a _really_ long time since I last had testing notes. So:

* Test everything! Major rewrites mean that things have changed, and there's plenty of room for bugs.
* Let me know if your buttons lose configuration or don't work quite right after the update. Please bring logs for your reports.
* I'm also particularly interested in performance, and if everything still feels better to navigate.

Full release notes and downloads are available [on the plugin GitHub](https://github.com/KazWolfe/XIVDeck/releases/tag/v0.5.0).

plugins.author: Haplo064, maintained by Franz
plugins.name: WOLdo
plugins.punchline: Making it easier to know where you are.
plugins.description: Movable text overlay of the current location name. Please consider migrationg to WhereAmIAgain, which is actively maintained and has more features.
plugins.changelog:
# Version 1.4.0

A complete visual overhaul, plus market value estimates.

- Every window redesigned around one theme: dark glass panels, brass rules and crystal-blue highlights.
- Removed the Compact and Neon layouts. Classic is now the only view and received all of the design work.
- Settings moved from stacked collapsing headers to a sectioned window with a navigation rail.
- New: estimated market value of everything you loot, priced for your home world via Universalis. The running total is independent of how many items the list keeps and has its own reset button. Can be turned off in the settings.
- Statistics charts are now properly drawn, with hover tooltips, in place of the old text bars.
- Statistics are computed off the draw thread; large histories no longer freeze the game when the window opens.
- Fixed an O(n^2) pass over the whole history that stalled the game for seconds on large collections.
- The loot list highlights new drops, marks rarity on every row and sizes its columns to the content.
- The roll window is now a set of rarity-tinted cards with a countdown ring and a crown on the winner.
- New: release notes appear once after each update, and from Settings - About.
- The overlay now waits until your character has finished logging in before it appears.
- Loot parsing recognises "sprig of".
- Fixed a drawing error being able to leave ImGui's window stack unbalanced.

plugins.author: darkarchon
plugins.name: XIVJitterFix
plugins.punchline: Fixes SquareEnix' botched antialiasing implementation
plugins.description:
With the release of 7.0 SquareEnix has implemented several temporal antialiasing solutions. However they all have a severe bug that affects image quality significantly.
This plugin will restore using jitter when talking to NPCs or in cutscenes and gpose. Jitter (not noticeable micromovements of the camera) is necessary for temporal antialiasing solutions (DLSS, DLAA, TSCMAA+jitter) to work properly.
For some reason, SquareEnix decided we don't need jitter during the time where the game benefits from using it the most.

- Fix NPC dialogue matching issue for alphabetic languages (English, French, German, etc.).

- Tooltip layout is computed more accurately for better alignment/less chance to break.
- Fix the issue where the config window still pops up when the NPC dialogue feature is disabled.

plugins.author: tesu
plugins.name: Penny Pincher
plugins.punchline: Copies 1 below the cheapest offer to your clipboard when you check marketboard prices
plugins.description:
Plugin for simplifying "pennying" (undercutting current lowest offer by 1).

The usual workflow for this is the following:
1. Open up the adjust price menu for the item you're undercutting
2. Click on the compare prices menu to view the current listings
3. Take a mental note of what the current lowest offer is
4. Subtract one from it
5. Close the current listings window
6. Update your item's price with the number you noted
7. Confirm your new price

This plugin eliminates the mental notekeeping steps in the middle by automatically copying the number you want onto your clipboard when you open the current listings window.  

Therefore, your new workflow becomes this:
1. Open up the adjust price menu for the item you're undercutting
2. Click on the compare prices menu to view the current listings
3. Close the current listings window
4. Paste the undercut value in
5. Confirm your new price

This both speeds up the process and reduces room for error from typos.
plugins.changelog: API 15

plugins.name: Party List Extras
plugins.punchline: Parses Buffs to help understand what your party is doing.
plugins.description: Adds Text and Icons next to the party list describing active buffs. Still missing some jobs - See github for progress. Please note the overlay goes to the left of your party list.
plugins.changelog:
First stable release.

Things To Do In Eorzea is more than just a simple to-do-list. It's one that automatically monitors what you need to collect, what duties you need to clear, FATEs and more! You can either set it up to track items you need or have it track your clears. Think that's not enough? You can even set yourself up some ridiculous tasks for yourself like doing MINE Bahamut or a whole Savage round without dying/wiping to just simply forcing yourself to play a specific job, or speedrun. There are always things to do in Eorzea. Just get creative!

Unlike other to-do plugins, Things To Do In Eorzea:
1. Auto-tracks your completed dungeons, trials and raids.
2. Auto-tracks your completed FATEs by region, a specific FATE or any FATE in general.
3. Auto-tracks the items in your inventory, making sure you have what you needed to get.
4. Make self-imposed challenges like doing Minstrel's Ballads on MINE difficulty, speedrun a Dungeon, one-shot/no kill, and more.
5. Read objectives in your native language*

   > Some languages may be partially broken in translation.

And you still have your sticky note for whenever you need it.

plugins.author: Infi, Caitlyn
plugins.name: Death Roll Helper
plugins.punchline: Plugin to help with a number of dice games. Also offers games like Tic-Tac-Toe, Minesweeper and Bahamood.
plugins.description:
## Modes
### Venue:
- Concise display of all concurrent players in a list-based format
- Supports multiple sorting types (min, max, nearest to)
- Highlight numbers based on regex matching

### DeathRoll:
- Supports multiple players
- Automatic checks to prevent number skipping

### Tournament (1v1 DeathRoll):
- Automatic bracket generation with byes to fill uneven
- Forfeit functionality if a player needs to leave

### Blackjack:
- Automatic reward calculation based on common rules
- Simplistic, or visual view of cards in play
- Automatic or manual player-based draw for cards

### Extra Features:
- Block or prevent players from partaking in any game
- Accept only /random or /dice commands

## Games
### Tic-Tac-Toe
- Play against your friends, or AI
- Easy, Medium, Hard
- 3x3, 4x4, 5x5

### Minesweeper
- Easy, Medium, Hard
- 8x8, 9x9, 16x16, 18x30
- Custom Games (planned)

More features are planned, following user feedback.
plugins.changelog:
Fixed `/dice` roll detection

Thanks to Zunetrix on Discord for submitting and sending over an updated sig

plugins.name: DeviceChangeFix
plugins.punchline: Stops controller input from freezing randomly.
plugins.description:
Stops controller input from freezing randomly by ensuring FFXIV only polls for controllers when one is actually connected or disconnected. Doesn't require any configuration.

Original plugin by PGGB, icon from Mutant Standard.
plugins.changelog:
- Volume control now also covers set-to-N lines, plus performance, mount BGM, and own/party/others sound effects
- New System option: show configuration change messages (`Changes saved.`, lost, discarded). Off by default
- Changing gearsets no longer hides ARR relic quest warnings that say you must be equipped with a specific weapon
- `The fish gets away…` follows the existing lose-bait option
- Settings search matches LogMessage IDs exactly, so short numbers don't hit unrelated options
- Custom filter and highlight channel lists stay open when the label updates
- Custom Allow filters can override condensed login/world-travel announcements

plugins.author: perchbird
plugins.name: PrefPro
plugins.punchline: Changes in-game dialogue to reference your desired gender and name.
plugins.description:
Your character is personal, so you should be able to have NPCs refer to them
the way that you want. With PrefPro, you can control which text option
will appear when an NPC uses dialogue meant for a specific in-game gender.
This allows you to use a female player model and be referred to as male, and
vice versa. In addition, there are a few name customization options - if you
want to only be referred to by your last name, so be it.
Note: This plugin currently will not swap voiced cutscene dialogue.
plugins.changelog: - **Fixed:** A crash due to changes to the Master's Bestiary in Patch 7.58.

plugins.author: Caraxi
plugins.name: Macro Chain
plugins.punchline: Run multiple macros one after the other.
plugins.description:
Allows for a macro to continue onto the next macro by using '/nextmacro' on the last line of a macro.
Adding '/nextmacro' on the last line of Macro #01 will automatically execute Macro #02
Adding '/nextmacro down' on the last line of Macro #01 will automatically execute Macro #11
Also allows executing any macro from chat using '/runmacro' but this command cannot be used while macros are running.

plugins.author: Una
plugins.name: Umbra XIV
plugins.punchline: Adds fully customizable toolbars and 3D world markers to the game.
plugins.description: Consolidates common UI elements and actions into a single uniform interface in the form of a set of highly customizable toolbars.
plugins.changelog:
# Umbra 3.1.18

## Fixes & Improvements

- Adds setting "Use windows draw list" to Toolbar Settings. By enabling it, other plugins may draw on top of Umbra Toolbars. This adds support for plugins that manage window layers. e.g. Gaolbreak (By [Bloodsoul](https://github.com/Bloodsoul)).
- Adds setting to auto-hide Auxiliary Toolbars (By [Bloodsoul](https://github.com/Bloodsoul)).
- Adds placeholders for Free Company name and tag (By [Bloodsoul](https://github.com/Bloodsoul)).
- Enables Occult Survey Point Markers for North Horn (By [Bloodsoul](https://github.com/Bloodsoul)).
- Added support for Fortune Carrot markers in North Horn (By [GayPotatoEmma](https://github.com/GayPotatoEmma)).
- Added support for Pot Coffer markers in North Horn (By [GayPotatoEmma](https://github.com/GayPotatoEmma)).
- Overhauled the Phantom Jobs widget with new display options. Users who prefer the old layout can easily swap back to it in the Widget Settings (By [GayPotatoEmma](https://github.com/GayPotatoEmma)).
- Fixes Dynamic Menu placeholders not being updated (By [Bloodsoul](https://github.com/Bloodsoul)).
- Fixes possible Access Violation while accessing equipments (By [LTS-FFXIV](https://github.com/LTS-FFXIV)).
- Fixes 24h clock displaying another format depending on operating system settings (By [Bloodsoul](https://github.com/Bloodsoul)).
- Fixes 12h clock displaying leading zero (By [Bloodsoul](https://github.com/Bloodsoul)).
- Gearset Switcher does now also hide the prefix in the header when configured (By [Bloodsoul](https://github.com/Bloodsoul)).
- Weather Widget now displays time left for the current weather (By [Bloodsoul](https://github.com/Bloodsoul)).
- Fix Teleport Widget keeping old housing entries e.g. when world visiting (By [Bloodsoul](https://github.com/Bloodsoul)).

---

Join [Umbra's Discord server](https://discord.gg/xaEnsuAhmm) for the latest updates and information.
Visit the [website](https://una-xiv.github.io/umbra-docs/) for more information and guides on how to make the most out of Umbra.

plugins.author: Nadya, Kagekazu
plugins.name: Tidy Chat
plugins.punchline: Cut down FFXIV chat spam with per-message toggles and shorter system lines.
plugins.description:
Trim the messages FFXIV dumps into your chat log.

  - Master filters for System, Progress, Loot, Obtained, Crafting, and Gathering
  - Toggles for currencies, FC and retainer messages, level-ups, mount unlocks, orchestrion lines, deep dungeon pomanders, combat log categories, and more
  - Shorter rewrites for instance entry, commendations, Novice Network, and treasure dungeon text
  - Copies /say quest dialogue to your clipboard; can block emote spam from others
  - Player whitelist, chat history deduplication, per-tomestone hides, and debug logging
plugins.changelog:
- The ready check and countdown sounds no longer play twice (which made them very loud)
- Fewer messages hidden by mistake: filters now look at whole words, so a line isn't hidden just because part of a word looks similar
- Playing in Japanese, German or French? Most built-in filters now work in your language too
- Currency messages are now filtered correctly when you only get one (e.g. "You obtain 1 Wolf Mark")
- Fixed some German and French names (Ventures, Sacks of Nuts, Grand Company seals) so those messages filter properly

plugins.author: Xorus
plugins.name: EngageTimer
plugins.punchline: Complete combat countdown, pull timer and OBS overlay
plugins.description:
Finally, display all the numbers when starting a countdown!
Comes with an accurate pull timer that starts when you or any of your party members enter combat.

Features :
- Big countdown that displays all the numbers
- Customizable big-number textures (default, yellow, WoW style or custom files)
- Display combat time in the Server Info Bar, and/or a floating window
- OBS browser-source compatible page with countdown and current combat duration

Why the OBS thing ? I like having a big stylized stopwatch in my private recordings and that's about it.
See repository for more info.

Feel free so send me feedback, bugs and potential improvements! Check the about page in the plugin settings for more
info. Please report urgent feedback on GitHub or XIVLauncher Discord's support thread for this plugin.
plugins.changelog: - Update for API15

plugins.author: Populo
plugins.name: Retainer Sales
plugins.punchline: See retainer sales quicker
plugins.description: Quickly see which retainers have sold something while you were logged off.
plugins.changelog:
# Version 1.4.0

A complete visual overhaul, plus market value estimates.

- Every window redesigned around one theme: dark glass panels, brass rules and crystal-blue highlights.
- Removed the Compact and Neon layouts. Classic is now the only view and received all of the design work.
- Settings moved from stacked collapsing headers to a sectioned window with a navigation rail.
- New: estimated market value of everything you loot, priced for your home world via Universalis. The running total is independent of how many items the list keeps and has its own reset button. Can be turned off in the settings.
- Statistics charts are now properly drawn, with hover tooltips, in place of the old text bars.
- Statistics are computed off the draw thread; large histories no longer freeze the game when the window opens.
- Fixed an O(n^2) pass over the whole history that stalled the game for seconds on large collections.
- The loot list highlights new drops, marks rarity on every row and sizes its columns to the content.
- The roll window is now a set of rarity-tinted cards with a countdown ring and a crown on the winner.
- New: release notes appear once after each update, and from Settings - About.
- The overlay now waits until your character has finished logging in before it appears.
- Loot parsing recognises "sprig of".
- Fixed a drawing error being able to leave ImGui's window stack unbalanced.

- The overlay now waits until your character has finished logging in before it appears.
- Loot parsing recognises "sprig of".

plugins.author: smileyhead
plugins.name: Sticky Focus Target
plugins.punchline: Like /focustarget, but with no overrides.
plugins.description:
(PvE-only.) Adds the /stickyfocustarget command, which focuses your current
target, as long as you do not already have a focus target set.
  
Have you ever felt focusing was under-utilised? Wanted to use it without a
dedicated keybind? Do you not even know what focus targeting is?
You've come to the right place.
  
You can add this command to your Attack Nearest macro and ensure that the
first enemy you target will also become focused, and stay that way, until it dies.
With this, you can focus enemies without having to consciously press a keybind,
and ensure that, for instance, when a focused boss spawns an add and you target it,
the boss' focus will NOT get overriden.

This plugin does not change the behaviour of the stock /focustarget command,
and must be triggered either manually or by adding it to a macro.
Placeholders are supported.

- Added tha ability to cycle between ImGui and Native UI in Settings.

plugins.author: GitHixy
plugins.name: LootView
plugins.punchline: See every item you and your party pick up, as it drops.
plugins.description:
LootView is a live loot tracker for you and your party, with a permanent history and statistics behind it.

WHAT YOU GET

Works with every game language: English, Japanese, German and French.

- Live overlay listing every drop with its icon, rarity, quantity, who received it and how long ago.
- Estimated market value of your haul, priced for your home world through Universalis.
- Currency drawer beside the overlay with every currency you hold, its cap and the weekly tomestone limit.
- A banner on screen when another player commends you.
- Need/Greed panel that appears while rolls are open: time left on every item, each Need, Greed and Pass, who is still deciding, and the winner. Roll Need, Greed or Pass right from the panel, with the game's own loot window kept out of the way.
- Collectibles you already have (minions, mounts, orchestrion rolls, Triple Triad cards, emotes, hairstyles, portrait frames) are marked on their icon.
- Detailed item tooltips with item level, jobs, stats, bonuses, materia slots and market price.
- Loot tables for dungeons, trials and raids - the duty you are in, or any duty you search for.
- Searchable history you can filter by item name, rarity, zone, high quality and owner.
- Statistics: rarity breakdown, top zones, daily and hourly activity, play streaks and period-over-period comparisons.
- Duty tracker recording your runs, clear times, items per run and personal bests.
- Export to JSON or CSV whenever you want.

GETTING STARTED

Type /lv to open the tracker and /lv config for settings. You can also open it from the server info bar.
Right-click any item to try it on, look it up, copy its name or blacklist it.
Found a bug or have an idea? Settings > Diagnostics copies a report and opens a GitHub issue for you, or come and talk about it on Discord: https://discord.gg/9kjUjWDBkJ

PRIVACY

Your history is stored locally in your Dalamud configuration folder and is never uploaded. Market prices are looked up from universalis.app and loot tables from garlandtools.org; both requests send only an item or duty ID. Price lookups can be turned off in the settings.
plugins.changelog:
# Version 1.6.5

- Jar on its own: the loot jar can now stay on screen by itself, just the glass with no frame. Move it, resize it from its edges and lock it in place from Settings > General. It fades back while nothing is happening and comes forward when something drops in.
- The loot jar now holds exactly what the loot list shows: clearing the list pours it out, and drops that leave the list leave the jar too.
- Ticker: Ctrl+click a drop, or pick Dismiss from its right-click menu, to clear it early. A broom button next to the ticker's controls clears every drop at once.
