plugins.author: dajoey
plugins.name: LazyCrafter
plugins.punchline: What can I make right now, what's it worth, and what would it take to make the rest?
plugins.description: Catalogs every recipe you can craft, buckets them by how much effort the missing materials take, prices them with Universalis, and hands the missing-material work to Artisan / GBR / ARC / Lifestream.
plugins.changelog:
v0.1.7.11 (2026-11-14) [testing]
- The plugin windows have been rebuilt on the shared LalaUiKit: one consistent layout with themed section headers, unified spacing and colour accents. All settings and behaviour are unchanged, and existing configuration loads as-is.

v0.1.7.10 (2026-11-10) [testing]
- Rebuilt against the Dalamud 15.0.4.0 payload for game patch 7.58. No functional changes.

v0.1.7.9 (2026-10-17) [testing]
- **Market-price lookups no longer log warnings while they retry.** When Universalis is slow or busy it answers with a temporary "try again" status or takes longer than before; the price client already retries those on its own with a pause between tries - that is its designed behavior, not a fault, so those lines now go to the debug log. Only one warning is written when a batch gives up entirely after all retries, and stale cached prices are used meanwhile, exactly as before.
- **The price client now waits up to 60 seconds per request instead of 20.** Under load, Universalis sometimes finishes a large price query just after the old 20-second cutoff; the request was cancelled while the server was still working on it and the prices for that batch were refetched from scratch. The longer budget lets those queries land.
- Market-price log lines no longer paste a hundred item numbers into the log; a batch is described as its item count instead.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Full harness: 401/401 PASS (6 new).

v0.1.7.8 (2026-10-07) [testing]
- **Knightshopper no longer buys units that are sitting on a retainer.** The purchase target counted everything the catalog can see, but the fetch-from-retainer step runs after the purchase and brings those units in anyway - with 90 units on a retainer, none in the bags and 9 missing, the run bought 99 instead of 9. The target now counts what is physically in the bags, and the fetch tops the bags up to exactly what the cart needs; every currency routes on the same corrected target.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Full harness: 395/395 PASS (4 new).

v0.1.7.7 (2026-10-07) [testing]
- **Cart dispatches can hand vendor purchases to Knightshopper.** When a dispatch is missing materials that a vendor sells - gil vendors, and currency vendors priced in one currency Knightshopper supports - the run groups that list by currency and buys it through Knightshopper's purchase IPC at target inventory totals, before any shopping stop fires. The run prints each group, its currency and the estimated total cost before anything is spent. Market-board items are never routed, and one attempt per group means a refused purchase never retries; a repeat dispatch asks for the same target totals at most, so nothing is ever bought twice.
- If Knightshopper is missing, busy, refuses LazyCrafter, or has no unlocked vendor for an item, those items fall back to the usual shopping stops - flagged and named in chat exactly as before. Purchases also need LazyCrafter on Knightshopper's allowed-plugins IPC list, which is set in Knightshopper's own settings (IPC permissions); LazyCrafter never changes Knightshopper's settings. The new switch (on by default) is "Buy vendor items through Knightshopper during a dispatch" in the settings.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- With the switch off, or without Knightshopper installed, the run behaves exactly as before.
- Full harness: 391/391 PASS (16 new).

v0.1.7.6 (2026-10-03) [testing]
- **Quick controls for the Lazy Hub window.** The plugin now offers the catalog and price settings (recipes above the character's level, the undersupplied thresholds, the revenue basis, pricing at the home world only, the price refresh interval, the price-match message) and the cart-run hand-off switches (fetching materials from retainers, walking to a summoning bell or to vendors, preferring a currency shop) to Lazy Hub (`/lazy`) over Dalamud IPC, so they can be changed from one window next to the other lalalazy plugins. Each change does exactly what the matching setting in the plugin's own window does.
- The cart-run hand-off switches can only be changed while no cart run is active.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Without Lazy Hub installed the plugin behaves exactly as before.

- Full harness: 401/401 PASS (6 new).

v0.1.7.8 (2026-10-07) [testing]
- **Knightshopper no longer buys units that are sitting on a retainer.** The purchase target counted everything the catalog can see, but the fetch-from-retainer step runs after the purchase and brings those units in anyway - with 90 units on a retainer, none in the bags and 9 missing, the run bought 99 instead of 9. The target now counts what is physically in the bags, and the fetch tops the bags up to exactly what the cart needs; every currency routes on the same corrected target.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Full harness: 395/395 PASS (4 new).

v0.1.7.7 (2026-10-07) [testing]
- **Cart dispatches can hand vendor purchases to Knightshopper.** When a dispatch is missing materials that a vendor sells - gil vendors, and currency vendors priced in one currency Knightshopper supports - the run groups that list by currency and buys it through Knightshopper's purchase IPC at target inventory totals, before any shopping stop fires. The run prints each group, its currency and the estimated total cost before anything is spent. Market-board items are never routed, and one attempt per group means a refused purchase never retries; a repeat dispatch asks for the same target totals at most, so nothing is ever bought twice.
- If Knightshopper is missing, busy, refuses LazyCrafter, or has no unlocked vendor for an item, those items fall back to the usual shopping stops - flagged and named in chat exactly as before. Purchases also need LazyCrafter on Knightshopper's allowed-plugins IPC list, which is set in Knightshopper's own settings (IPC permissions); LazyCrafter never changes Knightshopper's settings. The new switch (on by default) is "Buy vendor items through Knightshopper during a dispatch" in the settings.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- With the switch off, or without Knightshopper installed, the run behaves exactly as before.
- Full harness: 391/391 PASS (16 new).

v0.1.7.6 (2026-10-03) [testing]
- **Quick controls for the Lazy Hub window.** The plugin now offers the catalog and price settings (recipes above the character's level, the undersupplied thresholds, the revenue basis, pricing at the home world only, the price refresh interval, the price-match message) and the cart-run hand-off switches (fetching materials from retainers, walking to a summoning bell or to vendors, preferring a currency shop) to Lazy Hub (`/lazy`) over Dalamud IPC, so they can be changed from one window next to the other lalalazy plugins. Each change does exactly what the matching setting in the plugin's own window does.
- The cart-run hand-off switches can only be changed while no cart run is active.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Without Lazy Hub installed the plugin behaves exactly as before.

plugins.author: Akari
plugins.name: Market Helper
plugins.punchline: Undercut, list, gather and buy — market board automation end to end.
plugins.description:
Market Helper is an all-in-one market board tool with five tabs:

UNDERCUT — Walk a summoning bell's retainers and undercut every listed item. HQ and NQ are handled separately, your own retainers are matched rather than undercut, per-item overrides and price memory are supported, an obvious troll price is skipped, and mannequin/display items are never touched (if a row can't be verified it is skipped rather than risk delisting it). Closes the bell when it finishes.

LISTER — Build a list (hold CTRL and hover an item, or search) and press Go to list them all. Prices each item at the most common market price, ignoring lone troll listings, against your world, data center or whole region. Per-item stack sizes and list amounts, rolls extra items to the next retainer at the 20-slot cap, and includes a no-touch dry run.

FLIPPER — Compare any marketable item across Japan, America, Europe and Materia via Universalis. Top 10 listings per region, best cross-region flip, and seller/buyer tax modelling.

ITEM GATHERER — Pull designated items off your retainers into your bags, optionally returning your market listings first. Manual withdraw/deposit actions included.

BUYER — Build a shopping list by hand or import a MakePlace furniture list, then SCAN the market per world via Universalis and press SEND to travel with Lifestream and buy across worlds. Every purchase is verified against the game's own confirmation dialog before it is accepted. Listings are bought whole, so by default it never buys a bigger stack than you still need, and a hard sanity ceiling caps the price even with no cap set. If a planned listing has already been bought it chases the next cheapest, on other worlds if needed, until your order is filled. Dry run is on by default.

Open with /markethelp, /market, /mh, or /undercut.

plugins.author: yagi2
plugins.name: Restocker
plugins.punchline: Bulk reprice and split-list retainer market listings across all retainers.
plugins.description: Cross-retainer market workbench with a plan-then-apply flow. Reprice tab: per-retainer 'lowest -N g' / 'lowest exact' buttons walk each listing, fetch live market data via Dalamud's IMarketBoard.OfferingsReceived (skipping your own retainers, deduplicated per item/HQ), stage every change in a queue, then commit them all via a single Apply that calls SetRetainerMarketPrice directly. New listing tab: per-row qty x slots, target retainer combo, auto stack-splitting (e.g. 990 / 99 → ten listings of 99), and direct listing from character bag / Chocobo Saddlebag with no entrust step (saddle items are bulk-staged to the bag in one phase, then listed). Live progress dialog shows the current step (selecting retainer, fetching market data, listing, …) so long runs don't look frozen. Six-language UI (EN/JA/DE/FR/ZH/KO). Warns once at startup if AutoRetainer is also loaded since both drive retainer summoning.

plugins.author: Aschy
plugins.name: Armoury Cleaner
plugins.punchline: Filter and move unwanted gear out of your armoury chest.
plugins.description: Define filters by job, minimum/maximum equip level, and item level. Armoury Cleaner scans each gear slot and moves only items that match all active filters into your inventory so you can discard them.
plugins.changelog:
v1.0.9: New 'Skip Gearset Items' filter (default ON) ? items currently assigned to any saved gearset are excluded from the scan, so Discard All can never delete gear you actively use.
v1.0.8: Added /acplugin command for consistent access alongside /ac legacy alias.
v1.0.7: UI redesign ? removed Auto-Discard toggle; separate Move To Inventory and Discard All buttons; both now use random 800-1100ms delays for consistent pacing; direct discard from armoury is now the default for Discard All.
v1.0.6: Direct discard from armoury ? new option (under Auto-Discard) skips the move-to-inventory step and discards items straight from the armoury slot, with automatic fallback to move+discard if the game rejects it.
v1.0.5: Internal cleanup; repo renamed to AschyQOL.
v1.0.4: Discard All uses random 800-1100ms delay between items; Cancel Queue button.
v1.0.3: Auto-Discard mode via InventoryManager.DiscardItem.
v1.0.0: Initial release.

v1.0.0: Initial release.

plugins.punchline: Faloop Notification in Chat

plugins.changelog:
6ae42a0: Merge pull request #814 from SlashNephy/fix/faloop-login-failure

fix(FaloopIntegration): report rejected logins instead of retrying
7900863: fix(FaloopIntegration): report rejected logins instead of retrying

Faloop responds to a login with wrong credentials with 400 and
{"success":false,"msg":"Incorrect username or password."}. The client
threw on it, so nothing was shown in chat, and the connection loop
treated it as a transient error and kept retrying.

- Read the 400 response as a rejected login instead of throwing
- Print the reason to chat and stop retrying

Close #742

Co-Authored-By: Claude Mythos 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
229b134: Merge pull request #801 from SlashNephy/renovate/actions-download-artifact-8.x

Update actions/download-artifact action to v8.0.2
28f79de: Merge pull request #802 from SlashNephy/renovate/actions-upload-artifact-7.x

Update actions/upload-artifact action to v7.0.2
c2a211c: Merge pull request #803 from SlashNephy/renovate/actions-create-github-app-token-3.x

Update actions/create-github-app-token action to v3.3.0
aa78586: Update actions/create-github-app-token action to v3.3.0
4fb78c8: Update actions/upload-artifact action to v7.0.2
4a5ea84: Update actions/download-artifact action to v8.0.2
bdadbad: Merge pull request #813 from SlashNephy/feat/faloop-release-report

feat(FaloopIntegration): notify when a scheduled spawn is released
33272b7: feat(FaloopIntegration): notify when a scheduled spawn is released

Scheduled spawns are visible only to early access reporters at first,
and released to everyone later. The spawn_release handler was removed in
ac3fe87, so the release was no longer notified.

- Mark the spawn report of a scheduled spawn with "(scheduled)"
- Add a per-rank "Enable Mob Release Report" option (disabled by
  default) to notify "has been released!" on spawn_release
- Keep the stored spawn up to date on spawn_release even when the
  option is disabled
- Accept ISO 8601 strings as well as epoch milliseconds for the release
  timestamp, as Faloop's web client does

Close #685

Co-Authored-By: Claude Mythos 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

3cf9a9e: fix(FaloopIntegration): reconnect with a new client after disconnection

After "transport close", SocketIOClient's own reconnection kept the
engine.io session alive (pings continued) but the plugin never received
mob reports again until it was disabled and enabled.

Handle reconnection in the plugin instead, mirroring what re-enabling
the plugin does:

- Disable SocketIOClient's reconnection
- Run a connection loop that logs in again and connects with a new
  Socket.IO client on every disconnection, with exponential backoff
  from 5 seconds up to 5 minutes
- Time out a connection attempt that the server never accepts, since
  ConnectAsync only times out at the transport level
- Stop retrying when the credentials are rejected
- Ignore events from clients that have already been replaced

Refs #687

reusable-deploy-plugin.yml checks out the distribution repository, opens
a pull request there and merges it. Mint a GitHub App installation token
scoped to that repository instead of using a bot PAT.

Drop the Authorization header when fetching commits.json. This
repository is public so the request needs no authentication, and
expanding a token on the command line exposes it through the process
list.

change here does not take effect until every caller is updated, which
would leave a broken intermediate state whenever a secret is renamed.

plugins.author: dexcss
plugins.name: Glamour Sorter
plugins.description: Sorts glamour-able gear from your inventory into the Glamour Dresser — outfit sets as outfit glamours (including seasonal sets, with the Store as Outfit Glamour checkbox dialog automated) and loose items one by one — skipping anything already stored. Includes an extractor that withdraws dresser items back to your bags: all loose items, duplicates only, or one item type such as all rings. Open your Glamour Dresser, run /gsort, review the preview, then store.
plugins.changelog: v1.3.0.19: Spare copies are no longer planned as stores — a piece whose appearance is already in the dresser is dropped from the set plan and reported as a duplicate (the bag copy can be sold), which also removes the HQ leftovers that made the game refuse outfit stores. Skipped sets are always reported now (1.3.0.18 dropped them from the result list), and the plan card note text is fixed. v1.3.0.18: Outfit stores now hand in NQ pieces only — every HQ hand-in made the game refuse the combination silently (all successful stores in the 21:15-21:30 run used NQ pieces, all refusals involved HQ). HQ-only sets are reported as "the dresser will not take HQ gear as an outfit glamour" instead of failing after a click. Slot diagnostics also show each planned piece's quality. v1.3.0.17: Failed outfit stores now report the game's own reason — chat messages printed during the attempt are logged under "game said:" and the result reads "The game did not accept this outfit (left for manual review)", so the remaining refusals can be identified exactly instead of guessed. v1.3.0.16: Confirmation now clicks the real Yes button first (what a player does), then falls back to callback event 2 and event 0 in stages — the seasonal dialog was closing without depositing when only callbacks were fired. Combined with 1.3.0.15, "already in the stored outfit" is reported as ALREADY and is no longer counted as a store. v1.3.0.15: Honest results — "Already in the stored outfit — nothing to add" is now its own ALREADY state and no longer counts as a successful store; the tally reads stored / already there / need attention / failed. The store step also logs the click and, if no confirmation opens within 2 s, fires the addon's Store as Glamour callback (18) before giving up. v1.3.0.14: Diagnosis + fallback for the seasonal Outfit Glamour Creation stalls — the store step now logs the addon state, hand-in counts and every slot (item id, inventory type, flag), and if no confirmation opens within 2 s it fires the addon's Store as Glamour callback (18) as a fallback. v1.3.0.13: Quality consistency for outfit hand-ins — the outfit window only accepts pieces of one quality ("Only items of the same quality may be selected") and a mixed HQ/NQ selection made the game silently refuse the store while leaving the window open. The plugin now anchors on the quality it holds most of and hands in only pieces of that quality, logging any piece skipped for quality. v1.3.0.12: Checkbox-dialog fix — the confirm ladder now ticks the "Store as Outfit Glamour" checkbox first (synthetic ButtonClick + SetChecked) and fires Yes once the game enables it, instead of firing the default-confirm callback first, which closed the dialog without depositing on several sets (the "checkbox was never selected" symptom). The default-confirm callback is kept as a fallback for dialogs whose Yes cannot be enabled from the checkbox. v1.3.0.11: Cross-set outfit mismatch guard — a glamour piece can belong to more than one outfit set, and the game may open a different set's stored outfit when completing; the plugin now compares the opened outfit's item id with the planned set and skips with "left for manual review" instead of handing the piece into the wrong outfit and reporting a false failure. The store log keeps the dialog mode and prism-box index so any remaining case is diagnosable. v1.3.0.10: Fix the "No deposit detected" failures on outfit completions. The hand-in loop was allowed to target a slot already marked Filled (the outfit already contained that piece), which the game silently refused; it now only hands into Unfilled slots, and a set whose planned pieces are all already inside the outfit reports "Already in the stored outfit — nothing to add" instead of attempting a store. The native StoreExistingOutfit retry from 1.3.0.9 is removed — it returns success but deposits nothing unless the Glamour Creation window drives it. v1.3.0.9: Fix false "No deposit detected" results when completing an outfit — the game's confirm dialog sometimes closes without depositing for outfits that were only just created. After 1.5 s without a change the plugin now sends the same request the dialog sends (StoreExistingOutfit/StoreNewOutfit) once, then re-checks; store logs also report the dialog mode and prism-box index for diagnosis. v1.3.0.8: Withdraw tab clarity — the action buttons now state what they will do and grey out with an explicit empty-state label: "No duplicates to withdraw", "No singles to withdraw", and "No sets to withdraw & re-deposit" when there is nothing to pack (otherwise "Withdraw & re-deposit sets (N)" with counts). The consolidation description now explains the withdraw-then-pack-as-outfit loop and the slot saving. v1.3.0.7: Fix a window render crash when the set-consolidation loop ran with no loose set pieces left to start (the empty candidate list was indexed directly) — it now reports "Nothing to consolidate" instead. The consolidation pump is also exception-guarded so a future error cannot take the whole window down. v1.3.0.6: Set consolidation now runs in bag-sized batches — it withdraws one set's loose pieces (only as many as your free bag slots can hold), stores that set as a single outfit glamour, then repeats automatically. Before this the button tried to withdraw every loose set piece at once (359 items against 63 free slots) and was refused. v1.3.0.5: Dresser-full handling — at 800/800 the store run now stops with a clear 'Glamour Dresser is full' result instead of failing every remaining item with 'no deposit detected'. New "set pieces stored loose" detector on the Withdraw tab: it finds items the dresser stores individually that belong to an outfit set, shows how many pieces/sets and the approximate slots that would be freed, withdraws them (arm-then-confirm), then automatically runs the store pass that packs each set into one outfit glamour. v1.3.0.4: Single-item deposits now work — loose glamour items (not part of an outfit set) are stored with the game's own prism-box request command (the same request the Glamour Creation window's Yes button sends) instead of trying to open the outfit-store window, which the game only opens for set items. Each item costs one glamour prism (checked first) and the result reports "Stored item (dresser X->Y)". Outfit sets keep the existing flow. v1.3.0.3: Withdraw fix — the extractor was waiting on the dresser's 'requested' flag, which stays set while the data is loaded, so a run could stop before sending anything ("the dresser data stayed busy"); it now only gates on the loaded flag and retries refused sends. Store: the hand-in window is allowed to finish populating before the fill step decides nothing can be handed over. UI: two pages — Deposit (scan/store) and Withdraw (extractor) — with Abort reachable on the active page. v1.3.0.2: Gear-set protection hardening — items saved in a gear set are now detected from the saved gearset entries as well as the game's gear-set icon check (a 1.3.0.0 test scan saw 110 protected pieces on one pass and only 1 on another, so a piece could be misfiled as sortable). Deposit verification now reads the dresser list from MirageManager, so a dresser window that is momentarily unreadable no longer turns a successful deposit into a false "couldn't read the dresser" warning. v1.3.0.1: Fixes from the first 1.3.0.0 test. The dresser's "Add to pre-existing outfit glamour?" Yes/No prompt (shown when completing a stored outfit) is now answered automatically — before this it left the store flow stuck with the prompt on screen and froze the run. The Abort button stays clickable while a run is in progress. New watchdogs stop a set whose store window never opens or never produces its confirmation instead of stalling the rest of the run. Extractor: a refused RestorePrismBoxItem is retried (the client briefly refuses while a previous restore settles), waits for the dresser data request to finish, and skips further copies of a unique item (the game cannot give you a second copy while you hold one) instead of stopping the whole run; log lines now name the refused item. v1.3.0.0: Loose items — glamour-able items that belong to no outfit set are now stored as well, one at a time, and skipped when that item is already anywhere in the dresser. Extractor — withdraw dresser items back into your bags: all loose items, duplicates only (keeps one of each), or one item or item type such as all rings, with a live progress line. Item names and icons — planned pieces, duplicates and results now show the item icon, name and category instead of a raw item id. v1.2.0.1: Audit fixes. Completing an existing outfit works again — the pieces a stored outfit is still missing are planned as needed and are no longer listed as sellable duplicates. Deposit verification also accepts the planned pieces leaving your bags, so completing an outfit (or storing with a nearly full dresser) reports correctly instead of "No deposit detected". Store steps can no longer drop a set silently when a window does not open or the dresser closes mid-run, the store loop retries briefly while the dresser data reloads instead of stopping the rest of the run, and the Armoire toggle is locked while storing. /xllog now logs the scanned dresser/held counts for troubleshooting. v1.2.0.0: Full audit. Gear-set protection — pieces registered to a saved gear set are now left in your bags (the same check the game uses for its gear-set icon mark), instead of being pulled out of your gear sets. Smarter duplicates — stored outfit glamours are expanded into their pieces, so a second copy of an already-stored piece is flagged as sellable instead of being re-stored. The dresser's expanded item list is scanned, and a never-fill guard skips window slots the game already marks as part of the stored outfit. New model-duplicate hints show when a planned piece shares its appearance with something already stored. Deposit verification now retries briefly instead of failing on a single read. UI: version in the title, live progress tally while storing, MANUAL tag priority, gear-set and model-duplicate sections. Removed diagnostic logging. v1.1.1.0: The Store as Outfit Glamour checkbox dialog is now automated (synthetic checkbox click + default-confirm callback); all sets route to the dresser. v1.1.0.0: Armoire routing added.

plugins.description: A catalog of every mob in the game (16k+ models, 15.5k named) plus the full set of humanoid NPCs (Glamourer's NPC tab). plugins.author: XivHub
plugins.name: InventoryCleaner
plugins.punchline: Keep only the gear you actually use.
plugins.description:
Tidies the Armoury Chest against your saved gearsets. Anything equipped, referenced by a gearset, or a higher-ilvl upgrade for a job you still play is kept; everything else is moved out to your bags, fullest armoury container first, so the run frees space where it is tightest. Every run is previewed item by item with the reason for each decision, and nothing moves until you confirm.

Also does the reverse (pulling gearset pieces back into the armoury) and offers a discard picker: an icon grid of leftover gear, framed by rarity, where anything equipped, in a gearset, or on your allowlist is never listed.

plugins.author: yocopk
plugins.name: MogHouse Companion
plugins.punchline: Quality-of-life tools that connect your game to MogHouse. Timers and duty pops, pushed to your phone.
plugins.description:
Companion plugin for MogHouse (mog-house.com).

An all-in-one home for quality-of-life tools that link FINAL FANTASY XIV to your MogHouse account. Tools are added over time; each one can be switched on or off individually, and nothing leaves the game unless you enable it.

Timers: reads the timers you already see in the game's own Timers window (CTRL+U), including submarine and airship voyages, retainer ventures, map and leve allowances, custom deliveries and allied society dailies, and syncs them to your profile. MogHouse then pushes you a notification the moment one comes up, on web and mobile, even while the game and your PC are off. Voyages are timed to the last vessel back, so one notification means the whole fleet is home.

Duty Finder: when the confirm window appears, MogHouse pushes the duty or roulette name to your phone, so you know whether it is worth the sprint back to the desk. By default it stays quiet while the game is the window you are looking at.

The plugin is read-only: it collects your own data and reports status. It never performs an in-game action — it will not commence a duty for you, and it does not skip, confirm or automate anything.

Open it with /moghouse. Requires a MogHouse account, and a free one is enough: it syncs one character and sends one timer alert of your choosing, plus duty pops. Mog+ lifts both limits and warns you before a timer lands rather than as it does.

plugins.author: nxships
plugins.name: PlayerNexusTracker
plugins.punchline: Track every adventurer you meet in Eorzea.
plugins.description:
Track players you meet in FFXIV — who they are, when you ran into them, how their characters change over time. A focused social tracker built on the NexusKit framework.

Per-player detail view with Summary, Equipment, Class/Jobs, Achievements, Free Company, Encounters, History and Notes tabs. Optional enrichment from Lodestone (gear, FC link, achievement progress) and FFXIVCollect (mounts, minions, full achievement catalog). Live throttled refresh queue keeps external data fresh without hammering either service.

Configurable chat and toast notifications when players you've seen before change — rename, server transfer, Free Company join/leave/switch, achievement growth, refresh failures. Per-event filtering and history grouping so the chat doesn't drown you.

Powerful player-filter language with live preview to slice your list however you want; encounter history scoped per duty and content type; optional bridges to other Dalamud plugins (Lifestream world-travel, more to come).

Local-first: all data lives in a single SQLite file under your XIVLauncher config. Automated weekly maintenance keeps it tidy. English and German localization.
plugins.changelog:
## What's Changed
* fix: guard detail header table setup by @nxships in https://github.com/NexusFFXIV/PlayerNexusTracker/pull/65

SharkChat intercepts your chat before it's sent and swaps words or phrases for whatever you want.

Set up rules like Thanks → Thankies, and they'll apply automatically every time you chat — across any channel.

Features:
• Whole-word matching (so "tank" won't mangle "thanks")
• Case-insensitive by default
• Per-rule enable/disable
• Live preview so you can test rules before using them

Commands:
/shark — toggle on/off
/shark config — open settings

plugins.description:
Character Select+ allows you to create, save, and instantly apply fully customized character profiles with the press of a button. Switch between your OCs effortlessly using /select CharacterName, applying Penumbra Collections, Glamourer Designs, Customize+ Profiles, and Honorific Titles in one command.

While profile switching is its core purpose, Character Select+ includes additional features:
✔ Advanced Mode – Create custom macro setups for deeper character customization.
✔ Profile-Specific Designs – Use multiple outfits, styles, and looks per character.
✔ Favorites & Sorting – Keep profiles organized by name, date, or importance.
✔ Quick Swap Bar! 
✔ One-Click Macro Execution – Run predefined commands instantly when selecting a character.

Whether you're roleplaying, gposing, or just love quick customization, Character Select+ makes switching between characters faster, easier, and seamless.

plugins.author: The Redheaded Witch, WillWolf76
plugins.name: Fashion Report Calculator / Dye Finder
plugins.punchline: Know your Fashion Report points on the spot and help crowdsource new items and dyes!
plugins.description:
This is the new and improved Fashion Report System. This plugin will allow you to open a window that will show you what your fashion report status is vs the current week's theme.

There are a few parts to this. Since the only way to get Fashion Report for the week to my knowledge is speaking to Masked Rose after Tuesdays reset, this plugin takes the first person who does talk to him and updates everyone else. So only one person per week needs to speak to Masked Rose.

You can click on a theme and pull all the known items for that theme for that specific slot. You also get a very detailed breakdown of how much points you are getting based on what you are currently wearing.

The plugin also stores the attempts of those using the mod (just the data from fashioncheck, no user information) so that we can figure out the dyes faster and share information faster. The information in this table is wiped every week since once we discover the dyes, it is useless.

I still have more upgrades to do, including adding a dye window and the window that will help calculate the weekly dyes. I already have an idea of how I want to write them, so it shouldn't take me too long. If you have suggestions on how I can upgrade this, please share with me on github!

Credit for the program goes to it's original creator, WillWolf76, who wrote this for me originally.

When this plugin updates the database, it also updates my Discord Bot which you can set up to post fashion report each week. It's set to update on Tuesdays and Fridays (week start and dye information added). Link to add the Discord Bot is in the about section.
plugins.changelog: Fixed some minor bugs.

plugins.name: HMapSync (HMS)
plugins.punchline: Explore any zone together.
plugins.description: Load any in-game map client-side and explore it solo or with up to 20 friends, behind a packet filter that keeps the server seeing you as idle in your room. Co-op needs a relay key (closed beta); solo mode never connects to the relay.

plugins.author: dajoey
plugins.name: Lazy Gear Collector
plugins.punchline: Track upgradable gear sets and what it costs to finish them
plugins.description: Tracks upgradable gear collections piece by piece. Starts with Occult Crescent: North Horn's Phantom Vision sets - all 7 roles, 5 slots, 4 tiers. Shows which pieces you own and at what tier, what the next upgrade costs, and the exact obol/fixative shortfall to finish a role or the whole collection. Every item ID and price is read from the game's own shop data at runtime, so it stays correct across patches. Also flags Arcanaut's gear you can trade up for free. Use /lazygear to open.

- Without Lazy Hub installed the plugin behaves exactly as before.

plugins.changelog:
ec459fc: Update ARControl.csproj
f0ea323: Remove DiscardHelper integration
ea6de7c: Modernize codebase with C# 12 features

- Adopt primary constructors in VentureResolver, AutoRetainerReflection, and VentureListTab
  - Reduces boilerplate code by eliminating field declarations and assignments
  - Parameters are directly accessible throughout the class
- Standardize collection expressions using [] syntax
  - Replace 'new Dictionary<>()' with '[]' for cleaner initialization
  - Replace 'new List<>()' with '[]' for consistency
- Simplify LINQ queries by replacing .Where().Cast<>() with .OfType<>()
  - More efficient and cleaner null filtering
  - Removes unnecessary null-forgiving operators (!)
- Update array initializers to use collection expression syntax

These changes reduce code complexity while maintaining full compatibility with .NET 10 and C# 12.
1138beb: Switch to ECommons DalamudReflector

- Replace custom DalamudReflector implementation with ECommons.Reflection.DalamudReflector
- Simplify AutoRetainerReflection by removing IDisposable pattern (static method usage)
- Delete ARControl/Internal/DalamudReflector.cs (117 lines)
- Update .gitignore to exclude .claude/ directory

plugins.author: dajoey
plugins.name: Armoire Auto-Fill
plugins.punchline: Per-dungeon view of which armoire-eligible gear pieces you're still missing
plugins.description: Lists every armoire-eligible dungeon drop in the game and shows whether each is in your inventory, in your armoire, or still missing. Sort by level, hide completed dungeons, toggle to show owned items too. Open the armoire UI at an inn once per session to populate the in-armoire state; in-inventory and equipped state is detected automatically.
plugins.changelog:
v0.5.7.2 (2026-11-14) [testing]
- The plugin windows have been rebuilt on the shared LalaUiKit: one consistent layout with themed section headers, unified spacing and colour accents. All settings and behaviour are unchanged, and existing configuration loads as-is.

v0.5.7.1 (2026-11-10) [testing]
- Rebuilt against the Dalamud 15.0.4.0 payload for game patch 7.58. No functional changes.

v0.5.7.0 (2026-10-10)
- **The PvP shopping list now includes gear sold for Trophy Crystals and Wolf Collars.** The crystal quartermaster's Trophy Crystal Exchange (weapons, armour, accessories) and the collar quartermaster's exchange were missing from the list because their cost currencies were not mapped, so the PvP code came out empty. Both quartermasters are in the list now, checked against Knightshopper's own vendor catalog: every exported pair is one it accepts.
- Pieces no import code can name are now listed in the window by name with the reason (the shop has no vendor link in the game data, or Knightshopper has no vendor for its shop), instead of being dropped quietly. The Wolf Mark gear behind the mark quartermaster falls in this list: its shop opens through a dialogue handler, so no vendor pair can be written for it.
- The shopping summary line showed placeholder braces instead of the counts; it shows the numbers now.

v0.5.6.0 (2026-10-08)
- **Import codes now carry only what can actually be bought today.** Some pieces are gated behind more than a quest: seasonal vendors also gate pieces on an achievement, and the previous filter only knew about quests, so pieces the game would not sell yet were still written into the codes, and the first one of them made Knightshopper refuse the whole import ("Item N is not available from its shared Gil vendor"). The shopping list now checks live quest and achievement progress: what can be bought now goes into the code, a piece whose cheapest listing is locked falls back to a listing that can be bought, and a piece with no buyable listing at all is left out and counted at the bottom of the window ("N missing piece(s) need quest or achievement progress you don't have yet - left out of the import"). The rule applies to every currency, not just gil.

v0.5.5.0 (2026-10-08) [testing]
- **Import codes now name vendors that Knightshopper itself has.** The previous build still produced Gil codes that Knightshopper refused whole ("Item N is not available from its shared Gil vendor"): the rule it used to decide which vendors Knightshopper knows was a guess and was wrong for most Gil shops. The rule now follows how Knightshopper builds its own vendor list: a vendor is an NPC the game actually places in an area, and seasonal NPCs that are re-used under new ids with the same name and the same shops count once. It applies to every currency, not just gil. The Gil code now carries several times as many pieces, because shops the old rule dropped by mistake are back.
- Placeholder items with no name are no longer put in a code; Knightshopper has no entry for them.
- Every code and every catalog entry was checked offline against the vendor data produced by Knightshopper's own library (not against this plugin's own model): no refusals. This is not yet confirmed in the game, and newer game patches than the one checked are not covered.
- The shopping-list section says what the codes were checked against and that it is not yet confirmed in-game; the copy message also explains that Knightshopper names only the first item it refuses.
- The vendor placement is read from the game's area files once per session in the background (about one second), with one log line.

v0.5.4.0 (2026-10-08) [testing]
- **Import codes no longer contain items Knightshopper would refuse.** Knightshopper rejects a whole import when even one item is not in its own catalog, which the previous Gil code hit: shops whose vendors only spawn for an event never enter Knightshopper's catalog, but this plugin was still naming them. The catalog now only names shops with a permanently placed vendor, matching how Knightshopper derives its own list, and the same rule applies to every currency, not just gil.
- Pieces that this leaves out are no longer silent: the window shows "N items left out: Knightshopper cannot buy them", the build log counts the skipped shops, and the copy buttons never produce a code Knightshopper would answer with "not available from its shared vendor".

plugins.author: XivHub
plugins.name: AutoPincher
plugins.punchline: One-click retainer repricing against the live market board, fully local.
plugins.description: Repinches your retainer market listings by undercutting the cheapest live competitor by 1 gil. Reads each listing straight from game memory, clicks the in-game market board's Compare Prices to find the current cheapest offering, and sets your asking price to one below it, never below what a vendor gives, and never above your own cheapest copy. Your own retainers and housing mannequins are never treated as competitors, so two retainers selling the same item don't chase each other down. No server; nothing leaves your client unless you turn on the developer log and point it at your own server. Adds an Auto Pinch button next to AutoRetainer's retainer-list controls and a /autopinch command for the open retainer. AutoRetainer is optional (used only to pause its automation during a pinch run).

plugins.author: dajoey
plugins.name: AutoPotion
plugins.punchline: Per-job HP, MP, and deep dungeon potion automation.
plugins.description: Auto-uses the highest-tier HP potion, MP potion (Ether), and the deep dungeon regen potion (Sustaining / Eurekan / Orthos / Pilgrim's) at configurable thresholds. Each potion's threshold and on/off state is stored per-job, so casters and tanks can have completely different setups.
plugins.changelog:
v0.2.5.4 (2026-11-14) [testing]
- The settings window has been rebuilt on the shared LalaUiKit: one consistent layout with themed section headers, unified spacing and colour accents across every page. All settings, presets and automation behaviour are unchanged, and existing configuration loads as-is.

v0.2.5.3 (2026-11-10) [testing]
- Rebuilt against the Dalamud 15.0.4.0 payload for game patch 7.58. No functional changes.

v0.2.5.2 (2026-10-10) [testing]
- **Automatic item uses no longer cancel an open action sequence.** Any potion, ether, deep dungeon medicine or Echo Drops that would land while mudra seals or Ten Chi Jin are held is delayed until the sequence completes, instead of cancelling the ninjutsu mid-chain. The delay lasts only while the sequence is up (a mudra window is about six seconds) and lifts immediately after; at or below 25% HP the heal fires regardless - a cancelled jutsu is cheaper than dying. No other job's behaviour changes.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- With the optional decision log enabled, a held use is recorded with the `heldmudra` near-miss reason, rate-limited like every other near-miss line.

v0.2.5.1 (2026-10-03) [testing]
- **Quick controls for the Lazy Hub window.** The plugin now offers the master switch, "Only in combat", "Only in a duty", the HP, MP and Regen potion switches with their thresholds, and Cure Silence (Echo Drops) to Lazy Hub (`/lazy`) over Dalamud IPC, so they can be changed from one window next to the other lalalazy plugins. Each change does exactly what the matching setting in the plugin's own window does.
- The potion settings apply to the active job's profile, as in the settings window.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Without Lazy Hub installed the plugin behaves exactly as before.

v0.2.5.0 (2026-09-05)

- New per-job option: "Auto-use Echo Drops when silenced". When it is on and Silence lands (mob silence spells, AoE silences, deep dungeon traps), AutoPotion uses Echo Drops from inventory to cure it automatically. Item use is not blocked by Silence, so the cure works exactly when nothing else can.
- OFF by default like every option, and per job like the rest: tick the new box in the settings window for the jobs it should apply to. With it off (the default) nothing changes - not even a status check.
- It reuses the same machinery as the potions: HQ Echo Drops are preferred over normal ones, the shared 750 ms cooldown after any potion use applies, and a Silence that arrives during that cooldown is cured on the next tick.
- If the diagnostic tap is enabled, the cure logs as an `e` event; when it cannot fire the near-miss reasons are `edblocked` (on cooldown / blocked) or `ednostock` (none in the bags).
- No change to potion behaviour. HP/MP/regen thresholds, the overshoot guard, the deep dungeon Rehabilitation lockout and the in-combat / in-duty gates all work exactly as before.

v0.2.4.0 (2026-09-05)

- Added an optional "Log potion decisions" diagnostic, OFF by default. Turn it on with `/autopotion telemetry on` or the new Advanced / Diagnostics section of the settings window, and AutoPotion writes one line to its plugin log every time it uses a potion, plus a rate-limited line when a threshold was crossed and nothing fired.
- Purpose: the log line records the HP%, the MP%, the threshold that was in force and the job, so a threshold can be verified after the fact instead of guessed at. Nothing leaves the machine - the lines only go to the local Dalamud plugin log.
- The "nothing fired" lines say WHY in a short code: `hpover` (a potion was available but the heal would have been wasted), `hpblocked` / `mpblocked` / `rgblocked` (on cooldown or blocked by a status), `hpnostock` / `mpnostock` / `rgnostock` (none left in inventory) and `rgrehab` (Rehabilitation still up in a deep dungeon).
- These lines are heavily rate-limited on purpose: a repeated state logs once, not once per frame. Measured against 214 minutes of real play the near-miss lines come out under one line per minute, so the log stays readable.
- No change to potion behaviour. Thresholds, per-job profiles, the overshoot guard, the deep dungeon Rehabilitation lockout and the in-combat / in-duty gates all work exactly as before, and with the setting off (the default) the plugin does not even build a log line.

plugins.author: Faye, Kage
plugins.name: Better Occult Crescent & Chest Helper Interface
plugins.punchline: BOCCHI is here to smooth out your Occult Crescent experience.
plugins.description:
BOCCHI is here to smooth out your Occult Crescent experience.
- No more of that pesky 'walking' or 'finding chests'. That's for losers.
- A cute little Fate and CE panel that'll tell you what rewards it gives AND help you automatically path to it, wowee.
- An extra illegal 'illegal mode' for those of you that would rather be touching grass or playing a game with worthwhile content.

Command prefix: bocchi (alias: och)
  /bocchi → Opens the main window
  /bocchi config → Opens config (aliases: cfg, c)
  /bocchi config list → Lists config keys
  /bocchi config get <key> → Prints a config value
  /bocchi config set <key> <value> → Sets a config value
  /bocchi buff → Start/stop a buff run
  /bocchi tp [fate|ce|pot] → Teleport toward nearest matching activity
  /bocchi illegal [on|off|toggle] → Control Illegal Mode (no arg opens the window)
  /bocchi cmd flag-active-ce → Flag registering CE on the map
  /bocchi cmd flag-active-fate → Flag a FATE on the map
  /bocchi cmd flag-active-non-pot-fate → Flag a non-pot FATE
  /bocchi reload-translations → Reload translation files (alias: rt)
  /och … → Same as /bocchi (legacy alias; also /occultcrescenthelper)

plugins.author: Valenth Siveria
plugins.name: I Am Ready
plugins.punchline: Automatically accept or decline Duty Finder ready checks based on a configurable counter.
plugins.description:
# I Am Ready

**I Am Ready** is a Dalamud plugin for Final Fantasy XIV that automatically accepts or declines Party and Alliance Ready Checks based on a customizable counter. 

Whether you are stepping away for a moment or just tired of clicking, this plugin handles ready checks for you while mimicking human reaction times.

## ✨ Features

* **Auto-Answer Ready Checks:** Automatically clicks "Yes" or "No" when a ready check appears.
* **Configurable "Yes" Counter:** Set a specific number of times you want to automatically answer "Yes". Once that limit is reached, the plugin will automatically start answering "No" to prevent pulling when you are actually away.
* **Natural Delay:** Enable a randomized delay (0.7 to 2.5 seconds) before the plugin answers, making it look like a natural human reaction.
* **Smart Chat Triggers (Regex):** Add custom text phrases to the plugin. If someone says one of these phrases in Party or Alliance chat (e.g., "reset", "pulling"), your counter will automatically reset back to zero.
* **Bilingual Support:** The user interface is available in both English and German.

## 🚀 Usage

1. Type `/iar` in the in-game chat to open the configuration window.
2. Click the **Inactive/Active** button at the top to turn the auto-responder on or off.
3. Adjust the **Yes Count** slider. For example, if set to `5`, the plugin will answer "Yes" to the next 5 ready checks, and "No" to any checks after that.
4. Click the **Start** button at any time to manually reset your current counter back to zero.

### Chat Triggers (Regex Patterns)
At the bottom of the window, you can expand the **Regex Patterns** section. Here you can add simple words or complex regex patterns. 
If the plugin reads a matching message in your Party or Cross-World Party chat, it will instantly reset your counter to zero, assuming a new pull or instance is starting!

/iar - opens the I Am Ready tool

plugins.author: Blackcatz1911, dajoey
plugins.name: Lazy Currency Spender
plugins.punchline: Find the absolute best way to spend all your FFXIV currencies.
plugins.description: Fork of CurrencySpender by Blackcatz1911. Never wonder 'What should I do with this?' again. Access real-time prices from Universalis, identify missing collectibles tied to your currencies, and unlock new possibilities for utilizing your in-game resources effectively.
plugins.changelog:
v1.3.1.5 (2026-11-14) [testing]
- The plugin windows have been rebuilt on the shared LalaUiKit: one consistent layout with themed section headers, unified spacing and colour accents. All settings and behaviour are unchanged, and existing configuration loads as-is.

v1.3.1.4 (2026-11-10) [testing]
- Rebuilt against the Dalamud 15.0.4.0 payload for game patch 7.58. No functional changes.

v1.3.1.3 (2026-10-17) [testing]
- The configuration wizard's auto-open step now sets the actual auto-open setting instead of toggling the sellables table.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v1.3.1.2 (2026-10-08) [testing]
- Added a map location for the Faux Commander (the Faux Hollows vendor in Idyllshire). Its Flag and TP buttons now draw like every other listed shop, and the plugin no longer logs a `Missing location: 1033921` error once at every startup.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v1.3.1.1 (2026-10-07) [testing]
- **Upstream sync through CurrencySpender 1.3.1.** New tracked currencies (Faux Leaf, Achievement Certificate, Oizys Credit, Auxesia Credit) and vendors (Quinnana, Faux Commander), data-driven custom-shop generation (in-code CustomShops replaces the hardcoded Cosmocredit item lists), upstream's config version migrations, and the Service.ObjectTable API rename.
- **New optional integrations:** Lifestream and vnavmesh IPC wrappers with upstream's MovementTask movement helpers, and the NPC/menu highlight services. All are gracefully skipped when the providing plugin is absent.
- Font rendering keeps the fork's Dalamud asset-font setup; the fork keeps its own tab UI (Windows/), teleport flow, Hub integration and Quick Controls.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v1.2.7.4 (2026-10-05) [testing]
- Added map locations for the two shop NPCs at the Gold Saucer that had none: the tack & feed trader at Chocobo Square and the euphoric attendant. Both now draw their Flag and TP buttons like every other listed shop instead of having no buttons at all.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Five shop NPCs remain without a location on purpose: the game's own data places them nowhere (no Level-sheet placement, no placement dataset entry - campaign and seasonal attendants such as Eirene's Rain Exchange and Ermina that only exist while their event runs). They keep the behaviour introduced in 1.2.7.3: one note at debug level, no buttons.

plugins.author: croizat, dajoey
plugins.name: Lazy Fate Automation
plugins.punchline: Fully automated FATE grinding utilizing vnavmesh, lifestream, and Gluttony Combo.
plugins.description: Automates FATE grinding, including Zodiac Atma, Anima Luminous Crystals, Resistance Memories, Phantom Demiatmas, Yo-kai Watch Medals, and Bicolor Gemstones. Seamlessly integrates with vnavmesh for pathing and flight, lifestream for zone swapping, TextAdvance for dialogue skipping, and Gluttony Combo/BossMod for combat. Use /lazyfate to open.
plugins.changelog:
v0.0.3.12 (2026-11-14) [testing]
- The plugin windows have been rebuilt on the shared LalaUiKit: one consistent layout with themed section headers, unified spacing and colour accents. All settings and behaviour are unchanged, and existing configuration loads as-is.

v0.0.3.11 (2026-11-10) [testing]
- Rebuilt against the Dalamud 15.0.4.0 payload for game patch 7.58. No functional changes.

v0.0.3.10 (2026-10-31) [testing]
- **The FATE grind no longer starts FATEs above your level.** Level sync only lowers your level to match a FATE, it never raises it, so a FATE above your level could not be contributed to and walking to it only wasted time. FATEs above your level are now skipped; the tracker's unavailable list shows "FATE level N is above your level M". FATEs at or below your level run exactly as before.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.0.3.9 (2026-10-18) [testing]
- **Display name format and sort order changes are now saved.** Edits in the FATE tracker's "Sorting & Display" settings previously lived only in memory and reverted on the next plugin load; every change now persists immediately.
- **Reset to Default restores the actual default sort order.** The reset button dropped the Time Remaining criterion and put Time Remaining Urgent in ascending order (urgent FATEs last); it now restores the shipped six-entry default, shared with the config's own default so the two cannot drift apart.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.0.3.8 (2026-10-13) [testing]
- **BossMod Reborn no longer runs its own job rotations beside Gluttony Combo during FATEs.** The FATE grind creates and uses its own BossMod preset, "LazyFateAutomation", holding only the movement, FATE-targeting, level-sync and stay-close-to-target modules (melee and tanks close in, other roles hold at 10 yalms), and rewrites it each time the grind starts so an old or edited copy cannot bring job rotations back.
- **The grind no longer clears a BossMod preset another plugin (such as AutoDuty) or the player set.** It turns its preset on and off with BossMod Reborn's standard preset calls and only ever clears its own. Two calls BossMod Reborn does not provide, which failed on every attempt, are gone, and a failing call is logged once per run.
- The BossMod preset named "Gluttony" that earlier versions created is no longer used. It is left untouched in BossMod's preset list and can be deleted there by hand.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v0.0.3.7 (2026-10-05) [testing]
- **The boss FATE icon on the server info bar entry now actually renders.** The previous testing build showed no icon at all because the glyph reference pointed at an empty slot instead of the boss FATE icon; the icon value is now pinned so it stays the boss glyph.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Click behavior, the confirming second click and every other part of the server bar entry are unchanged.

plugins.author: dajoey
plugins.name: LazyCrucible
plugins.punchline: Crucible of the Unbroken familiar picks, filled in for every fight
plugins.description: For the Beastmaster duty Crucible of the Unbroken. Fills the ten-familiar run roster at the Bentbranch Meadows entry menu and the three Battlehorn slots before every fight with the familiars that answer that fight's mechanics: elemental weakness, interrupts, dispels, cleanses and crowd control, skipping knocked-out familiars and benching badly hurt ones. Picks are announced in chat. Every automation has its own toggle and manual edits always win. Includes the beast-pick advisor for every board and a read-only recorder that writes each Crucible screen to the Dalamud log. Use /lazycrucible to open.
plugins.changelog:
v0.1.9.18 (2026-11-14) [testing]
- The plugin windows have been rebuilt on the shared LalaUiKit: one consistent layout with themed section headers, unified spacing and colour accents. All settings and behaviour are unchanged, and existing configuration loads as-is.

v0.1.9.17 (2026-11-10) [testing]
- Rebuilt against the Dalamud 15.0.4.0 payload for game patch 7.58. No functional changes.

v0.1.9.16 (2026-10-13) [testing]
- **"Score: three familiars" run-roster mode, off by default.** For score runs. A run roster of one to three familiars scores the Beast Squad III bonus on every board, so with the option on the run roster is the best three familiars for the whole board instead of the board's full roster. The three are chosen from the familiars you own and that are not knocked out: they cover as many of the board's required interrupt, dispel and cleanse needs as any three can, then the damage the board calls to be blunted, then three of one kin when that costs no required cover (the Gambit bonus), then the rest by points. A roster of three saved for a different board is rewritten for the board you enter. Whatever the three cannot answer on the board is named on the window's summary line; nothing pops up. With three or fewer familiars the game registers the battlehorns itself, so the plugin leaves them alone. Found in the settings window and the Lazy Hub as "Score: three familiars".
- With the option off, nothing changes. While AutoDuty drives the run roster the plugin stands by there, option on or off.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v0.1.9.15 (2026-10-13) [testing]
- **Mitigation in the horn picks.** Fights with a damage wall now field a familiar that blunts it, ranked below every interrupt, dispel and cleanse need, and counted only for a familiar above the danger HP line. Durga's Atomic Ray gets a magic answer (drake's Smoldering Scales, pugil's Water Wall or a Scalekin's Scaleskin); Borgny gets coblyn's Vulcanize for the poison plus a magic answer; Gargoyle's Sweeping Evisceration gets a physical answer (a Beastkin's Beastskin, coblyn's Vulcanize or adamantoise's Harden Shell). The fight guide lists these under "Calls for".
- One telemetry line per fight names the team on the horns and the needs it cannot answer (`uncovered=`).
- **Works with AutoDuty.** While AutoDuty runs, it handles the run roster, shop, treasure, spoils and campsite itself, so the plugin stands by there; the battlehorns are AutoDuty's only with its "Fight picks" on, and the plugin picks them otherwise. AutoDuty's active profile is read through AutoDuty's own interface (its config file when that is unavailable), never changed; when neither can be read, every screen stands by, as before. The window shows one quiet line naming the screens it is standing by on.
- **No more corrections on top of AutoDuty's familiar picks.** AutoDuty re-applied its own picks every time, so they never reached a fight.
- **Fight guide: the Snarl -> Parting Blow advice is gone** (Parting Blow no longer dodges a hit since the September 17 hotfix). Plain tankbusters say to let a familiar with enough HP take them under Snarl; poisoning ones (Deadly Thrust, Cold Caress, Toxic Vomit) say to Parting Blow right after the hit so the poison leaves with the familiar; Gargoyle's Sweeping Evisceration says to save the Blink tome for it.
- Item values: Beastly Knife is valued like the elemental axes; Hero's Crown counts its Excellence proc (9 s of nullified attacks); Rapid Recast gear is valued; reraise items are worth a little less at Third Degree.
- **Patch 7.57: battlehorns the game registered itself (teams of three or fewer) are left alone**; a knocked-out member of a three-familiar team is no longer toggled off the horns.
- **Patch 7.57: the board's degree survives a job change** (the game now keeps the Crucible Mode until logout), so the degree passed to Gluttony Combo is no longer reset when the character returns to Beastmaster. It is forgotten at logout.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v0.1.9.14 (2026-10-06) [testing]
- **The board's difficulty degree now reaches Gluttony Combo during a fight.** The degree is set in the lobby (by a click or by AutoDuty) and the character then zones into the duty; the plugin used to forget it at every loading screen, so a fight always read as an unknown degree. It is now kept across loading screens and still forgotten when the Beastmaster job is left or the plugin unloads.

v0.1.9.13 (2026-10-06) [testing]
- **The board's difficulty degree is now read and shared with Gluttony Combo.** The Crucible board layout reports the degree whenever it is set, by a click or by AutoDuty; the plugin keeps the last one (Standard, First, Second or Third) and offers it to Gluttony Combo 1.0.4.288 or newer, which uses it to price the hits a familiar or the character will take. The degree is forgotten when the Beastmaster job is left, and until the first time it is set the plugin reports none. The change is logged as one `PS|` line (`note=degree`).
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

plugins.author: dajoey
plugins.name: LazyFoodBuff
plugins.punchline: Never forget to eat your food again.
plugins.description: Auto-eats food in combat duties with per-job selection, auto-select based on best stats, and a low-food warning.
plugins.changelog:
v0.1.5.3 (2026-11-14) [testing]
- The plugin windows have been rebuilt on the shared LalaUiKit: one consistent layout with themed section headers, unified spacing and colour accents. All settings and behaviour are unchanged, and existing configuration loads as-is.

v0.1.5.2 (2026-11-10) [testing]
- Rebuilt against the Dalamud 15.0.4.0 payload for game patch 7.58. No functional changes.

v0.1.5.1 (2026-10-03) [testing]
- **Quick controls for the Lazy Hub window.** The plugin now offers auto-eating, "Only in combat duties", the minutes of food left before eating again and the low-food warning with its count to Lazy Hub (`/lazy`) over Dalamud IPC, so they can be changed from one window next to the other lalalazy plugins. Each change does exactly what the matching setting in the plugin's own window does.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Without Lazy Hub installed the plugin behaves exactly as before.

v0.1.5.0 (2026-09-21)

- **"Only eat in combat duties" now covers Crucible of the Unbroken.** The five boards count as combat duties, and so does the Bentbranch Meadows entry area while playing Beastmaster (the one job that can enter), so the meal is eaten before a run starts. Eating before entry matters: a meal eaten inside does not refill HP to the raised maximum.

v0.1.4.0 (2026-09-05)

- Optional decision diagnostics, off by default. Turn on "Log food decisions" (settings window, Advanced / Diagnostics) or run `/lazyfoodbuff telemetry on`, and every time the plugin settles on a food for the current job it writes one line to the plugin log: the food it picked, its score, and the runner-ups it beat â€” plus a second line when that food is actually eaten. The point is the runner-ups: "picked X at 41.20 over Y at 40.80" is the shape of evidence that can eventually say whether the auto-select weights are right. Nothing leaves the machine; the lines only go to the local plugin log.

- Honest caveat: this is a data-collection investment, not an answer. The outcome side (what a food actually did to damage) needs weeks of encounter data before it says anything statistically â€” the plugin log will quietly accumulate the decision half in the meantime.
- Nothing about food selection changed. When the toggle is off, the only cost is one boolean read.

v0.1.3.1 (2026-09-05)

- The "What's new" popup now opens after this very update. 0.1.3.0 stayed silent the first time it ran because it had no record of the last version shown; the gate now tells an updated plugin (settings file already present) apart from a brand-new install (none yet) and only the latter stays quiet (`ChangelogGate.Options.ExistingInstall`, read from `pi.ConfigFile.Exists`.

- Nothing else changed. The notes can be reopened later with `/lazyfoodbuff changelog`.

The point is the runner-ups: "picked X at 41.20 over Y at 40.80" is the shape of evidence that can eventually say whether the auto-select weights are right. Nothing leaves the machine; the lines only go to the local plugin log.

- Honest caveat: this is a data-collection investment, not an answer. The outcome side (what a food actually did to damage) needs weeks of encounter data before it says anything statistically â€” the plugin log will quietly accumulate the decision half in the meantime.
- Nothing about food selection changed. When the toggle is off, the only cost is one boolean read.

v0.1.3.1 (2026-09-05)

- The "What's new" popup now opens after this very update. 0.1.3.0 stayed silent the first time it ran because it had no record of the last version shown; the gate now tells an updated plugin (settings file already present) apart from a brand-new install (none yet) and only the latter stays quiet (`ChangelogGate.Options.ExistingInstall`, read from `pi.ConfigFile.Exists`.

- Nothing else changed. The notes can be reopened later with `/lazyfoodbuff changelog`.

plugins.author: dajoey
plugins.name: LazyRetainerLive
plugins.punchline: Real-time retainer venture countdowns for your dashboard.
plugins.description: Serves the logged-in character's live retainer and venture state on loopback HTTP (127.0.0.1:10504) so the ffxiv dashboard relay can show real-time venture countdowns instead of AutoRetainer's occasionally-stale file cache.
plugins.changelog:
v0.1.0.4 (2026-11-14) [testing]
- The plugin windows have been rebuilt on the shared LalaUiKit: one consistent layout with themed section headers, unified spacing and colour accents. All settings and behaviour are unchanged, and existing configuration loads as-is.

v0.1.0.3 (2026-11-10) [testing]
- Rebuilt against the Dalamud 15.0.4.0 payload for game patch 7.58. No functional changes.

v0.1.0.2 (2026-10-03) [testing]
- **Quick controls for the Lazy Hub window.** The plugin now offers the switch that serves retainer data (the port stays in the plugin's own window) to Lazy Hub (`/lazy`) over Dalamud IPC, so they can be changed from one window next to the other lalalazy plugins. Each change does exactly what the matching setting in the plugin's own window does.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Without Lazy Hub installed the plugin behaves exactly as before.

v0.1.0.1 (2026-09-05)


- Corrected a wrong claim in the v0.1.0.0 notes below (and on the mod's web page): **the endpoint does not answer 503 on logout.** Once logged in, it keeps serving that character's last known retainer state - including at the title screen - and only ever answers 503 if it has never read the retainer table at all since the plugin loaded (i.e. it started at the title screen and no login has happened yet). That freeze is deliberate and is the better behaviour: measured previously the frozen live snapshot was still *newer* than AutoRetainer's file, so falling back to the file on logout would have shown the dashboard **older** data, not fresher. No behaviour was changed here - only the description was wrong.
- The settings window no longer reports "serving live snapshot" while logged out. It now distinguishes three states: no snapshot yet, serving a live snapshot, or serving the last-known snapshot while the game is in transition.


- For anything scripting against this endpoint: `readAt` is the time the request was **served**, not the time the data was read from the game, so it does not reveal how stale a frozen snapshot is. Use the settings window (or `/lazyretainerlive debug`) to tell live from frozen.

v0.1.0.0 (2026-09-05)


- First release. LazyRetainerLive reads the logged-in character's LIVE retainer table (the same in-memory data AutoRetainer uses to drive its own countdowns) and serves it as JSON on `http://127.0.0.1:10504/retainers`, so the ffxiv dashboard's retainer panel can show venture countdowns that update the moment a venture is collected instead of whenever AutoRetainer next saves its config file.
- When not logged in (or the live table has no data yet) the endpoint answers HTTP 503, which tells the dashboard relay to fall back to AutoRetainer's file. Loopback only - the port is never reachable from other machines.


- Companion of AutoRetainer - it reads, it never writes, assigns, or collects anything. Settings: Enabled (default on) and loopback port (default 10504). Commands: `/lazyretainerlive` opens settings, `/lazyretainerlive debug` dumps listener + snapshot state, `/lazyretainerlive changelog` reopens this popup.
- Why this exists: AutoRetainer's `DefaultConfig.json` (which feeds the dashboard today) is saved only at AutoRetainer's own save points, so its venture rows can be tens of minutes stale while ventures are actually completing. The countdown for the logged-in character lives in the game's memory - this plugin is a small read-only window onto it.

plugins.punchline: A modified fork of the old Macro Chain that allows you to run multiple macros one after the other (or repeat them).
plugins.description:
Allows for a macro to continue onto the next macro by using '/nextmacro' on the last line of a macro.
Adding '/nextmacro' on the last line of Macro #01 will automatically execute Macro #02
Adding '/nextmacro down' on the last line of Macro #01 will automatically execute Macro #11
Also allows executing any macro from chat using '/runmacro'
You can repeat a macro by using /runmacro inside the macro followed by the number of the macro you're editing
Using '/macrocancel' will stop the currently running macro
