metadataCompletePlugins.author: dajoey
metadataCompletePlugins.name: Gluttony Combo
metadataCompletePlugins.punchline: Lalalazy fork of Wrath Combo - XIVCombo for very lazy players.
metadataCompletePlugins.description: Gluttony Combo - lalalazy fork of Gluttony Combo. XIVCombo for very lazy players.
metadataCompletePlugins.changelog:
v1.0.4.339 (2026-11-14) [testing]
- The plugin windows have been rebuilt on the shared LalaUiKit: one consistent layout with themed section headers, unified spacing and colour accents. All settings and behaviour are unchanged, and existing configuration loads as-is.

v1.0.4.338 (2026-11-10) [testing]
- Rebuilt against the Dalamud 15.0.4.0 payload for game patch 7.58. No functional changes.

v1.0.4.337 (2026-11-09) [testing]
- **The AI decision layer is gone.** The Fight Brain's question side - the raidwide mitigation ask, the pre-pull plan reader (party finder text and the `/gluttony plan` note command), and the party-callout reader - has been removed from the plugin, together with its relay address setting and the two "Plan Reader"/"Callout Reader" switches. GluttonyCombo no longer asks any decision model anything, sends no snapshot anywhere, and keeps no relay URL: the only network path it still uses is the movement tap's `/move/ingest` upload, which records the movement profiles and never carried a decision.
- What stays is pure code and unchanged: the rotation and every combo, the Fight Brain forecast reads and `FB|forecast` lines, the countdown strip, the shadow cast-gate lines, the party-data shadow rules (`FB|party-mit`, `FB|pos-zone`), and the movement recorder and shadow move planner. The move planner's `MP|` decision lines keep their exact format and now always carry the code pick only.
- The shadow move planner no longer has its ask-side toggle; `/gluttony movelog` now switches the recorder and the planner together, and its status line reads two switches instead of three.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.336 (2026-11-09) [testing]
- **Saving a custom action to a hotbar while in PvP now writes the PvP layout.** The custom-action editor's hotbar save told the game the write was a normal-slot write regardless of the current content, so a save made while in PvP updated the regular hotbar set instead of the PvP one; the call now passes the content check (upstream's fix), so the PvP variant of the slot is the one written.
- **The action-replacing hook answers in the game's own yes/no shape.** The IsActionIdReplaceable detour and its delegate declared an unsigned 64-bit return where the game's callback uses a boolean, so the replace decision relied on 0/1 marshalling to land correctly; both signatures now match the native BOOL return (upstream's fix), and the early-return values read true/false instead of 1/0. No behavior change is intended - this removes a latent hook-contract mismatch.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.335 (2026-11-07) [testing]
- **AoE heals no longer fire back to back on a party that is at or near full HP.** Follow-up to 1.0.4.334: on a party whose bars all read full or nearly full, the auto-rotation kept pressing AoE heals - a bar just under 100% never counted as full (regen-tick oscillation and display rounding), and a heal that had just gone out did not stand the press path down while it landed. Two changes, shared by Astrologian, White Mage, Scholar and Sage. First, a member only counts as needing an AoE heal on a real deficit: a bar at or above 98% reads as full for both the one-button average and the auto-rotation's member count, so no threshold setting (including the 100 "disable this check" setting, and a target count of 0, which is now floored at 1) can make a full party eligible. Second, the auto-rotation presses one AoE heal at a time: after a press goes out, the next waits out that cast's flight plus a second for the heal to land and party HP to propagate, so a movement-cancelled cast is no longer re-issued every tick. Real damage is never starved - a party still under the threshold after the window heals again immediately. Single-target heals, raidwide pre-casts and the 1.0.4.334 out-of-range fix are unchanged; the manual one-button still heals when pressed.

v1.0.4.334 (2026-11-07) [testing]

metadataCompletePlugins.author: dajoey
metadataCompletePlugins.name: PvP Solver
metadataCompletePlugins.punchline: PvP-only auto-rotation
metadataCompletePlugins.description: PvP-only auto-rotation for FFXIV. Activates in PvP zones.
metadataCompletePlugins.changelog:
v0.1.2.15 (2026-11-14) [testing]
- The plugin windows have been rebuilt on the shared LalaUiKit: one consistent layout with themed section headers, unified spacing and colour accents. All settings and behaviour are unchanged, and existing configuration loads as-is.

v0.1.2.14 (2026-11-10) [testing]
- Rebuilt against the Dalamud 15.0.4.0 payload for game patch 7.58. No functional changes.


- **Removed the AI decision layer.** The optional relayed decision model (focus picking, Limit Break firing and the healer-call shadow lines, with their "call the shots" settings row and its relay address field) is gone from the plugin. No fight snapshot is built or sent anywhere anymore, and the plugin makes no decision calls of any kind.
- Targeting, Guard, Recuperate, the defensive table, StickyTarget and every other rotation behavior are unchanged. The defensive rules keep reading real HP (current HP out of the maximum) under the neutral name `RealHp.HpRatio`; no threshold or default moved.
- PvP Solver still never moves the character and never fires a PvP Limit Break on its own logic, exactly as before.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.


- **The Jev co-pilot logs the plain code rule's answer beside Jev's, for both of its questions.** Each `JV|focus-pick` line names the enemy Jev picked and the enemy the plain rule would pick (the lowest-HP enemy in attack range); each `JV|lb-shadow` line names Jev's Limit Break call and the code rule's. Both answers are recorded side by side and graded after the session, to show which one decides better. Log only: targeting, Limit Break firing and every other behavior are unchanged.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.


- Upstream engine sync (RotationSolverReborn a560469db): the rotation engine now builds in upstream's merged single-project layout.
- Ports upstream engine fixes: the action manager is read at call time instead of a pointer cached at startup (a stale-pointer crash class), configuration saves are atomic (write to a temp file, then replace), and the shield-value calculation can no longer overflow on very large HP values.
- No rotation behavior change; the 21 PvP rotations and their presets are untouched.

v0.1.2.10 (2026-11-01) [testing]
- **The per-job defensive actions also read real HP.** Heart of Corundum, Tempera Coat, Earth's Reply, Riddle of Earth, the Bloodbath rows, Lady of Crowns, Microcosmos, Meisui, Impalement, Xenoglossy's low-HP arm and Shadowbringer's HP arm compared their "use below this HP" thresholds against predicted HP, which counts heals still on the way; predicted can read 84% one second before a death at about 40% real HP. They now compare against the current HP out of the maximum, the same real value Guard and the defensive table already use. Thresholds and defaults are unchanged, and reads of enemies' and allies' HP (Smite, Guardian, Blasting Zone, Perfectio, the burst target) are untouched.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v0.1.2.9 (2026-11-01) [testing]
- **Self-defence now reads real HP.** Guard, Recuperate and the generic defensive actions (the "use below X% HP" table) compared their thresholds against predicted HP, which counts heals still on the way; predicted can read 84% one second before a death at about 40% real HP, so nothing fired. All of them now compare against the current HP out of the maximum, the same real value the Jev snapshot uses. Thresholds and defaults are unchanged.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v0.1.2.8 (2026-10-31) [testing]
- **"Let Jev call the shots" now sees real HP.** The player's and allies' HP sent to Jev is the current HP out of the maximum, no longer PvP Solver's predicted HP, which counts heals still on the way. In one match Jev was told 84% one second before a death at about 40%.
- **Jev's pick no longer drops when Jev is briefly unsure.** The relay now keeps the last pick itself while that enemy is still hittable, and drops it on purpose when the enemy goes under Guard, out of reach or stale. PvP Solver follows the relay's call and never brings a dropped pick back. Only with an older relay does PvP Solver keep the last pick, for up to three seconds after Jev gave it, while that enemy is still a valid target.
- **The Limit Break log matches what happened.** `JV|lb-fired` is written once when the Limit Break goes off in a fire window. `JV|lb-fire-skip` is written only when a window closes without it, with the reason: unusable, follow-up, out-of-range, no-target or timeout. A report of the use that arrives up to two seconds late still counts as fired. Before, a skip line could appear in windows that then fired, and windows that really failed wrote nothing.
- **Each action used is reported once.** The game reports each action twice; the same action on the same target within 1.5 seconds now counts once in the snapshot.
- **Alliance members are included (Frontline).** After the party members, the nearest alliance members are sent too, marked as alliance, up to eight allies in all. Each ally now carries its object id, so Jev can name an ally to heal.
- **Healer call, logged only.** When Jev suggests whom a healer should heal (an ally, self, attack or Guard), the suggestion is written as one `JV|heal-shadow` log line for the first suggestion in each fight and each time it changes; an answer with no suggestion does not count as a change. Nothing acts on it yet.
- **Relay failures are visible in the log.** One summary line per fight (when combat ends, or every 60 seconds while calls fail) counts calls that succeeded, timed out, got an error reply or failed. No line per call, and no call is counted in a later fight. An unreadable heal or Limit Break value in a reply no longer drops the rest of the answer.
- PvP Solver still never moves the character.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.1.2.7 (2026-10-29) [testing]
- **"Let Jev call the shots" reports what actually happened.** Each snapshot also carries the player's current target and the actions actually used since the last one (action and target only), so each of Jev's picks can be checked against what PvP Solver did and whether that enemy went down.
- Jev's focus pick is kept steady: it moves to another enemy only when that one is clearly the better pick.
- **A line, cone or splash Limit Break that Jev called could be skipped** because the action kept its own "most enemies" target. It is now aimed at the enemy Jev chose, which the game has just confirmed as a valid target. A skipped fire writes one reason line to the log.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

rawManifest.Name: PvP Solver
rawManifest.Punchline: PvP-only auto-rotation
rawManifest.Description: PvP-only auto-rotation for FFXIV. Activates in PvP zones.
rawManifest.Changelog:
v0.1.2.15 (2026-11-14) [testing]
- The plugin windows have been rebuilt on the shared LalaUiKit: one consistent layout with themed section headers, unified spacing and colour accents. All settings and behaviour are unchanged, and existing configuration loads as-is.

v0.1.2.14 (2026-11-10) [testing]
- Rebuilt against the Dalamud 15.0.4.0 payload for game patch 7.58. No functional changes.


- **Removed the AI decision layer.** The optional relayed decision model (focus picking, Limit Break firing and the healer-call shadow lines, with their "call the shots" settings row and its relay address field) is gone from the plugin. No fight snapshot is built or sent anywhere anymore, and the plugin makes no decision calls of any kind.
- Targeting, Guard, Recuperate, the defensive table, StickyTarget and every other rotation behavior are unchanged. The defensive rules keep reading real HP (current HP out of the maximum) under the neutral name `RealHp.HpRatio`; no threshold or default moved.
- PvP Solver still never moves the character and never fires a PvP Limit Break on its own logic, exactly as before.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.


- **The Jev co-pilot logs the plain code rule's answer beside Jev's, for both of its questions.** Each `JV|focus-pick` line names the enemy Jev picked and the enemy the plain rule would pick (the lowest-HP enemy in attack range); each `JV|lb-shadow` line names Jev's Limit Break call and the code rule's. Both answers are recorded side by side and graded after the session, to show which one decides better. Log only: targeting, Limit Break firing and every other behavior are unchanged.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.


- Upstream engine sync (RotationSolverReborn a560469db): the rotation engine now builds in upstream's merged single-project layout.
- Ports upstream engine fixes: the action manager is read at call time instead of a pointer cached at startup (a stale-pointer crash class), configuration saves are atomic (write to a temp file, then replace), and the shield-value calculation can no longer overflow on very large HP values.
- No rotation behavior change; the 21 PvP rotations and their presets are untouched.

v0.1.2.10 (2026-11-01) [testing]
- **The per-job defensive actions also read real HP.** Heart of Corundum, Tempera Coat, Earth's Reply, Riddle of Earth, the Bloodbath rows, Lady of Crowns, Microcosmos, Meisui, Impalement, Xenoglossy's low-HP arm and Shadowbringer's HP arm compared their "use below this HP" thresholds against predicted HP, which counts heals still on the way; predicted can read 84% one second before a death at about 40% real HP. They now compare against the current HP out of the maximum, the same real value Guard and the defensive table already use. Thresholds and defaults are unchanged, and reads of enemies' and allies' HP (Smite, Guardian, Blasting Zone, Perfectio, the burst target) are untouched.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v0.1.2.9 (2026-11-01) [testing]
- **Self-defence now reads real HP.** Guard, Recuperate and the generic defensive actions (the "use below X% HP" table) compared their thresholds against predicted HP, which counts heals still on the way; predicted can read 84% one second before a death at about 40% real HP, so nothing fired. All of them now compare against the current HP out of the maximum, the same real value the Jev snapshot uses. Thresholds and defaults are unchanged.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v0.1.2.8 (2026-10-31) [testing]
- **"Let Jev call the shots" now sees real HP.** The player's and allies' HP sent to Jev is the current HP out of the maximum, no longer PvP Solver's predicted HP, which counts heals still on the way. In one match Jev was told 84% one second before a death at about 40%.
- **Jev's pick no longer drops when Jev is briefly unsure.** The relay now keeps the last pick itself while that enemy is still hittable, and drops it on purpose when the enemy goes under Guard, out of reach or stale. PvP Solver follows the relay's call and never brings a dropped pick back. Only with an older relay does PvP Solver keep the last pick, for up to three seconds after Jev gave it, while that enemy is still a valid target.
- **The Limit Break log matches what happened.** `JV|lb-fired` is written once when the Limit Break goes off in a fire window. `JV|lb-fire-skip` is written only when a window closes without it, with the reason: unusable, follow-up, out-of-range, no-target or timeout. A report of the use that arrives up to two seconds late still counts as fired. Before, a skip line could appear in windows that then fired, and windows that really failed wrote nothing.
- **Each action used is reported once.** The game reports each action twice; the same action on the same target within 1.5 seconds now counts once in the snapshot.
- **Alliance members are included (Frontline).** After the party members, the nearest alliance members are sent too, marked as alliance, up to eight allies in all. Each ally now carries its object id, so Jev can name an ally to heal.
- **Healer call, logged only.** When Jev suggests whom a healer should heal (an ally, self, attack or Guard), the suggestion is written as one `JV|heal-shadow` log line for the first suggestion in each fight and each time it changes; an answer with no suggestion does not count as a change. Nothing acts on it yet.
- **Relay failures are visible in the log.** One summary line per fight (when combat ends, or every 60 seconds while calls fail) counts calls that succeeded, timed out, got an error reply or failed. No line per call, and no call is counted in a later fight. An unreadable heal or Limit Break value in a reply no longer drops the rest of the answer.
- PvP Solver still never moves the character.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.1.2.7 (2026-10-29) [testing]
- **"Let Jev call the shots" reports what actually happened.** Each snapshot also carries the player's current target and the actions actually used since the last one (action and target only), so each of Jev's picks can be checked against what PvP Solver did and whether that enemy went down.
- Jev's focus pick is kept steady: it moves to another enemy only when that one is clearly the better pick.
- **A line, cone or splash Limit Break that Jev called could be skipped** because the action kept its own "most enemies" target. It is now aimed at the enemy Jev chose, which the game has just confirmed as a valid target. A skipped fire writes one reason line to the log.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

metadataCompletePlugins.author: The Combat Reborn Team
metadataCompletePlugins.name: Rotation Solver Reborn
metadataCompletePlugins.punchline: Analyses combat information every frame and finds the best action.
metadataCompletePlugins.description:
Analyses combat information every frame and finds the best action.

This means almost all the information available in one frame in combat, including the status of all players in the party, the status of any hostile targets, skill cooldowns, the MP and HP of characters, the location of characters, casting status of the hostile target, combo, combat duration, player level, etc.
Then, it will highlight the best action on the hot bar, or help you to click on it.
It is designed for `general combat`, not for savage or ultimate. Use it carefully.

metadataCompletePlugins.author: NightmareXIV
metadataCompletePlugins.name: Splatoon
metadataCompletePlugins.punchline: Scriptable overlay engine for drawing mechanics, markers, and indicators in real-time
metadataCompletePlugins.description:
Splatoon is a scriptable telegraph and overlay engine for Final Fantasy XIV, built on the Dalamud plugin framework. It allows scripts to draw shapes, markers, labels, and indicators directly in the game world. These overlays can be attached to actors, positions, or events, and are rendered with precise positioning.

Splatoon does not include presets or encounter logic by default. If you want presets, you must create them yourself or import them from others.

In short, Splatoon draws things. What it draws is up to you!
metadataCompletePlugins.changelog:
- Library updates
- Improvements to map effect tab

metadataCompletePlugins.author: attick, daemitus, alymphocyte, grammernatzi
metadataCompletePlugins.name: XIV Combo Expandedest
metadataCompletePlugins.punchline: Condenses combos and mutually exclusive abilities onto a single button. Plus extras.
metadataCompletePlugins.description:
This is an enhanced version of XIVCombo with a variety of new added features.
This is mutually exclusive with other XIVCombo versions, so make sure they do not conflict!
metadataCompletePlugins.changelog:
New features unlikely to be added until Evercold releases. Bug fixes will still happen, though.
    
    1.5.0.91: 
    * Removed Burst Strike/Fated Circle to Bloodfest as you now cannot overcap with Bloodfest.
    * Added Bloodfest to No Mercy.
    * Fixed a bug where Blizzard/Fire switcher did not work without Enochian unlocked.

    1.5.0.90: 
    * Updated to 7.4.
    * Some more changes coming soon but emergency maintenance started RIP
    
    1.5.0.82:
    * Reawakened Fangs Feature now also applies to Steel Maw.
    
    1.5.0.79:
    * Phlegma into Eukrasian Dyskrasia added.
    
    1.5.0.73:
    * Meisui/Tenri priority fixed and DWaD to Meisui added.
    * Monk's Draconic Leap feature now properly syncs below level 50 when you don't have a form.
    * Raise Hard Target Lockout Feature added.
    
    1.5.0.72:
    * Double Down features now account for its new cost.
    * New option for Royal Authority to Atonement where it will only activate if you are about to overwrite Sword Oath in your combo.
    * Empyreal Arrow will no longer turn into Pitch Perfect under any circumstances.
    
    1.5.0.71:
    * Updated for 7.1 compatibility.
    * Devilment to Starfall Dance feature removed as it is now vanilla.
    * Removed Jump to Mirage Dive due to it being vanilla, as I completely forgot to earlier.
    * Added an 'Only When Full' option to Sidewinder to Pitch Perfect.

    1.5.0.70:
    * Added Comet Overwrite Prevention feature. Or did I?
    * Removed Holy overcap features (it made no sense when you gain, not lose, DPS by letting it overcap).
    
    1.5.0.69 (Nice):
    * Sacrificium Feature added.
    * Despair to Flare Star added.
    * Dragon Kick to Forbidden Chakra added.
    
    1.5.0.67:
    * Blizzard 3 & 2 to Flare Star feature added.
    
    1.5.0.61:
    * Lucid Dreaming Reminders now have a configurable MP threshold, as well as a configurable cooldown remaining offset where they stop replacing the cooldown.
    
    1.5.0.60:
    * Combos to Saber Dance during Devilment feature added.
    * Some other stuff added to Dancer, too. Maybe.
    * Phlegma to Psyche added.
    
    1.5.0.59:
    * Isle Sprint feature added.
    
    1.5.0.53:
    * Reaving Steel added from regular XIVComboExpanded. Maybe something else, too? Tis a secret.
    * Hooking Hooksets and Chummy Cast added.
    
    1.5.0.51:
    * Chaotic Glide added.
    
    1.5.0.49:
    * Standard Step into Technical Step added.
    
    1.5.0.41:
    * Viper features added. Please look forward to it (happening right now).

metadataCompletePlugins.author: DhogGPT
metadataCompletePlugins.name: Deep Ducking
metadataCompletePlugins.punchline: Deep Ducking public host and authenticated module access.
metadataCompletePlugins.description:
The Deep Ducking public host provides the introduction, community links and authenticated loading of separately supplied DDuck modules. /deepducking and /dduck open the introduction when no module is loaded.

Full module required for all commands below except opening the host window.

Commands (use /deepducking; /dduck is an alias):
/deepducking [toggle main window]
/dduck [alias for /deepducking; accepts all commands below]
/deepducking mini [toggle Mini]
/deepducking settings [open Settings]
/deepducking config [open Settings]
/deepducking debug [reveal and open Advanced for this plugin load]
/deepducking help [open command help]
/deepducking start [floor] [start or continue selected save; optional fresh-run floor]

metadataCompletePlugins.author: Ice
metadataCompletePlugins.name: Gather & Chill
metadataCompletePlugins.punchline: The gathering companion that we all needed.
metadataCompletePlugins.description: A gathering plugin that will help you with your gathering needs. Between gathering items for you, or self applying buffs to make the task of gathering monotonous.
metadataCompletePlugins.changelog:
- Cordials now have a node type restriction allowance
	- You can set if you want to (or not) used them for ephemeral, legendary, and normal nodes
- Collectables got a little bit of a logic overall
	- Short end, less strict and less following the TC guide... this might backfire on me, but allows for being a bit more reserved in gp usage. Will probably still fine tweak this as time goes on
- Collectables also have a setting to set which goal you would like to go for (high/mid/low)
- General gatherables have profiles that can be assigned with rules
	- The baseline is still there, if you don't feel like fucking with it, you don't have to
	- Allows for setting a minimum maximum integrity to allow for specific buffs to be used
	- I haven't tested this *-extensively-*, but for ya'll who want to nit pick which buffs you wanna use, it's there now
- Added a calculator for gatherable as well, that way you can tell what you're roughly going to gather based on what you have enabled for that profile
- Gathering also has a replay built into it, it'll track
	- What you gathered at a node
	- What buffs it used
	- How many items you got
	- This is mainly so I can actually tell what's being used on gathering nodes, and why certain things aren't. 
- Maps have been told they are *-in fact-* hidden items (they weren't in the sheets, so now... well now they are)

metadataCompletePlugins.author: dajoey
metadataCompletePlugins.name: Lazy Fish Sitter
metadataCompletePlugins.punchline: Sits you down while you fish. That's it.
metadataCompletePlugins.description: Checks every few seconds while you are fishing; if you are not sitting, it runs /sit for you. Leaves you alone once you are seated (ground sit, chair, or pose).
metadataCompletePlugins.changelog:
v0.1.5.3 (2026-11-14) [testing]
- The plugin windows have been rebuilt on the shared LalaUiKit: one consistent layout with themed section headers, unified spacing and colour accents. All settings and behaviour are unchanged, and existing configuration loads as-is.

v0.1.5.2 (2026-11-10) [testing]
- Rebuilt against the Dalamud 15.0.4.0 payload for game patch 7.58. No functional changes.

v0.1.5.1 (2026-10-03) [testing]
- **Quick controls for the Lazy Hub window.** The plugin now offers the "Sit while fishing" switch to Lazy Hub (`/lazy`) over Dalamud IPC, so they can be changed from one window next to the other lalalazy plugins. Each change does exactly what the matching setting in the plugin's own window does.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Without Lazy Hub installed the plugin behaves exactly as before.

v0.1.5.0 (2026-09-25)

- Persistent seating across fishing hole visits: if the character stands up during a visit to a fishing hole (such as putting the rod away to change bait or use cordials, or manually standing up), the automation now detects the stand and re-seats upon resuming fishing or on the subsequent cast.
- Unaccepted send cap: the 3-send limit per hole visit is now scoped to consecutive unaccepted sends rather than a lifetime cap per hole visit. When a sit is accepted by the game, the counter resets, ensuring long fishing sessions with multiple bait changes or pauses remain seated while still guarding against unbounded retry loops if commands are blocked.

v0.1.4.0 (2026-09-25)

- Sits after a cast: the automated /sit check now runs after a cast once the line is settled in the water (`LineInWater`), in addition to the pre-cast standby beat (`PoleReady`). In active fishing loops or when using automated casting tools, the standby beat between casts typically lasts under a second, which previously prevented the automation from ever triggering across repeated casts (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `IsStandbyBeat`).
- Safe timing: commands are sent only after the line has been in the water for at least 1 second to ensure the cast animation has resolved, and continue to be refused during active casting, biting, hooking, reeling, and position change animations.

v0.1.3.0 (2026-09-05)

- Correction first, because the last release's notes got the game wrong: FFXIV does NOT force standing on every hooked fish. If the character is sitting when the cast starts, the game keeps it seated for the whole loop - a hook may cause a momentary stand, but the game sits back down on its own. v0.1.2.0 was designed around that mistake (one /sit per cast) and this release replaces it entirely.
- Sit once, then stay out of the way. The plugin now sends a single /sit per fishing trip, at a moment the game will actually accept it, and then does nothing for the rest of the trip (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `Decide`).
- That moment is the standby beat: rod out, no line in the water (`FishingEventHandler.State == PoleReady`), held for a second, at least 3 seconds clear of a bite/hook/reel, with the character read as standing for 3 seconds straight. It will never fire mid-cast, with a line in the water, mid-bite, mid-reel, or while already sitting down or standing up (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `IsStandbyBeat`).
- That is why v0.1.1.0 looked like it did nothing: it sent its one /sit the instant the fishing flag came on, which is after the line is already out, and the game swallows the emote there - ten sends across ten sessions, no effect. v0.1.2.0 still counted "line in water" as a valid moment and would have done the same thing.
- No re-sit after every cast, ever. A brief standing read just after a bite, hook, reel or collectable prompt is treated as the game's own animation, not as the character standing up, so the plugin does nothing and lets the game re-seat (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `IsHookish`).
- A "trip" is one visit to a fishing hole, not one cast. The fishing flag drops between casts (v0.1.1.0 saw ten "sessions" in 21 minutes), so the limits are now anchored to the hole and only reset after 20 seconds away from it (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `StartTrip` / `EndTrip`).
- Anti-yo-yo guards, all hard, because a /sit on a seated character STANDS them: never sends while any seated signal reads seated; at least 10 seconds between sends; at most 3 sends per trip with a log line when it stops; and once the game has taken a sit this trip it will not send again unless the seated read has proved it still reports seated with the rod out (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `Decide`, guards 1-5).
- The settings window now shows the trip counters: whether the character is at a hole, sits used out of 3, whether the game took the sit, and whether the seated read works while fishing (file: `ConfigWindow.cs`).
- Removed the "check interval" slider. The plugin now looks every frame, because every limit that matters is a real time limit (10 seconds between sends, 3 seconds of standing before it believes the read, 3 sends a trip) and a 2-second poll just made it step over short standby beats between quick casts. Saved values are ignored, not lost (files: `ConfigWindow.cs`, `Configuration.cs`).
- The policy is now a plain C# class with no game code in it (`Core/SitPolicy.cs`), replayed offline against 26 scripted fishing sessions by `tests/LazyFishSitter.Harness`. Three releases in a row shipped a rule that only broke in game; the harness caught three more before this one shipped, including a dead window that would have stopped a refused /sit from ever being retried.
- Keeps the detailed state logging (every fishing-state and posture change, 40 lines a minute max) and adds a one-line trip summary, so the still-open question - does the game ever report seated while a line is out - can be answered from the log without typing anything in game (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `EndTrip`).

rawManifest.Name: Lazy Fish Sitter
rawManifest.Punchline: Sits you down while you fish. That's it.
rawManifest.Description: Checks every few seconds while you are fishing; if you are not sitting, it runs /sit for you. Leaves you alone once you are seated (ground sit, chair, or pose).
rawManifest.Changelog:
v0.1.5.3 (2026-11-14) [testing]
- The plugin windows have been rebuilt on the shared LalaUiKit: one consistent layout with themed section headers, unified spacing and colour accents. All settings and behaviour are unchanged, and existing configuration loads as-is.

v0.1.5.2 (2026-11-10) [testing]
- Rebuilt against the Dalamud 15.0.4.0 payload for game patch 7.58. No functional changes.

v0.1.5.1 (2026-10-03) [testing]
- **Quick controls for the Lazy Hub window.** The plugin now offers the "Sit while fishing" switch to Lazy Hub (`/lazy`) over Dalamud IPC, so they can be changed from one window next to the other lalalazy plugins. Each change does exactly what the matching setting in the plugin's own window does.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Without Lazy Hub installed the plugin behaves exactly as before.

v0.1.5.0 (2026-09-25)

- Persistent seating across fishing hole visits: if the character stands up during a visit to a fishing hole (such as putting the rod away to change bait or use cordials, or manually standing up), the automation now detects the stand and re-seats upon resuming fishing or on the subsequent cast.
- Unaccepted send cap: the 3-send limit per hole visit is now scoped to consecutive unaccepted sends rather than a lifetime cap per hole visit. When a sit is accepted by the game, the counter resets, ensuring long fishing sessions with multiple bait changes or pauses remain seated while still guarding against unbounded retry loops if commands are blocked.

v0.1.4.0 (2026-09-25)

- Sits after a cast: the automated /sit check now runs after a cast once the line is settled in the water (`LineInWater`), in addition to the pre-cast standby beat (`PoleReady`). In active fishing loops or when using automated casting tools, the standby beat between casts typically lasts under a second, which previously prevented the automation from ever triggering across repeated casts (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `IsStandbyBeat`).
- Safe timing: commands are sent only after the line has been in the water for at least 1 second to ensure the cast animation has resolved, and continue to be refused during active casting, biting, hooking, reeling, and position change animations.

v0.1.3.0 (2026-09-05)

- Correction first, because the last release's notes got the game wrong: FFXIV does NOT force standing on every hooked fish. If the character is sitting when the cast starts, the game keeps it seated for the whole loop - a hook may cause a momentary stand, but the game sits back down on its own. v0.1.2.0 was designed around that mistake (one /sit per cast) and this release replaces it entirely.
- Sit once, then stay out of the way. The plugin now sends a single /sit per fishing trip, at a moment the game will actually accept it, and then does nothing for the rest of the trip (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `Decide`).
- That moment is the standby beat: rod out, no line in the water (`FishingEventHandler.State == PoleReady`), held for a second, at least 3 seconds clear of a bite/hook/reel, with the character read as standing for 3 seconds straight. It will never fire mid-cast, with a line in the water, mid-bite, mid-reel, or while already sitting down or standing up (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `IsStandbyBeat`).
- That is why v0.1.1.0 looked like it did nothing: it sent its one /sit the instant the fishing flag came on, which is after the line is already out, and the game swallows the emote there - ten sends across ten sessions, no effect. v0.1.2.0 still counted "line in water" as a valid moment and would have done the same thing.
- No re-sit after every cast, ever. A brief standing read just after a bite, hook, reel or collectable prompt is treated as the game's own animation, not as the character standing up, so the plugin does nothing and lets the game re-seat (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `IsHookish`).
- A "trip" is one visit to a fishing hole, not one cast. The fishing flag drops between casts (v0.1.1.0 saw ten "sessions" in 21 minutes), so the limits are now anchored to the hole and only reset after 20 seconds away from it (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `StartTrip` / `EndTrip`).
- Anti-yo-yo guards, all hard, because a /sit on a seated character STANDS them: never sends while any seated signal reads seated; at least 10 seconds between sends; at most 3 sends per trip with a log line when it stops; and once the game has taken a sit this trip it will not send again unless the seated read has proved it still reports seated with the rod out (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `Decide`, guards 1-5).
- The settings window now shows the trip counters: whether the character is at a hole, sits used out of 3, whether the game took the sit, and whether the seated read works while fishing (file: `ConfigWindow.cs`).
- Removed the "check interval" slider. The plugin now looks every frame, because every limit that matters is a real time limit (10 seconds between sends, 3 seconds of standing before it believes the read, 3 sends a trip) and a 2-second poll just made it step over short standby beats between quick casts. Saved values are ignored, not lost (files: `ConfigWindow.cs`, `Configuration.cs`).
- The policy is now a plain C# class with no game code in it (`Core/SitPolicy.cs`), replayed offline against 26 scripted fishing sessions by `tests/LazyFishSitter.Harness`. Three releases in a row shipped a rule that only broke in game; the harness caught three more before this one shipped, including a dead window that would have stopped a refused /sit from ever being retried.
- Keeps the detailed state logging (every fishing-state and posture change, 40 lines a minute max) and adds a one-line trip summary, so the still-open question - does the game ever report seated while a line is out - can be answered from the log without typing anything in game (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `EndTrip`).

metadataCompletePlugins.author: dajoey
metadataCompletePlugins.name: Lazy Market Companion
metadataCompletePlugins.punchline: Auto-lists your always-sell items and matches market board prices
metadataCompletePlugins.description: Keep an Auto-Market list of items you always sell. The companion lists them through your retainers in the stack size you choose (keeping a reserve in your bags if you want), prices every listing by matching the lowest board price instead of undercutting, and can do all of it inside AutoRetainer's venture cycle. Also re-prices existing listings (Auto Pinch). Successor to Dagobert Price Matcher; your old settings are imported automatically.
metadataCompletePlugins.changelog:
v0.2.8.21 (2026-11-14) [testing]
- The plugin windows have been rebuilt on the shared LalaUiKit: one consistent layout with themed section headers, unified spacing and colour accents. All settings and behaviour are unchanged, and existing configuration loads as-is.

v0.2.8.20 (2026-11-10) [testing]
- Rebuilt against the Dalamud 15.0.4.0 payload for game patch 7.58. No functional changes.

v0.2.8.19 (2026-11-10) [testing]
- **Mannequin listings are now detected on clients in any language.** The mannequin check matched a hardcoded English/German/French list of the context menu's "adjust price" label, so on a client in any other language a mannequin listing was never detected and the automation clicked "adjust price" on a mannequin item. The check now compares the menu against the client's own localized Adjust Price label (the fix is ported from upstream Dagobert's Auto Pinch, whose absorbed price formula this plugin already carries).
- **The manual post hotkey now starts from fresh prices.** Opening a retainer's sell dialog while the post hotkey was held kept whatever the previous session had left behind - cached board prices, an in-flight price lookup, per-session gates - so the price written into the dialog could be stale. The session state is now cleared when the sell dialog opens, before the post chain runs (the fix is ported from upstream Dagobert's Auto Pinch).
- **The manual post chain no longer fires from unrelated windows.** The listener behind the post hotkey was registered for every addon opening, so any window that opened while the hotkey was held could queue a manual post chain for a window that was not the retainer sell dialog. It is now scoped to the retainer sell dialog itself (the fix is ported from upstream Dagobert's Auto Pinch).
- Untried build: tested offline against the plugin's offline test suite, not yet in the game.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.2.8.18 (2026-11-09) [testing]
- **Holding the pinch hotkey no longer re-fires the pinch.** The hotkey was read as a level: on every frame the key stayed down the retainer list and sell list draws each re-ran their pinch check, so holding the key queued a new Auto Pinch every drawn frame - and fired again the moment a finished run freed the busy guard. The key is now read as an edge: one press is one fire, and a held key stays quiet until it is released and pressed again (the fix is ported from upstream Dagobert's Auto Pinch, whose absorbed price formula this plugin already carries). Cancelling a run is unchanged: the Cancel button and the /lmc command; the upstream press-again-to-cancel shortcut was deliberately not adopted.
- Untried build: tested offline against the plugin's offline test suite, not yet in the game.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.2.8.17 (2026-11-06) [testing]
- **The overlay buttons no longer have to cover the retainer windows' own controls.** The Auto Pinch, Auto Market and Sweep to Bags buttons are pinned to the top-right corner of the retainer list and retainer sell list windows, where they can cover the venture currency and the windows' close button (reported in issue #12). Each of the three buttons can now be hidden individually under Settings -> Retainers & Hotkeys -> "Retainer window buttons". A hidden button's action stays reachable through the /lmc subcommands, and the Cancel button shown while a run is in progress is never hidden. All three default to shown, so existing settings keep working exactly as before.
- Untried build: tested offline against the plugin's offline test suite, not yet in the game.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.2.8.16 (2026-10-17) [testing]
- **Fresh installs no longer show an import notice for a plugin that was never installed.** A leftover line in the configuration loader set the "imported from Dagobert Price Matcher" flag true on every load that created a new configuration, so a brand-new install showed the import notice and the uninstall hint even though no settings were ever imported. The flag now keeps its false default; a genuine import from a found Dagobert configuration still sets it, and the load log's imported= field reports the real value.
- Untried build: tested offline against the plugin's offline test suite, not yet in the game.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

metadataCompletePlugins.author: dajoey
metadataCompletePlugins.name: LazyCrafter
metadataCompletePlugins.punchline: What can I make right now, what's it worth, and what would it take to make the rest?
metadataCompletePlugins.description: Catalogs every recipe you can craft, buckets them by how much effort the missing materials take, prices them with Universalis, and hands the missing-material work to Artisan / GBR / ARC / Lifestream.
metadataCompletePlugins.changelog:
v0.1.7.11 (2026-11-14) [testing]
- The plugin windows have been rebuilt on the shared LalaUiKit: one consistent layout with themed section headers, unified spacing and colour accents. All settings and behaviour are unchanged, and existing configuration loads as-is.

v0.1.7.10 (2026-11-10) [testing]
- Rebuilt against the Dalamud 15.0.4.0 payload for game patch 7.58. No functional changes.

v0.1.7.9 (2026-10-17) [testing]
- **Market-price lookups no longer log warnings while they retry.** When Universalis is slow or busy it answers with a temporary "try again" status or takes longer than before; the price client already retries those on its own with a pause between tries - that is its designed behavior, not a fault, so those lines now go to the debug log. Only one warning is written when a batch gives up entirely after all retries, and stale cached prices are used meanwhile, exactly as before.
- **The price client now waits up to 60 seconds per request instead of 20.** Under load, Universalis sometimes finishes a large price query just after the old 20-second cutoff; the request was cancelled while the server was still working on it and the prices for that batch were refetched from scratch. The longer budget lets those queries land.
- Market-price log lines no longer paste a hundred item numbers into the log; a batch is described as its item count instead.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Full harness: 401/401 PASS (6 new).

v0.1.7.8 (2026-10-07) [testing]
- **Knightshopper no longer buys units that are sitting on a retainer.** The purchase target counted everything the catalog can see, but the fetch-from-retainer step runs after the purchase and brings those units in anyway - with 90 units on a retainer, none in the bags and 9 missing, the run bought 99 instead of 9. The target now counts what is physically in the bags, and the fetch tops the bags up to exactly what the cart needs; every currency routes on the same corrected target.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Full harness: 395/395 PASS (4 new).

v0.1.7.7 (2026-10-07) [testing]
- **Cart dispatches can hand vendor purchases to Knightshopper.** When a dispatch is missing materials that a vendor sells - gil vendors, and currency vendors priced in one currency Knightshopper supports - the run groups that list by currency and buys it through Knightshopper's purchase IPC at target inventory totals, before any shopping stop fires. The run prints each group, its currency and the estimated total cost before anything is spent. Market-board items are never routed, and one attempt per group means a refused purchase never retries; a repeat dispatch asks for the same target totals at most, so nothing is ever bought twice.
- If Knightshopper is missing, busy, refuses LazyCrafter, or has no unlocked vendor for an item, those items fall back to the usual shopping stops - flagged and named in chat exactly as before. Purchases also need LazyCrafter on Knightshopper's allowed-plugins IPC list, which is set in Knightshopper's own settings (IPC permissions); LazyCrafter never changes Knightshopper's settings. The new switch (on by default) is "Buy vendor items through Knightshopper during a dispatch" in the settings.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- With the switch off, or without Knightshopper installed, the run behaves exactly as before.
- Full harness: 391/391 PASS (16 new).

v0.1.7.6 (2026-10-03) [testing]
- **Quick controls for the Lazy Hub window.** The plugin now offers the catalog and price settings (recipes above the character's level, the undersupplied thresholds, the revenue basis, pricing at the home world only, the price refresh interval, the price-match message) and the cart-run hand-off switches (fetching materials from retainers, walking to a summoning bell or to vendors, preferring a currency shop) to Lazy Hub (`/lazy`) over Dalamud IPC, so they can be changed from one window next to the other lalalazy plugins. Each change does exactly what the matching setting in the plugin's own window does.
- The cart-run hand-off switches can only be changed while no cart run is active.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Without Lazy Hub installed the plugin behaves exactly as before.

metadataCompletePlugins.author: Akari
metadataCompletePlugins.name: Market Helper
metadataCompletePlugins.punchline: Undercut, list, gather and buy — market board automation end to end.
metadataCompletePlugins.description:
Market Helper is an all-in-one market board tool with five tabs:

UNDERCUT — Walk a summoning bell's retainers and undercut every listed item. HQ and NQ are handled separately, your own retainers are matched rather than undercut, per-item overrides and price memory are supported, an obvious troll price is skipped, and mannequin/display items are never touched (if a row can't be verified it is skipped rather than risk delisting it). Closes the bell when it finishes.

LISTER — Build a list (hold CTRL and hover an item, or search) and press Go to list them all. Prices each item at the most common market price, ignoring lone troll listings, against your world, data center or whole region. Per-item stack sizes and list amounts, rolls extra items to the next retainer at the 20-slot cap, and includes a no-touch dry run.

FLIPPER — Compare any marketable item across Japan, America, Europe and Materia via Universalis. Top 10 listings per region, best cross-region flip, and seller/buyer tax modelling.

ITEM GATHERER — Pull designated items off your retainers into your bags, optionally returning your market listings first. Manual withdraw/deposit actions included.

BUYER — Build a shopping list by hand or import a MakePlace furniture list, then SCAN the market per world via Universalis and press SEND to travel with Lifestream and buy across worlds. Every purchase is verified against the game's own confirmation dialog before it is accepted. Listings are bought whole, so by default it never buys a bigger stack than you still need, and a hard sanity ceiling caps the price even with no cap set. If a planned listing has already been bought it chases the next cheapest, on other worlds if needed, until your order is filled. Dry run is on by default.

Open with /markethelp, /market, /mh, or /undercut.

metadataCompletePlugins.author: Aschy
metadataCompletePlugins.name: Market Master Pro
metadataCompletePlugins.punchline: Manual market intelligence and arbitrage scanner for FFXIV.
metadataCompletePlugins.description: Analyzes market opportunities with Universalis data, watchlists, velocity filters, and manual undercut helpers. All actions are manual. Now includes real-time undercut notifications.
metadataCompletePlugins.changelog:
v1.1.36: Installer reliability hotfix - release asset now uses a versioned filename to avoid stale CDN cache and ensure distributed package version matches feed version.
v1.1.35: Reissued release package on a fresh tag to bypass stale CDN artifact and restore install/update reliability for latest opportunities persistence update.
v1.1.34: Scanner now persists the most recent opportunities and keeps them visible until a new scan completes; latest opportunity snapshot is restored on startup.
v1.1.33: Stability pass: opportunities table now supports row caps, compact mode, and optional detailed tooltips; exclusion inspector now uses TTL caching with refresh debounce; added pluginmaster feed validation script for safer releases.

metadataCompletePlugins.punchline: 生产求解器 Raphael 的 Dalamud 包装

metadataCompletePlugins.author: yagi2
metadataCompletePlugins.name: Restocker
metadataCompletePlugins.punchline: Bulk reprice and split-list retainer market listings across all retainers.
metadataCompletePlugins.description: Cross-retainer market workbench with a plan-then-apply flow. Reprice tab: per-retainer 'lowest -N g' / 'lowest exact' buttons walk each listing, fetch live market data via Dalamud's IMarketBoard.OfferingsReceived (skipping your own retainers, deduplicated per item/HQ), stage every change in a queue, then commit them all via a single Apply that calls SetRetainerMarketPrice directly. New listing tab: per-row qty x slots, target retainer combo, auto stack-splitting (e.g. 990 / 99 → ten listings of 99), and direct listing from character bag / Chocobo Saddlebag with no entrust step (saddle items are bulk-staged to the bag in one phase, then listed). Live progress dialog shows the current step (selecting retainer, fetching market data, listing, …) so long runs don't look frozen. Six-language UI (EN/JA/DE/FR/ZH/KO). Warns once at startup if AutoRetainer is also loaded since both drive retainer summoning.
metadataCompletePlugins.changelog: 0.1.0.0 — Initial release.

metadataCompletePlugins.author: Aschy
metadataCompletePlugins.name: Armoury Cleaner
metadataCompletePlugins.punchline: Filter and move unwanted gear out of your armoury chest.
metadataCompletePlugins.description: Define filters by job, minimum/maximum equip level, and item level. Armoury Cleaner scans each gear slot and moves only items that match all active filters into your inventory so you can discard them.
metadataCompletePlugins.changelog:
v1.0.9: New 'Skip Gearset Items' filter (default ON) ? items currently assigned to any saved gearset are excluded from the scan, so Discard All can never delete gear you actively use.
v1.0.8: Added /acplugin command for consistent access alongside /ac legacy alias.
v1.0.7: UI redesign ? removed Auto-Discard toggle; separate Move To Inventory and Discard All buttons; both now use random 800-1100ms delays for consistent pacing; direct discard from armoury is now the default for Discard All.
v1.0.6: Direct discard from armoury ? new option (under Auto-Discard) skips the move-to-inventory step and discards items straight from the armoury slot, with automatic fallback to move+discard if the game rejects it.
v1.0.5: Internal cleanup; repo renamed to AschyQOL.
v1.0.4: Discard All uses random 800-1100ms delay between items; Cancel Queue button.
v1.0.3: Auto-Discard mode via InventoryManager.DiscardItem.
v1.0.0: Initial release.

rawManifest.Punchline: Save and apply Party Finder recruitment presets instantly.
rawManifest.Description:
Store a full Party Finder recruitment setup (duty, job slots, description, objective, loot rule, one player per job, language, and more) as a named preset and apply it in one go, instead of filling the form out by hand every time.

Fill a preset and review it, or fill and post the party in a single click. Optional auto-refresh keeps an active listing alive near the end of its hour, with the windows closed, and leaves your away status alone.

Open the Recruitment Criteria form (Recruit Members) to save or apply. Use /clarion.

metadataCompletePlugins.changelog:
6ae42a0: Merge pull request #814 from SlashNephy/fix/faloop-login-failure

fix(FaloopIntegration): report rejected logins instead of retrying
7900863: fix(FaloopIntegration): report rejected logins instead of retrying

Faloop responds to a login with wrong credentials with 400 and
{"success":false,"msg":"Incorrect username or password."}. The client
threw on it, so nothing was shown in chat, and the connection loop
treated it as a transient error and kept retrying.

- Read the 400 response as a rejected login instead of throwing
- Print the reason to chat and stop retrying

Close #742

bdadbad: Merge pull request #813 from SlashNephy/feat/faloop-release-report

feat(FaloopIntegration): notify when a scheduled spawn is released
33272b7: feat(FaloopIntegration): notify when a scheduled spawn is released

Scheduled spawns are visible only to early access reporters at first,
and released to everyone later. The spawn_release handler was removed in
ac3fe87, so the release was no longer notified.

- Mark the spawn report of a scheduled spawn with "(scheduled)"
- Add a per-rank "Enable Mob Release Report" option (disabled by
  default) to notify "has been released!" on spawn_release
- Keep the stored spawn up to date on spawn_release even when the
  option is disabled
- Accept ISO 8601 strings as well as epoch milliseconds for the release
  timestamp, as Faloop's web client does

Close #685

Co-Authored-By: Claude Mythos 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
2fee79f: Merge pull request #812 from SlashNephy/fix/alic-queued-teleport-notification

fix(AetheryteLinkInChat): notify queued teleports only when they start
bc00f9c: fix(AetheryteLinkInChat): notify queued teleports only when they start

TeleportToQueuedAetheryte printed "Teleporting to ... (queued)" without
checking the result of ExecuteTeleport, so a queued teleport that
failed to start still showed the notification.

Refs #659

Co-Authored-By: Claude Mythos 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
ed4a33d: Merge pull request #811 from SlashNephy/feat/faloop-spawn-sound

feat(FaloopIntegration): play a sound effect on spawn reports
223d58b: feat(FaloopIntegration): play a sound effect on spawn reports

Add a per-rank "Sound on Spawn Report" option:

- None (default)
- <se.1> to <se.16>, the same sounds as chat sound effects
- A custom UI sound effect ID, for sounds such as "Feature Unlocked"

The sound is played whenever a spawn report is printed to chat, and can
be previewed from the settings.

Close #464

Co-Authored-By: Claude Mythos 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
6f7ea10: Merge pull request #810 from SlashNephy/feat/alic-print-conditions

feat(AetheryteLinkInChat): add options to skip own messages and local Lifestream links
5b47730: feat(AetheryteLinkInChat): add options to skip own messages and local Lifestream links

- "Hide the Lifestream link for messages about the current world":
  skip the Lifestream link when the world detected from the message is
  the current world
- "Do not add teleport links to your own messages": skip messages sent
  by the local player

Both are disabled by default, so the current behaviour is unchanged.

Close #677

Co-Authored-By: Claude Mythos 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
05acc63: Merge pull request #809 from SlashNephy/fix/faloop-reconnect

fix(FaloopIntegration): reconnect with a new client after disconnection
47500d7: fix(FaloopIntegration): log the whole spawn_location payload

Passing the nullable ZonePoiId alone as the params argument of the log
call made it a null array when the value was null (CS8604). Log the
whole payload instead, as the spawn case does.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Mythos 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
3cf9a9e: fix(FaloopIntegration): reconnect with a new client after disconnection

After "transport close", SocketIOClient's own reconnection kept the
engine.io session alive (pings continued) but the plugin never received
mob reports again until it was disabled and enabled.

Handle reconnection in the plugin instead, mirroring what re-enabling
the plugin does:

- Disable SocketIOClient's reconnection
- Run a connection loop that logs in again and connects with a new
  Socket.IO client on every disconnection, with exponential backoff
  from 5 seconds up to 5 minutes
- Time out a connection attempt that the server never accepts, since
  ConnectAsync only times out at the transport level
- Stop retrying when the credentials are rejected
- Ignore events from clients that have already been replaced

Refs #687

Co-Authored-By: Claude Mythos 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
3e3cbf9: Merge pull request #808 from SlashNephy/docs/api13-repository

docs: describe the Dalamud API 13 repository
d2aee34: docs: describe the Dalamud API 13 repository

Point clients that are still on Dalamud API 13, such as the Traditional
Chinese client, to plugins/api13.json, which serves the frozen
AetheryteLinkInChat 7.3.1.14 build.

Refs #727

Co-Authored-By: Claude Mythos 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
0f2ec49: Merge pull request #807 from SlashNephy/fix/faloop-pending-spawn-location

fix(FaloopIntegration): announce spawns whose location is reported later
6daa4d0: fix(FaloopIntegration): announce spawns whose location is reported later

When "Ignore Pending Report" is enabled, a spawn reported without
coordinates was dropped before being stored, so the following
spawn_location could not find it and was ignored as well.

- Hold location-less spawns as pending and announce them once
  spawn_location arrives
- Accept a null zonePoiId in spawn_location and a singular zonePoiId in spawn
- Replace the stored report on location change instead of appending

Co-Authored-By: Claude Mythos 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
8b422a6: Merge pull request #805 from SlashNephy/fix/faloop-messaging-socket

fix(FaloopIntegration): connect to Faloop's new Socket.IO endpoint
01daabc: fix(FaloopIntegration): connect to Faloop's new Socket.IO endpoint

Faloop's frontend update (2026-10-30) moved the Socket.IO endpoint from
/comms/socket.io to the /legacy namespace on /messaging/socket.io/.
The old endpoint still accepts connections but no longer delivers mob
reports, so follow the new endpoint.

Close #804

Co-Authored-By: Claude Mythos 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
d2ea413: feat: use a divination-deploy App token instead of DEPLOY_GITHUB_TOKEN (#799)

reusable-deploy-plugin.yml checks out the distribution repository, opens
a pull request there and merges it. Mint a GitHub App installation token
scoped to that repository instead of using a bot PAT.

Drop the Authorization header when fetching commits.json. This
repository is public so the request needs no authentication, and
expanding a token on the command line exposes it through the process
list.

Reference the reusable workflow by local path. Pinning it by SHA means a
change here does not take effect until every caller is updated, which
would leave a broken intermediate state whenever a secret is renamed.

Drop the explicit create-pull-request author: it defaults to
github.actor, which attributes the deployment to whoever triggered it.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

metadataCompletePlugins.changelog:
The aetheryte network now works whatever language you play in. Playing in anything but English, no shard was ever found and EchoNav quietly walked everywhere instead.
Travelling to a shard you have never stood at yourself now works. It used to need you to have visited a shard before it could take you there.

metadataCompletePlugins.author: XivHub
metadataCompletePlugins.name: InventoryCleaner
metadataCompletePlugins.punchline: Keep only the gear you actually use.
metadataCompletePlugins.description:
Tidies the Armoury Chest against your saved gearsets. Anything equipped, referenced by a gearset, or a higher-ilvl upgrade for a job you still play is kept; everything else is moved out to your bags, fullest armoury container first, so the run frees space where it is tightest. Every run is previewed item by item with the reason for each decision, and nothing moves until you confirm.

Also does the reverse (pulling gearset pieces back into the armoury) and offers a discard picker: an icon grid of leftover gear, framed by rarity, where anything equipped, in a gearset, or on your allowlist is never listed.

metadataCompletePlugins.changelog:
v0.1.1.5 (2026-11-14) [testing]
- The bundled interface toolkit no longer carries an unused image-processing library, so the plugin installs fewer files and no longer ships a package with known security advisories. No behavior changes.

v0.1.1.4 (2026-11-14) [testing]
- The plugin windows have been rebuilt on the shared LalaUiKit: one consistent layout with themed section headers, unified spacing and colour accents. All settings and behaviour are unchanged, and existing configuration loads as-is.

v0.1.1.3 (2026-11-10) [testing]
- Rebuilt against the Dalamud 15.0.4.0 payload for game patch 7.58. No functional changes.

v0.1.1.2 (2026-11-07) [testing]

- No plugin-code changes: the plugin now builds against a fixed Dalamud library set (the pinned staging 15.0.3.9 payload) instead of whichever libraries the build machine happens to have installed, so packaging this plugin works reliably again. The hub window is unchanged.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.1.1.1 (2026-11-05) [testing]

v0.1.1.2 (2026-11-07) [testing]

- No plugin-code changes: the plugin now builds against a fixed Dalamud library set (the pinned staging 15.0.3.9 payload) instead of whichever libraries the build machine happens to have installed, so packaging this plugin works reliably again. The hub window is unchanged.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

- Updated the bundled KamiToolKit UI library to the current upstream version; the hub window is built on the framework's current internals now, and the window-frame tint targets the framework's texture-backed chrome nodes.
- The native window is created on the game's main thread after the UI framework finishes initializing, instead of during plugin load.
- Kept the fork's hot-reload safety guard: teardown disables the hooks, lets any call already inside them finish, and only then disposes.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

metadataCompletePlugins.author: yocopk
metadataCompletePlugins.name: MogHouse Companion
metadataCompletePlugins.punchline: Quality-of-life tools that connect your game to MogHouse. Timers and duty pops, pushed to your phone.
metadataCompletePlugins.description:
Companion plugin for MogHouse (mog-house.com).

An all-in-one home for quality-of-life tools that link FINAL FANTASY XIV to your MogHouse account. Tools are added over time; each one can be switched on or off individually, and nothing leaves the game unless you enable it.

Timers: reads the timers you already see in the game's own Timers window (CTRL+U), including submarine and airship voyages, retainer ventures, map and leve allowances, custom deliveries and allied society dailies, and syncs them to your profile. MogHouse then pushes you a notification the moment one comes up, on web and mobile, even while the game and your PC are off. Voyages are timed to the last vessel back, so one notification means the whole fleet is home.

Duty Finder: when the confirm window appears, MogHouse pushes the duty or roulette name to your phone, so you know whether it is worth the sprint back to the desk. By default it stays quiet while the game is the window you are looking at.

The plugin is read-only: it collects your own data and reports status. It never performs an in-game action — it will not commence a duty for you, and it does not skip, confirm or automate anything.

Open it with /moghouse. Requires a MogHouse account, and a free one is enough: it syncs one character and sends one timer alert of your choosing, plus duty pops. Mog+ lifts both limits and warns you before a timer lands rather than as it does.

metadataCompletePlugins.author: nxships
metadataCompletePlugins.name: PlayerNexusTracker
metadataCompletePlugins.punchline: Track every adventurer you meet in Eorzea.
metadataCompletePlugins.description:
Track players you meet in FFXIV — who they are, when you ran into them, how their characters change over time. A focused social tracker built on the NexusKit framework.

Per-player detail view with Summary, Equipment, Class/Jobs, Achievements, Free Company, Encounters, History and Notes tabs. Optional enrichment from Lodestone (gear, FC link, achievement progress) and FFXIVCollect (mounts, minions, full achievement catalog). Live throttled refresh queue keeps external data fresh without hammering either service.

Configurable chat and toast notifications when players you've seen before change — rename, server transfer, Free Company join/leave/switch, achievement growth, refresh failures. Per-event filtering and history grouping so the chat doesn't drown you.

Powerful player-filter language with live preview to slice your list however you want; encounter history scoped per duty and content type; optional bridges to other Dalamud plugins (Lifestream world-travel, more to come).

Local-first: all data lives in a single SQLite file under your XIVLauncher config. Automated weekly maintenance keeps it tidy. English and German localization.

rawManifest.Author: nxships
rawManifest.Name: PlayerNexusTracker
rawManifest.Description:
Track players you meet in FFXIV — who they are, when you ran into them, how their characters change over time. A focused social tracker built on the NexusKit framework.

Per-player detail view with Summary, Equipment, Class/Jobs, Achievements, Free Company, Encounters, History and Notes tabs. Optional enrichment from Lodestone (gear, FC link, achievement progress) and FFXIVCollect (mounts, minions, full achievement catalog). Live throttled refresh queue keeps external data fresh without hammering either service.

Configurable chat and toast notifications when players you've seen before change — rename, server transfer, Free Company join/leave/switch, achievement growth, refresh failures. Per-event filtering and history grouping so the chat doesn't drown you.

Powerful player-filter language with live preview to slice your list however you want; encounter history scoped per duty and content type; optional bridges to other Dalamud plugins (Lifestream world-travel, more to come).

Local-first: all data lives in a single SQLite file under your XIVLauncher config. Automated weekly maintenance keeps it tidy. English and German localization.
rawManifest.Punchline: Track every adventurer you meet in Eorzea.
rawManifest.FeedbackMessage:
Please send feedback over to GitHub instead of using this dialog — the form there lets you pick the right category (Bug report, Feature request, or General question via Discussions) and asks for the context we need to act on the report (plugin version, repro steps, etc).

Open the chooser at:
https://github.com/NexusFFXIV/PlayerNexusTracker/issues/new/choose

Note: text you type in this Dalamud dialog goes to the Dalamud team aggregator and does not reach the plugin author directly.

metadataCompletePlugins.author: VimaFFXIV
metadataCompletePlugins.name: SharkChat
metadataCompletePlugins.punchline: Auto-replace words in your outgoing chat messages.
metadataCompletePlugins.description:
SharkChat intercepts your chat before it's sent and swaps words or phrases for whatever you want.

Set up rules like Thanks → Thankies, and they'll apply automatically every time you chat — across any channel.

Features:
• Whole-word matching (so "tank" won't mangle "thanks")
• Case-insensitive by default
• Per-rule enable/disable
• Live preview so you can test rules before using them

Commands:
/shark — toggle on/off
/shark config — open settings

metadataCompletePlugins.author: The Redheaded Witch, WillWolf76
metadataCompletePlugins.name: Fashion Report Calculator / Dye Finder
metadataCompletePlugins.punchline: Know your Fashion Report points on the spot and help crowdsource new items and dyes!
metadataCompletePlugins.description:
This is the new and improved Fashion Report System. This plugin will allow you to open a window that will show you what your fashion report status is vs the current week's theme.

There are a few parts to this. Since the only way to get Fashion Report for the week to my knowledge is speaking to Masked Rose after Tuesdays reset, this plugin takes the first person who does talk to him and updates everyone else. So only one person per week needs to speak to Masked Rose.

You can click on a theme and pull all the known items for that theme for that specific slot. You also get a very detailed breakdown of how much points you are getting based on what you are currently wearing.

The plugin also stores the attempts of those using the mod (just the data from fashioncheck, no user information) so that we can figure out the dyes faster and share information faster. The information in this table is wiped every week since once we discover the dyes, it is useless.

I still have more upgrades to do, including adding a dye window and the window that will help calculate the weekly dyes. I already have an idea of how I want to write them, so it shouldn't take me too long. If you have suggestions on how I can upgrade this, please share with me on github!

Credit for the program goes to it's original creator, WillWolf76, who wrote this for me originally.

When this plugin updates the database, it also updates my Discord Bot which you can set up to post fashion report each week. It's set to update on Tuesdays and Fridays (week start and dye information added). Link to add the Discord Bot is in the about section.

metadataCompletePlugins.name: Lazy Gear Collector
metadataCompletePlugins.punchline: Track upgradable gear sets and what it costs to finish them
metadataCompletePlugins.description: Tracks upgradable gear collections piece by piece. Starts with Occult Crescent: North Horn's Phantom Vision sets - all 7 roles, 5 slots, 4 tiers. Shows which pieces you own and at what tier, what the next upgrade costs, and the exact obol/fixative shortfall to finish a role or the whole collection. metadataCompletePlugins.description: A visual wardrobe for Penumbra mods. Each entry targets a single equipment slot, so you can wear or unwear exactly what you want without disturbing the rest of your look. Handles items spanning several mods, mod option groups, variants, and hair and other customisation mods. Save looks as outfits with per-item dyes, dye a whole outfit at once, and edit an outfit by wearing it and swapping pieces on the character. Import a whole batch of mods at once, or one at a time. Animations, VFX and mounts can be managed alongside your gear if you want them. Also does image previews, tags, favourites, search and sort, and automated screenshot sessions.

metadataCompletePlugins.punchline: Browse FFXIV venues and teleport to them with one click.
metadataCompletePlugins.description:
Discover active FFXIV venues with data powered by the FFXIV Venues API. Browse currently open and upcoming venues in a sortable table featuring color-coded data centers, opening times, and a visual timeline. Use /avf to open.
metadataCompletePlugins.changelog: Fixed missing opening hours for venues with unrecognized time zones.

Adds an IPC surface (ARC.AddItem, ARC.GetInProgress, ARC.GetListCount) for other plugins to hand off venture work - LazyCrafter's ArcDispatch uses it when present, falling back to reflection otherwise. Not for general use; installed alongside production ARControl to verify the PR in-game before replying to the maintainer.

metadataCompletePlugins.description: Lists every armoire-eligible dungeon drop in the game and shows whether each is in your inventory, in your armoire, or still missing. Sort by level, hide completed dungeons, toggle to show owned items too. Open the armoire UI at an inn once per session to populate the in-armoire state; in-inventory and equipped state is detected automatically.
metadataCompletePlugins.changelog:
v0.5.7.2 (2026-11-14) [testing]
- The plugin windows have been rebuilt on the shared LalaUiKit: one consistent layout with themed section headers, unified spacing and colour accents. All settings and behaviour are unchanged, and existing configuration loads as-is.

v0.5.7.1 (2026-11-10) [testing]
- Rebuilt against the Dalamud 15.0.4.0 payload for game patch 7.58. No functional changes.

v0.5.7.0 (2026-10-10)
- **The PvP shopping list now includes gear sold for Trophy Crystals and Wolf Collars.** The crystal quartermaster's Trophy Crystal Exchange (weapons, armour, accessories) and the collar quartermaster's exchange were missing from the list because their cost currencies were not mapped, so the PvP code came out empty. Both quartermasters are in the list now, checked against Knightshopper's own vendor catalog: every exported pair is one it accepts.
- Pieces no import code can name are now listed in the window by name with the reason (the shop has no vendor link in the game data, or Knightshopper has no vendor for its shop), instead of being dropped quietly. The Wolf Mark gear behind the mark quartermaster falls in this list: its shop opens through a dialogue handler, so no vendor pair can be written for it.
- The shopping summary line showed placeholder braces instead of the counts; it shows the numbers now.

v0.5.6.0 (2026-10-08)
- **Import codes now carry only what can actually be bought today.** Some pieces are gated behind more than a quest: seasonal vendors also gate pieces on an achievement, and the previous filter only knew about quests, so pieces the game would not sell yet were still written into the codes, and the first one of them made Knightshopper refuse the whole import ("Item N is not available from its shared Gil vendor"). The shopping list now checks live quest and achievement progress: what can be bought now goes into the code, a piece whose cheapest listing is locked falls back to a listing that can be bought, and a piece with no buyable listing at all is left out and counted at the bottom of the window ("N missing piece(s) need quest or achievement progress you don't have yet - left out of the import"). The rule applies to every currency, not just gil.

v0.5.5.0 (2026-10-08) [testing]
- **Import codes now name vendors that Knightshopper itself has.** The previous build still produced Gil codes that Knightshopper refused whole ("Item N is not available from its shared Gil vendor"): the rule it used to decide which vendors Knightshopper knows was a guess and was wrong for most Gil shops. The rule now follows how Knightshopper builds its own vendor list: a vendor is an NPC the game actually places in an area, and seasonal NPCs that are re-used under new ids with the same name and the same shops count once. It applies to every currency, not just gil. The Gil code now carries several times as many pieces, because shops the old rule dropped by mistake are back.
- Placeholder items with no name are no longer put in a code; Knightshopper has no entry for them.
- Every code and every catalog entry was checked offline against the vendor data produced by Knightshopper's own library (not against this plugin's own model): no refusals. This is not yet confirmed in the game, and newer game patches than the one checked are not covered.
- The shopping-list section says what the codes were checked against and that it is not yet confirmed in-game; the copy message also explains that Knightshopper names only the first item it refuses.
- The vendor placement is read from the game's area files once per session in the background (about one second), with one log line.

v0.5.4.0 (2026-10-08) [testing]
- **Import codes no longer contain items Knightshopper would refuse.** Knightshopper rejects a whole import when even one item is not in its own catalog, which the previous Gil code hit: shops whose vendors only spawn for an event never enter Knightshopper's catalog, but this plugin was still naming them. The catalog now only names shops with a permanently placed vendor, matching how Knightshopper derives its own list, and the same rule applies to every currency, not just gil.
- Pieces that this leaves out are no longer silent: the window shows "N items left out: Knightshopper cannot buy them", the build log counts the skipped shops, and the copy buttons never produce a code Knightshopper would answer with "not available from its shared vendor".
